opportunities.name: Relying-Party-as-a-Service: the verifier side of the EU Digital Identity Wallet
opportunities.thesis: eIDAS 2.0 forces every member state to issue a certified EU Digital Identity Wallet, and forces banks, telecoms, energy, transport, healthcare and very large online platforms to accept it. Every one of those businesses must be entered in a national register of wallet-relying parties, obtain a relying-party access certificate from an authorised CA, declare the exact attributes it will request, and then actually validate mdoc/SD-JWT-VC presentations against the right national trust list — in each member state where it operates. The business is the single layer that does all of it: managed relying-party registration and certificate lifecycle across 27 registrars, plus one OpenID4VP verifier endpoint with attribute-policy linting, trust-list resolution and a signed, audit-defensible verification receipt. Speak US mobile driver's licence (ISO/IEC 18013-5, AAMVA) from the same integration so the customer buys age and identity verification once for both continents.
opportunities.why_overlooked: Money and attention went to wallets and issuers, because that is where the government funding is; the specialist vendors that exist (walt.id, Gataca, Procivis, iGrant, Signicat, eID Easy, Namirial) are small European identity shops selling issuance, with no self-serve motion and no US distribution. The registration plumbing was assumed to be a government problem, and the ARF's own discussion threads show the spec authors have not resolved basic questions — whether registration in one state confers EU-wide recognition, whether each airport kiosk is a separate relying party, how third-country entities register. The verification path is visibly being hand-rolled: GitHub's entire public surface here is the EU's own 742-star ARF repo, a 22-star Python mdoc/CBOR verifier, a 4-star consortium spec, a 39-star .NET OpenID4VP library, and a live issue (advatar/ActiveChain#442, opened 2026-08-01) of a team building an external mdoc/COSE verifier by hand.
opportunities.why_now: The 31 December 2026 wallet-issuance deadline is statutory, and obliged private-sector relying parties must accept wallets from late 2027 — so registration demand compresses into roughly a 12-month window. Readiness is deliberately uneven, which is the point: an assessment of the 27 member states put 3 as almost certain, 5 very likely, 8 likely, 7 'might' and 4 unlikely, so verifiers must handle a patchwork rather than a standard. Spec risk has already collapsed (ARF at 2.9.0, implementing acts on relying-party registration adopted, Commission reference registration service published) while operational capacity has not: as of February 2026 none of the 27 member states had deployed a live RP registration portal. Convergence pressure arrives simultaneously from US mDL adoption and from age-assurance mandates — the Texas App Store Accountability Act took effect 1 January 2026 after the Fifth Circuit stayed the injunction, with Apple and Google shipping Declared Age Range and Play Age Signals APIs.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two engineers who can read the ARF and ISO 18013-5, plus one regulatory-ops person. Ninety days: (1) a hosted verifier plus SDK that accepts an OpenID4VP presentation, validates mdoc/SD-JWT-VC signatures, resolves the correct national trust list and returns a signed verification receipt; (2) a free open-source presentation debugger — paste a presentation, see exactly why it failed — as the developer wedge, since teams are demonstrably building this by hand today; (3) managed registration completed in three member states among the most likely to be live (Germany, Italy, Spain, Poland, the Nordics), with automated issuance and rotation of relying-party access certificates and an attribute-request linter that checks each presentation request against what the customer actually declared. First customers: 5 design partners among EU-facing gambling, telco, marketplace and alcohol-delivery businesses that already have a legal need to check age or identity today. Price per verification with a registration setup fee.

opportunities.name: Killing lead-line 'unknowns' before the Nov 1, 2027 LCRI baseline locks in
opportunities.thesis: Under the Lead and Copper Rule Improvements, every public water system must hold a baseline service-line inventory by 1 November 2027 covering all lines and connectors regardless of ownership, publish a replacement plan, update it annually, and notify affected customers individually. Lines still classified 'unknown' are treated as lead, and the 2027 baseline locks in the mandatory replacement rate (roughly 10% of remaining inventory per year) and schedule for the following decade — so every unknown you reclassify correctly before the deadline is thousands of dollars of avoided capital, times an estimated 3.5-6.6 million unknown lines nationally. The business sells that arbitrage two ways: an outcome-priced 'unknowns reduction' engagement for mid-size utilities (predictive targeting model plus subcontracted vacuum-excavation potholing plus the regulatory documentation package), and a $200/month self-serve version of the paperwork for the tens of thousands of tiny systems run by a part-time operator who also drives the plow truck.
opportunities.why_overlooked: 120Water, BlueConduit and Trinnex took the top of the market — municipalities with GIS staff, consultants and capital budgets. Below that, the very small community systems and non-transient non-community systems (schools, mobile home parks, small manufacturers on their own wells) are numerically the majority and commercially invisible: no procurement process, no conference presence, ACVs too small for an enterprise sales motion, and currently running on paper and Excel toward default non-compliance. At the mid-market, the specific procurement insight — that the composition of the 2027 baseline determines a decade of obligations, so verification spend in 2026-27 has a computable ROI — is being executed by regional engineering firms billing hourly; nobody has packaged it as outcome-priced work. (Evidence caveat: both scouts hit a hard egress block and could only work at search-extract level, so dates and figures below are strong leads, not page-verified citations.)
opportunities.why_now: 1 November 2027 is the statutory compliance date for the baseline inventory, the lowered 10 ppb action level, updated sampling plans and the school/childcare list — and the practical deadline is earlier, because unknowns must be resolved by field verification, which takes dig seasons. After that date most systems must replace covered lines within ten years, with all lead service lines replaced by 1 November 2037 and remaining unknowns validated by 2034, so the annual reporting, notification and progress-tracking obligation runs continuously for a decade. Systems serving 3,300 or fewer people plus all NTNCWSs get an alternative route that still requires proving 100% replacement of lead and galvanized-requiring-replacement lines at a minimum annual rate within five years — a documentation obligation, not relief. The scale of remaining ambiguity is measurable: Wisconsin Watch reported in June 2026 that more than 181,000 Wisconsin service lines, about 12% statewide, are still classified unknown.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two people plus one subcontracted hydro-excavation crew, 90 days, one state. Build the predictive unknowns model from public data (parcel age, permit records, prior dig results), and sell a fixed-price 'unknowns reduction' engagement to five mid-size utilities priced as a share of avoided replacement obligation. In parallel ship the paperwork product that funds distribution: spreadsheet-import-first, takes whatever the operator has, structures it to the EPA inventory template, generates the public inventory page and annual replacement-plan document, and sends the individually-required customer notifications with delivery evidence — priced self-serve. Distribution for the small-system tier is state primacy agencies and rural water associations, which are already fielding these questions with no tool to point operators toward.

opportunities.name: Copper sunset triage for fire-alarm, elevator and area-of-refuge lines
opportunities.thesis: When a carrier retires a wire center, every copper POTS line it serves dies at once — and the lines that die are not phones, they are fire-alarm DACT circuits, elevator emergency phones and ADA area-of-refuge phones that building codes legally require to work (NFPA 72, ASME A17.1). Ordinary VoIP is not a substitute because it corrupts the Contact ID and SIA signaling tones a fire alarm communicator uses to report. Build the national data layer nobody owns: carrier copper-retirement and §214 discontinuance filings normalized to wire-center level, geocoded and joined to commercial property, elevator permit and fire-inspection records, so you can tell a portfolio owner 'these 42 buildings lose POTS within 90 days, here are the devices at risk.' Monetize as a per-line compliance registry — code-obligation mapping, sequenced cutover runbook, and an inspector-ready signed documentation packet — with managed cutover referred through the integrators who already hold the building relationship.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The visible market is hardware vendors selling a box (Ooma AirDial, DataRemote, MetTel, Granite) and thousands of local integrators doing reactive, door-to-door truck rolls. Nobody owns the layer above: a per-line risk registry keyed to wire-center retirement filings, mapped to the specific code obligation and the AHJ that will actually inspect it. Search turns up essentially one thin player (CopperAlerts) doing any form of wire-center alerting. It is invisible to software investors because it reads as a telecom reseller business, and invisible to telecom because it is a compliance-documentation business; HN treats POTS as a nostalgia topic rather than a live building-code emergency. (Evidence caveat: both scouts were blocked from opening pages directly, so URLs and quotes are search-extract level.)
opportunities.why_now: The FCC voted on 26 March 2026 to streamline copper wire-center retirement and declined to impose any compatibility requirement on replacement services, having already cut the notice period from 180 to 90 days — and Section 214 relief means carriers now give notice rather than seek approval. Ninety days is not enough for a facilities manager to inventory dependent systems, source a vendor, install, test and get re-inspected. AT&T began decommissioning roughly 500 wire centers (about 10% of its footprint) from June 2026 targeting effectively full copper retirement by 2029, with a November 2026 filing seeking to discontinue POTS for approximately 90,000 customers across 18 states; Verizon, Lumen, Frontier and CenturyLink have filed their own 2026-2029 retirement notices. Pricing forces action independently: POTS line rates are rising more than 30% per year, with single lines reaching $500-$2,700/month.
opportunities.buildable_today: 90 days, 1-3 people: scrape and normalize carrier copper-retirement and §214 discontinuance notices into a wire-center-level database, join to a CLLI/NPA-NXX lookup and to commercial property, elevator permit and fire-inspection datasets, and ship a free 'is my building in the blast radius' checker that takes a list of phone numbers or addresses. Convert to a paid per-line registry: line inventory, NFPA 72 / A17.1 obligation mapping, cutover runbook, and a signed documentation packet for the fire marshal or elevator inspector. First customers are portfolio owners with concentrated exposure and mandatory inspection cycles — hospital systems, school districts, senior living operators, REITs — sold alongside the fire-alarm integrators and elevator maintenance companies who are currently tracking this in spreadsheets and will refer deals to get the paperwork off their desks.

opportunities.name: Key-state custody for LMS/XMSS firmware signing under CNSA 2.0
opportunities.thesis: CNSA 2.0 mandates the stateful hash-based schemes LMS and XMSS — not ML-DSA — for software and firmware signing, and NIST SP 800-208 requires key generation and signing to happen inside a FIPS 140 Level 3 HSM with one-time keys that are never reused. That converts code signing into a crash-consistent distributed-state problem the industry has never had to solve: one HSM clone, DR failover, backup restore, CI rerun or parallel build job can silently and permanently destroy a device root of trust. Build the state custodian: a signing API in front of cloud HSMs that allocates monotonic indices under a replicated ledger, reserves disjoint HSS/XMSS-MT subtrees per builder so parallelism can never collide, refuses to sign on ambiguous state, and emits a tamper-evident index-usage log plus the audit evidence that no index was ever reused.
opportunities.why_overlooked: Essentially all post-quantum discourse and product is ML-KEM/ML-DSA in TLS, plus crypto discovery and inventory (Venafi, Keyfactor, QuSecure, SandboxAQ); a GitHub search for XMSS/LMS hash-based signatures returns exactly one repository — a 4-star academic VHDL artifact from a university chair, last touched 2026-02-12 — while CBOM/inventory tooling is already productised (cbomkit at 121 stars, awesome-post-quantum at 499). Stateful signatures are treated as an HSM vendor footnote; guidance itself notes that not all HSMs supporting ML-DSA support the stateful schemes and that state-persistence semantics differ per vendor, so there is no portable answer. The failure mode — state exhaustion and index reuse under backup/restore — is an operations problem, so cryptography vendors underrate it and sell HSMs or advisory hours instead.
opportunities.why_now: CNSA 2.0 says new firmware/software releases for National Security Systems should already have been signed with CNSA 2.0 algorithms by 2025; from 1 January 2027 all new NSS acquisitions must support CNSA 2.0, and classical-only signatures are not accepted by 2030 — 1 January 2027 is the point where guidance becomes a procurement gate, and the requirement flows down contractually to the defense industrial base. On the civilian side, OMB M-26-15 (24 June 2026, issued under the June 2026 executive order) sets a five-phase federal migration through 2035 with agency PQC migration plans due October 2026, and NIST IR 8547 deprecates RSA/ECDSA after 2030 and disallows them after 2035. Note one discrepancy in the raw material worth verifying before acting: the June 2026 executive order is cited as EO 14412 by one source and EO 14409 by another. Silicon and bootloaders architected in 2026 ship in 2028-2030 and stay in the field to roughly 2045, so the decision is being made now and cannot be re-made later.
opportunities.buildable_today: 1-3 people, 90 days. Ship an open-source LMS/XMSS state manager: a small daemon fronting PKCS#11 HSMs that hands out signature indices under a Raft-replicated ledger, implements SP 800-208 state partitioning (disjoint subtrees per CI runner), refuses to sign on ambiguous state, and emits a tamper-evident index-usage log — plus an open-source verifier and MCUboot/U-Boot reference code so customers can validate independently. Free wedge: a 'state fork detector' that scans an existing signing log for reuse. Sell the hosted multi-region control plane and the audit report first to defense-industrial-base and embedded/industrial OEMs who have just found CNSA 2.0 flow-down clauses in contracts or are failing CNSA 2.0 questions in RFPs, and to the ODMs who sign firmware on their behalf. Drop-in integrations for Yocto, Zephyr, MCUboot and U-Boot are the adoption surface.

opportunities.name: Trust-anchor retrofit for fleets whose boot ROM can't be changed
opportunities.thesis: Two forced root-of-trust migrations are landing on the same installed base: the 2011 UEFI Secure Boot certificates expiring in 2026, and the CNSA 2.0 / NIST IR 8547 move off RSA and ECDSA before 2030. All published guidance targets IT-managed Windows and RHEL fleets with vendor support contracts; the hard case is the long tail — industrial PCs, medical carts, ATMs, kiosks, POS terminals, network appliances, vehicle ECUs, defense COTS — where the OEM is gone, will never ship a firmware update embedding the 2023 certificates, or has the verification algorithm fixed in immutable boot ROM with no field upgrade path at all. Build the trust-anchor lifecycle layer: a read-only fleet scanner that enumerates PK/KEK/db/dbx state across heterogeneous embedded estates, joins it to a curated model-to-firmware-availability database, and produces a remediation plan plus an attestation artifact an auditor accepts. Convert that into the higher-margin engagement: PQC boot-chain assessments and a hosted stateful-signature (LMS/XMSS, SP 800-208) signing service so a mid-size device maker can issue PQC-signed firmware without building its own PKI.
opportunities.why_overlooked: Every artifact found — Microsoft's Windows IT Pro playbook, Red Hat's advisory, Dell's transition FAQ, Eclypsium's analysis, university KB pages — is written for managed Windows/RHEL fleets and explicitly punts on 'systems with no vendor firmware updates,' which is the population that matters. No product enumerates trust-anchor state across mixed embedded/OT estates via UEFI variables, BMC/Redfish and vendor tooling and maps model to firmware-release availability. The PQC vendor landscape (SandboxAQ, Thales, the PQC Coalition) is organised around enterprise IT discovery, TLS and VPN, sold to a CISO; embedded firmware signing uses different standards and a different buyer (a VP of Engineering at an industrial device maker), and most crypto engineers avoid SP 800-208 because state management is scary. Meta published its multi-year PQC migration and the discussion still centred on inventory and hybrid TLS; the HN response to the Secure Boot expiry was sarcasm ('Updating the Expiring Secure Boot Certificates Is Sure to Go Without a Hitch'), not tooling.
opportunities.why_now: Microsoft Corporation KEK CA 2011 expired 24 June 2026 and Microsoft UEFI CA 2011 expired 27 June 2026, with Windows Production PCA 2011 following in October 2026 — the failure is silent (devices keep booting but stop receiving signed pre-boot updates) and then catastrophic on a CMOS clear or motherboard RMA, where a system with no 2023-cert firmware release can become unbootable. The June 2026 executive order 'Securing the Nation Against Advanced Cryptographic Attacks' puts federal agencies on a clock — key establishment to NIST standards by 2030, digital signatures by 2031 — cascading immediately to federal suppliers, and the EU's coordinated PQC roadmap requires transition activities to start by end of 2026 with high-risk systems secured by 2030. The CRA's full application on 11 December 2027 turns 'this device can no longer accept signed updates' into a legal product defect for a declared support period. And the physics is unforgiving: a controller or ECU signed in 2026 may still need to verify firmware in 2041, so every unit shipped before the retrofit is a permanent liability. (Note: the raw material cites the June 2026 executive order as EO 14409 here and EO 14412 elsewhere — verify the number before quoting it.)
opportunities.buildable_today: Two embedded-security engineers, 90 days, two products that feed each other. First, a read-only fleet scanner: parse UEFI variables (PK/KEK/db/dbx) via efivarfs on Linux hosts, Redfish/IPMI on servers and vendor tooling on Windows, normalise into a trust-anchor inventory, and join against a hand-curated database of which OEM model has published a 2023-cert firmware release — sell the inventory report to hospitals, manufacturers, retail chains and colo operators, then attach remediation runbooks and a signed attestation artifact. Second, a fixed-scope $25-50k 'PQC boot chain assessment' for industrial controls, automotive tier-1s, medical device makers, energy meters and defense suppliers: enumerate every signature verification point, classify upgradeable versus immutable, and produce a migration plan with LMS/XMSS parameter selection. Target for 90 days: 8 assessments, 2 signing-service design partners, and an open-source SP 800-208 state-management reference that becomes the credibility asset.

opportunities.name: NQA-1 qualification and commercial grade dedication as a service
opportunities.thesis: The binding constraint on both the US nuclear build-out and the submarine industrial base is qualification, not capital, fuel or reactor design: a competent machine shop, forge, valve maker or cable house cannot sell a safety-related part until its quality program is audited against 10 CFR 50 Appendix B / ASME NQA-1 or NAVSEA requirements, and a commercial off-the-shelf part cannot be used until an engineer performs commercial grade dedication identifying and verifying critical characteristics. Today that is bespoke consulting in Word documents, and the only reuse mechanism (NUPIC) is a closed utility club new entrants structurally cannot join. Build the industrialised path: a fixed-fee turnkey program that installs an Appendix B / NQA-1 quality system in an existing AS9100 or ISO 9001 shop, plus — the real product — an outsourced dedicating-entity service with a structured critical-characteristics library, guided Method 1-4 verification workflow, and exportable, auditable dedication packages. Revenue is per-supplier onboarding plus recurring per-lot dedication fees and re-audit retainers.
opportunities.why_overlooked: Nuclear venture capital went almost entirely to reactor developers, fuel (HALEU) and now data-center PPAs. The qualification layer is served by aging QA consultancies billing hourly with no leverage, by ASME certification (a credential, not a service), and by incumbents like Curtiss-Wright and Paragon whose model is selling their own dedicated parts rather than enabling other people's suppliers. The problem is described in the trade literature as 'workforce qualification,' which reads as a training problem and gets answered with curricula rather than software. The reuse infrastructure entrenches the gap: NUPIC eligibility requires sponsorship by five member licensees and enrolls you into a 33-month audit cycle designed for the operating LWR fleet, and NIAC is likewise an incumbent club. Searches for nuclear supplier qualification software return NRC pages, EPRI reports and consortium PDFs — no vendor. (Evidence caveat: two of the three scouts were blocked from opening pages and worked at search-extract level.)
opportunities.why_now: The Nuclear Scaling Initiative's landscape report, covered by ANS on 23 March 2026, names the qualification pathway itself as the bottleneck — 'strict quality standards, including NQA-1, narrow the supplier base and slow expansion,' and without 'more efficient, repeatable approval pathways' the domestic industrial base cannot grow — alongside shortfalls in nuclear-qualified machinists, welders, inspectors and NDE specialists. Demand finally broke the chicken-and-egg deadlock in 2025-2026 via hyperscaler nuclear PPAs, plant restarts, the ADVANCE Act, DOE reactor pilot programs and a federal 300 GW-by-2050 target. On the naval side the money is already obligated: a roughly $950M NAVSEA award to BlueForge Alliance and 169 supplier projects totaling $648M across 32 states, against a submarine supplier base that has contracted from 17,000 to about 5,000 since the Cold War. Qualification takes 12-36 months, so shops that start in 2026 are the ones with capacity when first-of-a-kind SMR fabrication and fleet orders land in 2028-2031 — every month of delay now is a schedule slip then.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two to three people: ideally one ex-NUPIC lead auditor, one ex-supplier quality manager, one technical writer. 90-day wedge, product one: a fixed-price 'Appendix B readiness sprint' sold to five non-nuclear precision shops in Tennessee, Ohio and the Carolinas that already hold AS9100 or ISO 9001 and are chasing SMR RFQs — deliver the QA manual, procedure set and a mock audit for roughly $75-150k per shop plus an ongoing audit retainer. Product two, higher margin and faster to cash: commercial grade dedication on named obsolete or long-lead items for operating plants, which wins on both cost and schedule against reverse engineering or plant modification. Do not try to replace NUPIC — build the CGD workbench (critical-characteristics library keyed to common component families, guided Method 1-4 workflow, exportable dedication package) and sell it to two advanced-reactor developers and their top ten suppliers, where identical parts are being dedicated repeatedly across buyers and the reuse value is immediately measurable. Referral channel: reactor developers and BlueForge-funded supplier expansion programs with a starved supply base.

opportunities.name: Material Assistance Cost Ratio files for FEOC-exposed clean energy
opportunities.thesis: The OBBBA's foreign-entity-of-concern rules make every US clean-energy tax credit contingent on a Material Assistance Cost Ratio — the share of total direct component and material cost NOT sourced from a prohibited foreign entity — computed per facility or per component, supported by tiered supplier certifications, and defensible for six years against an extended IRS statute of limitations. This is a bill-of-materials cost-attribution and evidence-custody problem governed by tax rules, not an ESG or carbon problem, and getting it wrong voids 45Y/48E/45X credits worth more than the project margin. Build the supplier-certification collection network plus MACR computation and evidence-vault engine: templated attestations mapped to the Notice 2026-15 safe harbors, tiered supplier outreach, immutable document timestamps, and a calculator that produces the numerator and denominator with drill-down to each certification — sold per project and per product line with recurring annual recertification and IRS-examination defense.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The supply-chain traceability startup crowd is chasing carbon footprint, digital product passports and forced-labor screening; MACR is a different animal — cost-basis arithmetic under tax rules with statutory safe harbors, bought by tax equity counsel and CFOs rather than sustainability teams. Guidance only arrived in 2026, so the category is younger than the deal flow, and searches across FEOC content surface law-firm alerts (Cravath, McGuireWoods, Novogradac, Plante Moran, Baker Tilly, Morgan Lewis), distributor blog posts, installer checklists and one testing lab (Intertek CEA) — but no purpose-built tooling. The field is being served by spreadsheets and $1,200/hr counsel; the one company positioned nearby (Empact) frames itself as FEOC supplier risk evaluation, not certification chain-of-custody. (Evidence caveat: both scouts worked at search-extract level; WebFetch was blocked.)
opportunities.why_now: The trigger has already fired: the definitive FEOC rules bite for tax years and construction starts beginning after 31 December 2025, and Treasury/IRS issued Notice 2026-15 with interim MACR guidance — identification, cost-percentage and supplier-certification safe harbors — in February 2026. Thresholds ratchet annually: roughly 40% MACR for qualified facilities under 45Y/48E beginning construction in 2026 and about 50% for solar components claiming 45X, rising roughly 5 points a year toward 60% by 2029, so the burden gets strictly harder every year through the decade. Documentation must survive a six-year lookback, failure means full credit disqualification with a 10-year recapture window, and suppliers filing false certifications face a penalty of the greater of 10% of the underpayment or $5,000. Readiness is measurably poor: SEIA's Q4 2025 survey reportedly found only 38% of solar firms describe themselves as fully prepared for FEOC compliance.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two people — one tax/energy-credit specialist, one data engineer — in 90 days. Ship a hosted supplier-certification portal (standardised templates matching each Notice 2026-15 safe harbor, tiered supplier outreach, document capture with immutable timestamps) plus a cost-attribution calculator seeded with published module, cell, inverter and BESS cost stacks, producing a drill-downable MACR file. Two beachheads, pick both: sell a fixed-fee 'MACR opinion package' to mid-market EPCs and BESS integrators who cannot afford a national law firm — start with battery storage, where 2026 thresholds are highest and the supply chain is most China-exposed — and sell the same file format to tax-credit transfer buyers and tax-insurance underwriters, who have the sharpest incentive to demand a machine-checkable standard and will drag developers into it. The 2029-2031 revenue is recertification plus examination defense on a decade of installed base.

opportunities.name: Managed PSIRT for the CRA's 24-hour ENISA clock
opportunities.thesis: From 11 September 2026, anyone placing a product with digital elements on the EU market owes ENISA's Single Reporting Platform and a national CSIRT an early warning within 24 hours of learning of an actively exploited vulnerability, a full notification within 72 hours, and a final report within 14 days — including for products already shipped. Sell the outsourced product-PSIRT as a service, not a SaaS: component inventory and SBOM upkeep, exploit-signal monitoring mapped to that inventory, a defensible 'awareness clock' evidence log, a staffed 24/7 triage rota, and a human who actually drafts and files the three-stage notification under the customer's name. The differentiated asset is the SLA on the 24-hour clock, because no incumbent will underwrite it. The reporting relationship in 2026 converts into the December 2027 conformity contract — CE marking, technical documentation, declared support periods — which is the far larger, recurring annuity.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The commercial conversation is entirely 'SBOM generation,' aimed at software vendors and open-source foundations. The population actually caught flat-footed is small and mid-size hardware makers — industrial controllers, EV chargers, HVAC and building automation, lab instruments, connected appliances, robotics — who think of themselves as manufacturers who already survived CE/RED, plus US and UK companies who have just discovered EU law calls them 'manufacturers' and who have no EU regulatory function at all. The 2026 CRA Awareness and Readiness Report puts unfamiliarity as high as 72% in some regions, with only ~32% of manufacturers producing SBOMs for all products and 54% still unclear on the manufacturer/steward distinction. Notified bodies and testing houses sell audits, not an operational 24/7 notification capability; GRC platforms (Vanta/Drata-shaped) are built for SOC 2 questionnaires, not a statutory clock with forensic evidence requirements. GitHub contains roughly a dozen repositories matching CRA compliance — the largest an awesome-list at 41 stars created 2026-04-16, with craevidence/cli at 1 star and Complaro/cra-scanner at 3 — i.e. the tooling market is empty six weeks before the deadline. The hard part is not detection; it is a judgement call under time pressure with incomplete information, which is exactly what a service should absorb.
opportunities.why_now: 11 September 2026 is a hard statutory date roughly six weeks out, and it applies to legacy products already on the EU market, not just new releases. The horizontal vulnerability-handling standard has an adoption deadline of 30 August 2026 — the earliest of any CRA standard — and as of June 2026 several CEN drafts had closed public enquiry with none ratified or cited in the Official Journal, so manufacturers must self-assess without presumption of conformity. ENISA's Single Reporting Platform was reported as still not live in mid-2026. Full application, CE marking and enforceable SBOM duties land 11 December 2027 (with vertical/Milestone-3 standards due 30 October 2027), penalties reported up to EUR 15 million, and published cost estimates of EUR 20-50k per self-assessed product line and EUR 80-200k for Class I/II, plus at least half an FTE of ongoing PSIRT work. Evidence caveat: several contributing scouts could not open primary pages (proxy 403s), so figures drawn from search extracts and secondary reporting should be re-verified against the regulation and the OpenSSF report before capital is committed.
opportunities.buildable_today: A security engineer plus a regulatory writer. Pick one vertical where component stacks are near-identical across vendors (industrial automation or EV charging). Sell a EUR 3-8k/month retainer or per-product-line annual subscription with a contractual 24-hour SLA; 90-day target is 10-15 retainers. opportunities.name: Reachability-grade SBOMs and kernel-CVE triage for embedded Linux
opportunities.thesis: The CRA's expensive, recurring engineering cost is not writing an SBOM — it is deciding, every week, whether this week's kernel and package CVEs actually reach a specific shipped device, and proving it in a document that survives a market surveillance authority. Build the embedded compliance auditor: ingest a Yocto/Buildroot/PetaLinux build (or a raw firmware binary), emit an SBOM that scores clean against BSI TR-03183-2 rather than merely being schema-valid, index reachability from the kernel .config, defconfig and driver set, and run that index daily against the kernel CNA feed. Output a ranked affects-you / does-not-affect-you list with OpenVEX statements carrying justification strings ('not exploitable: subsystem not compiled in'), candidate backport patches, and the declared-support-period and technical-documentation artifacts. Charge per device family per year — this is a maintenance annuity attached to hundreds of millions of shipped units.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The CRA vendor landscape crowded into SBOM generation, storage and policy documentation and skipped both ends of the real work: the reachability decision, and whether the resulting document actually passes the de-facto quality benchmark. Maintainers document the gap themselves — a July 2026 CycloneDX .NET issue from a team preparing for CRA reports scoring 5.0 out of 10 on sbomqs because supplier, license, hash and dependency-depth fields simply are not in package metadata; relusion/CycloneDX.CRA.Validator, which checks against BSI TR-03183-2 v2.1.0, has 1 star, while cdxgen (generation) has ~1,023. The embedded estate where CRA's Annex III product classes actually live was skipped because it needs binary analysis and BitBake knowledge security vendors do not have: 'yocto SBOM' returns eleven repositories, the largest a 38-star vendor lead magnet, and the genuinely CRA-shaped tools are weeks old and tiny (shipcheck 17 stars created 2026-04-01, complira/yocto-sbom 3 stars, BitVex 1 star created 2026-05-29). BSP maintenance is served by boutique consultancies (Timesys, Koan, Ginzinger), not a scalable product; LTS-for-OSS exists for JavaScript and enterprise frameworks (HeroDevs) but not for embedded Linux.
opportunities.why_now: Reporting duties start 11 September 2026 and apply to products already on the market — so vendors owe answers before they own the inventory and reachability data needed to answer. Full application and CE marking land 11 December 2027, with Annex I Part II mandating an SBOM covering at least top-level dependencies, and the vertical product standards for routers, smart locks, cameras, microcontrollers and industrial firewalls were requested for delivery by 30 October 2026 — roughly a year of lead time. The kernel community now issues roughly fifty CVEs a week with no severity scores, while the default support window for a new LTS kernel has contracted from six years to two, widening the gap between what SoC vendors ship and what a CRA support period demands. And capacity is missing: on 11 June 2026 the CRA's notified-body rules began to apply with none designated, and accreditation typically takes 12-18 months.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two people with kernel experience, 90 days, one SoC family (NXP i.MX8 or TI AM62). Take a customer's Yocto/Buildroot manifest plus kernel .config, build the reachability index (is the vulnerable file compiled, is the subsystem enabled, is the interface exposed), run it daily against the kernel CNA and CVE feeds, and emit the ranked verdict list with justification strings plus OpenVEX. Free wedge with immediate pull: SBOM extraction from legacy firmware images that cannot be upgraded to a modern Yocto release, and a free BSI TR-03183-2 scoring report on whatever SBOM the customer already generates — then charge for the field enrichment, the signed attestation, and the per-device-family annual subscription. First customers: industrial and medical-adjacent device makers already fielding CRA questions from integrators.

opportunities.name: Cloud exit rehearsal before EU switching fees hit zero on 12 January 2027
opportunities.thesis: EU Data Act Article 29 abolishes all switching charges — egress included — from 12 January 2027, Article 30 obliges IaaS providers to enable functional equivalence, and the switch must complete inside a 30-day window. The price of leaving is legislated to zero while the engineering cost stays enormous, which turns exit from a CIO slide into a budgeted, dated project. Build exit as a continuously verified property: scan an AWS/Azure/GCP estate, score every resource for portability risk (proprietary managed services, IAM coupling, egress paths, data gravity), stand up a shadow target on a second provider, and run scheduled restore-and-verify rehearsals that emit a signed evidence report mapped to Data Act Articles 25/29/30/34 and DORA exit-plan testing. Sell the evidence report in 2026; sell the executor in 2027. The same pipeline runs in reverse as a compliance-and-remediation product for the thousands of ordinary B2B SaaS vendors who are 'data processing services' under the definition and have never modelled what functional equivalence means for their schema.
opportunities.why_overlooked: Coverage split into two lanes that both miss the build: IoT data sharing, and hyperscaler egress fees. Law firms have produced dozens of alerts on contract remediation and zero engineering products; FinOps vendors optimise spend inside a cloud; migration consultancies sell bodies on one-way lift-and-shift, not a continuously provable ability to leave — which is precisely what a DORA auditor asks for and what Article 30 makes contractually demandable. Legal advisories note companies are actively mis-scheduling roadmaps because most Data Act provisions applied 12 September 2025 while the switching rules only bite January 2027. And the mid-market SaaS long tail — 10,000+ vendors captured by the definition, not just the hyperscalers — has no product aimed at it at all. Until now the economics made rehearsal prohibitive, so nobody built the muscle.
opportunities.why_now: Article 29's transitional regime permitting reduced, cost-based switching charges runs 11 January 2024 to 12 January 2027; after that the ban is general and non-negotiable. That is roughly five months out — and practitioner analysis is explicit that six months' lead time is barely enough for serious exit planning, so contracts signed today already need the clauses. It compounds: the European Commission opened DMA market investigations into whether Amazon and Microsoft should be designated cloud gatekeepers, and the EU Cloud and AI Development Act proposed 3 June 2026 introduces a four-level sovereignty framework for sensitive workloads. Gartner projects European sovereign cloud IaaS spend rising from $6.9B in 2025 to $12.6B in 2026 and ~$23.1B by 2027 — that is the budget line this gets bought from. Sell against the loophole too: Recital 99 excludes continuous bi-directional data movement, so hybrid architectures keep the egress meter running.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two people, 90 days, two products off one engine. (1) Free 'Data Act Switching Readiness' scanner — read-only cloud scan plus a check of the vendor's public API surface, export formats and contract terms — as lead-gen. (2) Paid: a fixed-price EUR 15-40k remediation for SaaS vendors (draft Article 25 contract terms, build the bulk export endpoint, document functional equivalence) and, for buyers, a scheduled restore-and-verify rehearsal producing a signed exit-evidence report. Start narrow on object storage plus one managed database engine. First customers: EU-regulated mid-market where an auditor will demand the artifact — DORA-scoped financial entities, health, and public-sector suppliers. The clause library you publish becomes the standard and the distribution.

opportunities.name: Sealed-at-capture evidence for insurance claims and field inspection
opportunities.thesis: Stop detecting fakes and start attesting originals. Ship a mobile capture SDK that binds every photo, video and audio file to hardware attestation (Play Integrity, App Attest, secure enclave), seals it at the sensor with C2PA/PAdES-style signing and a timestamp anchor, and binds the seal to a claim number or work-order ID — plus an intake portal that verifies seals, checks anchors, and routes unsealed or provenance-stripped submissions to human review. The business is not the cryptography, which is collapsing to free: it is the vertical intake workflow that makes 'we only accept attested media' a defensible carrier policy and gives an adjuster a documented reason to reject everything else. Sell fraud-loss reduction per verified capture, not signatures.
opportunities.why_overlooked: Nearly all funded effort went into detection, because detection retrofits onto the fraud team that already exists — while the field numbers are publicly terrible: models scoring 95%+ on curated datasets fall to 50-65% on real claims media once compression, lighting and device variance enter. Attestation requires changing the capture workflow, which is harder to sell, so almost nobody sells it. C2PA discourse stayed inside newsroom provenance and never crossed into claims, lending, inspection or litigation exhibits. And the issuance layer is being deliberately commoditised — SEAL/letsseal gives away PAdES/X.509 sealing, OpenTimestamps anchoring and an RFC 6962 transparency log, stating outright that authenticity 'shouldn't be for rent' and that it is run as a public-benefit foundation, not a startup. Because the free layer looks like the whole product, the workflow above it is unbuilt.
opportunities.why_now: 2026 is when the loss data and the legal gap arrived together. Verisk documented an appraiser submitting 170 duplicate photos over two years against claims with $1M+ indemnity paid; 98% of insurers say AI editing tools are fuelling digital fraud and 99% report already encountering manipulated or AI-altered documentation, while only 32% feel very confident detecting deepfakes; 55% of Gen Z say they would consider editing a claim photo or document. On the legal side, proposed Federal Rule of Evidence 707 on machine-generated evidence was sent back for revision in June 2026 and cannot take effect before 1 December 2027 — and commentators note it applies only where AI creation is acknowledged, doing nothing for evidence whose authenticity is disputed. Meanwhile letsseal went from creation on 2026-07-16 to roughly 300 stars in under three weeks, and the C2PA conformance program now gives hardware-attested capture devices a certification path with assurance levels carried in the signing certificate — so 'sealed by a certified capture device' becomes a claim an adjuster can rely on rather than a vibe.
opportunities.buildable_today: 90 days: mobile capture SDK (seal at sensor, bind to claim/work-order ID) plus a verification API and intake dashboard that flags unsealed and stripped submissions. Beachhead on one workflow where the payer controls the app and fraud exposure is acute with few buyers: auto physical damage appraisal, auto glass, roof inspection, or equipment-finance collateral condition reports. Price per verified capture. Land one regional carrier or one large independent adjuster firm as design partner, and publish the honest benchmark showing detection accuracy collapsing from lab to field — that benchmark is the distribution.

opportunities.name: The C2PA referee: conformance evidence, survivability scores, and verification at ingest
opportunities.thesis: C2PA just became certifiable — a Governing Authority, Administering Authority, Certificate Policy, Generator Product Security Requirements, machine-evaluated Asset Rubrics, Assurance Levels carried in a dedicated X.509 extension, and a Conforming Products List. Three unbuilt businesses sit on top of one asset. First, conformance prep: a rubric-runner in CI plus the security architecture documentation and assurance-level gap assessment, the way SOC 2 prep firms grew around an audit standard. Second, the referee: an adversarial benchmark that measures whether a marking pipeline actually survives recompression, cropping, screenshotting, re-render and diffusion regeneration, publishing per-generator survivability scores. Third, verification-as-infrastructure for platforms and newsrooms: validate manifests at ingest scale, resolve trust lists and revocation, and — the interesting part — adjudicate the difference between 'no manifest' and 'manifest removed', cross-checked against soft-binding watermarks. Whoever owns the measurement owns the Underwriters Laboratories chair for content provenance.
opportunities.why_overlooked: GitHub's revealed preference is brutal and nobody is contesting it: the most-starred C2PA-related repository in existence is a provenance destroyer — wiltodelta/remove-ai-watermarks at 4,394 stars, created 2026-03-25 and still updated daily, roughly twelve times the 375 stars on the official contentauth/c2pa-rs SDK — with noai-watermark (148), C2PAremover (31) and image-fingerprint-remover (15, created 2026-05-21, offering safe/paranoid/nuclear stripping modes) corroborating. A search for 'c2pa content credentials' returns twelve community repositories and four of them are removers. Official conformance tooling launched in 2026 with 1 star each (c2pa-conformance-tool created 2026-01-26; the CLI 2026-03-11), while c2pa-rs carries 206 open issues. The ecosystem builds markers and viewers; literally nobody scores them adversarially and publishes the result, and there is no practitioner directory or prep vendor for an accreditation regime that is days old.
opportunities.why_now: The dated trigger is publication of the C2PA Conformance Program v0.2, Certificate Policy, Asset Rubrics and Generator Product Security Requirements on 2026-07-31, which converts C2PA from a voluntary format into an accreditation with named roles, assurance levels in the certificate, and a Conforming Products List. Simultaneously, removal industrialised in 2026: a PyPI-distributed CLI with a hosted consumer front end at raiw.cc, batch directory processing, and diffusion-regeneration attacks on invisible marks across Sora, Veo, Seedance, Hailuo and Kling — claiming an oracle-certified profile for defeating video SynthID. Those two curves cross now, with EU AI Act transparency duties for machine-readable marking of synthetic content and analogous US state provenance laws moving from principle to enforcement.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two people, one quarter, one wedge that feeds the other two. Ship an open-source asset-rubric runner as a GitHub Action — the rubrics are YAML with json-formula expressions evaluated against the crJSON a Validator Product emits — using c2pa-org/public-testfiles as the corpus. In parallel, assemble a transform corpus (recompression, crop, screenshot, re-render, diffusion regeneration, metadata strip), run it against those test files plus fresh outputs from each major generator, and publish a weekly per-generator, per-transform survivability leaderboard. The leaderboard is the marketing. Paid products: (a) fixed-fee Generator Product Security Architecture Document completion and assurance-level gap assessment for vendors chasing the Conforming Products List, and (b) a monitoring/verification API that samples a platform's live ingest and reports what fraction of arriving assets had credentials and lost them.

opportunities.name: Entry Type 13 and instrument-aware duty recovery for the post-de-minimis long tail
opportunities.thesis: The $800 de minimis exemption is gone, so parcels that used to clear on a manifest now need a real entry with 10-digit HTS classification, valuation, origin, an EIN and a bond — filed by licensed customs brokers, a profession gated by an exam with a 12-22% pass rate. That is a hard supply constraint meeting a demand shock. Build software that lets one licensed broker supervise 50-100x the entry throughput on low-value shipments, sold as entry-as-a-service to the SMB importers who have never spoken to a broker and for whom $50-100 of brokerage on a $500 shipment destroys unit economics. Bolt on the second half: duty recovery eligibility now varies sharply by which legal instrument a tariff was imposed under (Section 301 duties are generally drawback-eligible, Section 232 generally not), and reasoning across instrument, HTS line, country of origin and disposition is exactly the legal-grade work that LLMs newly do at near-zero marginal cost. The license is the moat; software multiplies it.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The visible startups — Zonos, Passport, Portless, Flexport — sell cross-border to consumer brands with real volume and real ops teams. The stranded population is the small domestic importer: the Etsy-scale seller, the parts distributor, the specialty retailer bringing in a pallet, whom 3PLs and forwarders are actively turning away. Nobody has attacked the broker-capacity bottleneck itself, which is the actual scarce asset, because investors read 'customs brokerage' as a low-margin services business. On recovery, roughly 80% of eligible refunds are never filed and about $15 billion in eligible tariff refunds go unclaimed annually — true for years because matching import entry lines to export lines cost more than it recovered below Fortune-500 scale; Charter Brokerage alone accounts for approximately one-third of all US duty drawback refunds, on 50/50 contingency splits and 9-12 month timelines. Honest caveat: 'best duty drawback companies in 2026' listicles now exist, so plain drawback-as-a-service is no longer uncontested — the unwritten layer is instrument-aware planning (drawback vs. FTZ vs. bonded warehouse vs. first-sale valuation vs. tariff engineering, per SKU per instrument), which today is sold as $800/hour trade-attorney time.
opportunities.why_now: De minimis ended for China/Hong Kong on 2 May 2025 and for all countries on 29 August 2025; the One Big Beautiful Bill Act signed 4 July 2025 permanently repeals the statutory basis effective 1 July 2027; and on 24 June 2026 CBP published an indefinite suspension of the administrative exemption. FY2024 saw over 1.36 billion de minimis packages enter the US. The integration door opens in seven weeks: CBP begins a voluntary ACE test of Entry Type 13 — a fully electronic informal-entry path for shipments valued at $2,500 or less — on 22 September 2026. On the recovery side, search-level sources report that following a February 2026 Supreme Court ruling (6-3) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, CBP launched the CAPE refund system on 20 April 2026, with roughly 75,300 CAPE declarations covering over 11.2 million entries submitted by 26 April — six days of filings covering eleven million entries. VERIFY BEFORE ACTING: the scout could not page-verify the SCOTUS holding or the CAPE figures; treat them as strong search extracts, not diligence. The strategic read is unchanged either way — striking IEEPA channels protectionism into Section 232/301/122 instruments with different eligibility and refund mechanics, creating a permanent reclassification and recovery surface.
opportunities.buildable_today: 90 days, two people plus one licensed customs broker as co-founder, advisor or broker-of-record — the license is a hiring problem, not a technical one. Product one: an HTS classification assistant plus an ACE ABI filing pipeline aimed at Entry Type 13, joining CBP's 22 September 2026 voluntary test as a day-one participant, delivered as a Shopify/WooCommerce/marketplace app that classifies a merchant's SKU catalog once, stores rulings and origin evidence, and auto-files at a flat per-entry price well under the incumbent $50-100. Product two, sold to the same accounts: ingest ACE entry summary data (importers can grant agent portal access today) plus export/destruction records and ship an eligibility triage that says, per entry line, which instrument applied, whether it is drawback-eligible, and the dollars at stake — priced flat, which is the obvious wedge against 50/50 contingency incumbents. Distribution: 3PLs and freight forwarders currently declining small accounts.

opportunities.name: Lot-code reconciliation and the 24-hour FSMA 204 spreadsheet
opportunities.thesis: FDA's Food Traceability Rule (21 CFR 1 Subpart S) requires covered firms handling Food Traceability List items to assign a Traceability Lot Code, capture Key Data Elements at every Critical Tracking Event, and hand FDA an electronic sortable spreadsheet within 24 hours of request. Do not build another EPCIS/GS1 platform. Build the seam layer: ingest whatever a trading partner actually sends — email, PDF, scanned BOL, EDI 856, a spreadsheet with a different lot format, a photographed case label — parse it into CTE/KDE records, probabilistically match inbound to outbound lot codes, score each shipment for traceability continuity, and produce two artifacts: the FDA-format sortable spreadsheet on demand, and a 'broken links' report the customer can email to the specific supplier who caused it. Own the mid-chain data and you own the traceability graph for US produce, seafood, cheese and prepared foods — with obvious downstream value in recall speed, shrink, supplier scoring and insurance underwriting.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The 30-month extension, made binding by the Continuing Appropriations Act of 2026, killed the market's urgency and its funding narrative: vendors who raised on the January 2026 deadline pivoted or died, and competitor roadmaps were deprioritised while the obligation itself did not move. Incumbents (Trustwell, ReposiTrak, TrueCommerce, iFactory, Wherefour) sell a system-of-record that assumes your partners adopt it too — but FDA's own data says the failure is at the seams, not inside the systems, and nobody sells 'lot-code identity resolution' as a category. Every vendor also aims upstream at growers, packers and processors where the CTE-heavy obligations and big contracts sit, leaving the two largest under-served populations untouched: the tens of thousands of mid-chain packers, distributors and cold storages, and the independent restaurants and 3-30 unit groups whose obligation is narrow (receiving records only) and whose ACV looks unexciting. Manufacturers are better equipped than downstream end users, who must receive, maintain and transmit information they do not handle today.
opportunities.why_now: 20 July 2028 is fixed by rule and reinforced by statute — in November 2025 Congress directed FDA not to enforce before that date through the Continuing Appropriations Act of 2026 — and there is no blanket small-business carve-out for anything on the Food Traceability List (only an exemption for establishments under $250,000 in average annual food sales). FDA has since published new industry resources, a stakeholder engagement initiative with guidance in 2026, and, decisively, the Traceability Readiness Tabletop Exercises run 9 March to 1 April 2026: traceability lot codes appeared in 80% of participant records, but only 40% of firms maintained a consistent lot code across every CTE they performed. That is a free, credible, government-authored sales deck naming the exact failure mode. Real implementation takes 18-24 months because it requires trading-partner data alignment, so serious buyers must start budgeting in 2026-2027, and upstream partners will push KDEs downstream well before the deadline.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two people, 90 days, seeded on the published FDA data model. Pick one FTL commodity with painful traceback history (leafy greens, shell eggs, or fresh-cut fruit) and one geography. Ship two thin capture paths and one export: (1) a phone app where the receiver photographs or scans the case label and pallet tag, OCRs and parses the TLC and KDEs into a searchable receiving log; (2) a document ingest that parses partner PDFs, scanned BOLs, email bodies and EDI into CTE/KDE records and runs the inbound/outbound TLC match; and (3) the only feature that closes deals — one-click FDA-format sortable spreadsheet export for any date range, plus the broken-links report. Charge $200-600/month. Sell to distributors and foodservice operators, who sit in the middle and get blamed for upstream breaks, and go to market through broadline and specialty distributors who need their independent accounts compliant. Ninety-day target: 25 paying mid-chain handlers and signed data-sharing links across three tiers of one supply chain.

opportunities.name: Battery Passport plumbing: supplier data chase, EPCIS event store, GS1-conformant resolver
opportunities.thesis: The EU is converting product traceability from a nice-to-have into a condition of market access, batteries first, and the passport is not a document — it is a signed, resolvable data object assembled from tier-2 and tier-3 suppliers who share no schema, system, or language. Three layers are needed and none is owned: the supplier data-collection-and-attestation workflow, an EPCIS 2.0 event store that logs what happened to each item, and a GS1 Digital Link resolver that serves the passport at scan time (the same resolver GS1's own Sunrise 2027 retail cutover requires). Sell the unglamorous middle — chase the missing supplier attributes, sign each claim, and run the resolver and event store as a managed service priced per supplier onboarded and per GTIN served. The consumer-facing QR experience everyone builds first is the worthless half.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The entire credible open-source surface is abandoned or hobbyist. Eclipse Tractus-X's digital-product-pass — the canonical EcoPass KIT reference implementation at 50 stars — is archived. GS1's own community-edition Digital Link resolver has 58 stars and opens its README disowning it ('not maintained by GS1 ... users should not assume that it conforms fully to the published GS1-Conformant resolver standard'), and GS1's own conformance test suite (14 stars) warns 'it's near-certain that there are bugs ... that could lead to false results.' The whole openEPCIS organisation — 22 repos of models, converters, validators, hash generators, and the flagship EPCIS 2.0 server — tops out at 11 stars, a single-maintainer dependency sitting under multi-billion-dollar compliance regimes. Everything else is 1-8 stars and a striking share are blockchain proofs-of-concept solving immutability, which was never the hard problem; the hard problem is that a mid-size manufacturer cannot answer what recycled-content percentage sits in a part bought from a tier-3 supplier.
opportunities.why_now: Dated triggers, with one caveat the scouts flagged and I am preserving: the EU Battery Regulation's passport obligation for LMT, EV, and industrial batteries above 2 kWh is understood to bite on 18 February 2027, but neither scout could open the primary legal text this session (WebFetch was blocked), so that date is UNVERIFIED and must be confirmed against the Official Journal before any go-to-market. What is directly evidenced from repo metadata retrieved 2026-08-02: serious implementation began January 2026 (artiso-ai/dppvalidator created 2026-01-29, 8 stars; hadijannat/mini-dpp-platform created 2026-01-04, 3 stars) and is still at single-digit-star scale seven months later, and the cross-standard vocabulary harmonisation work (openepcis/openepcis-dpp-ready, created 2026-04-27, 2 stars, harmonising GS1, EU ESPR, UNTP and CEN/CENELEC JTC 24) started only four months ago — schema stabilising, deadline dated, tooling absent. GS1's Sunrise 2027 2D-barcode cutover lands on the same Digital Link carrier, so one resolver serves both the retail and the regulatory demand. Note also that the 2025 EU Omnibus rollback of CSRD scope softened corporate sustainability *reporting*, a separate legal instrument from product-level passport obligations — that distinction is the thesis and is itself unconfirmed.
opportunities.buildable_today: Give away the wedge, charge for the labor. Ship (a) a free DPP schema validator and gap report that tells a manufacturer exactly which required fields it cannot currently answer, and (b) a free public conformance checker that scores any existing GS1 Digital Link resolver URL — both are lead-generation instruments against every brand already failing, and the dppvalidator precedent shows the free validator becomes the reference everyone tests against. Behind it, the paid product is a supplier-onboarding portal that chases named tier-2/tier-3 contacts for missing attributes with reminders, extracts values from the PDFs and spreadsheets they send back in six languages, signs each claim as a verifiable credential, and serves the result through a hosted conformant resolver backed by an Apache-licensed openEPCIS event store. First customer: a mid-size EV or industrial battery importer selling into the EU with no in-house compliance headcount — not VW or CATL. Price per supplier onboarded. 1-3 people, 90 days.

opportunities.name: Conformance oracles for tax code an AI wrote: golden vectors and Schematron drift diffs
opportunities.thesis: Government e-invoicing specs contradict their own reference clients, national CIUS profiles version several times a year, and implementers hand-transcribe hundreds of Schematron assertions into their own language where they silently drift. AI agents now write most of this integration glue and faithfully reproduce the wrong sentence from the docs. The business is an executable conformance oracle rather than documentation: versioned golden test vectors and byte-exact request/response fixtures per tax regime, a mechanically generated negative corpus with one document violating exactly one rule, a drift-detection service that diffs an implementation's rules against the official artefacts when they version, and an MCP server exposing validate_invoice() and explain_rejection() so an agent verifies a payload instead of hallucinating one. Compliance is the ideal beachhead for verified agent output because correctness is externally adjudicated: the invoice is accepted or it is not.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The sharpest artifact: Poland's Ministry of Finance repo CIRFMF/ksef-api issue #839 (2026-07-21) documents that the official docs say the initialization vector is prefixed to the ciphertext while BOTH official clients (C# and Java, with line numbers cited) do the opposite — producing a misleading HTTP 430 'invoice size mismatch' that sends integrators hunting through byte counting, BOM and encoding. The filer found it while building an AI-agent skill for KSeF integration and states the skill reproduced the doc sentence and therefore generated code incapable of sending a single invoice. A GitHub search for 'agent skill tax compliance e-invoicing MCP server' returns 0 repos — nobody has connected 'agents write integration code now' to 'government specs are wrong.' opportunities.name: Uptime as the product: continuity gateway for national e-invoicing rails
opportunities.thesis: When a country routes all invoicing through one government system, that system's downtime becomes a legally defined business state, not an IT incident — Poland codified this with a public, auth-free outage API whose legal basis is Article 106ne of the VAT Act of 11 March 2004, declaring MAINTENANCE, FAILURE and TOTAL_FAILURE events that trigger prescribed offline invoicing modes. Build the continuity layer: subscribe to the outage feed, expose a health gate the ERP calls before issuing, auto-switch to compliant offline issuance with correct numbering and storage, then reconcile and back-file with legally correct timestamps when the system returns. Generalize it into an event-sourced durability gateway — append-only outbox, exactly-once submission, signing-device state persistence, callback deduplication, automatic reconciliation sweeps against the authority's ledger — so a customer's core systems never encode a government's instability. Compliance vendors sell coverage breadth; nobody sells reliability as the headline product.
opportunities.why_overlooked: CIRFMF/ksef-latarnia is a real Ministry of Finance component, 16 stars, 27 open issues, with 'the Latarnia API interfaces are publicly available and require no authorization' in its README — and as of 2026-08-02 there are ZERO third-party products consuming it. All 22 KSeF repos on GitHub are invoice senders, viewers or gateways; the closest neighbour, 50bitSolutions/ksefwatch (created 2026-07-30), merely polls for new invoices every 12 hours and emails PDFs. The durability framing exists in the wild only as one developer's solo project: codercollo/axon (Kenya, created 2026-04-19, 0 stars) explicitly positions on decoupling from 'government API churn.' Kenya eTIMS has 11 repos total and two of the top three are unofficial API documentation individuals wrote because the authority's own docs were inadequate. Downtime handling is invisible to founders because it only becomes obvious after you have shipped and been paged at 2am.
opportunities.why_now: Poland's KSeF went to production on 28.07.2026, after the MoF changed validation rules on a live schedule (TEST 21.07, DEMO 23.07, PRD 28.07.2026), then publicly walked a validation back — issue #837: 'the validation described below will not be implemented at this stage; the case returns to analysis' — and a warning message was still misfiring after its own 16.07.2026 cutoff, per issue #843 filed 2026-08-01. opportunities.name: DMSMS resolution desk: last-time-buy brokerage plus qualified resupply for 20-year platforms
opportunities.thesis: Medical devices, factory PLCs, rail signalling, avionics and defense platforms run 10-25 year lifecycles on DDR4, LPDDR4 and legacy analog ICs that are being end-of-lifed and repriced upward at the same time, and these buyers cannot redesign because requalification means re-certification. The existing DMSMS tools are component-intelligence databases: they tell you a part is dying and then stop. Build the resolution layer — broker and finance last-time-buys against customer POs, certify pulled and refurbished parts with provenance, and when substitution is unavoidable, turn an EOL alert into a buildable technical data package and a qualified alternate source (including reverse-engineered or additively manufactured circuit card assemblies) with the qualification evidence attached so a program office can actually buy it. It is a working-capital and engineering-evidence business wearing a software hat, and the spread is set by other people's regulatory inflexibility.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The incumbent category self-describes its own limit: 2026 vendor comparison content on SiliconExpert and Z2Data states plainly that 'both are component-intelligence platforms, not sourcing tools. They tell you about risk; they don't give you a supplier to call.' So the expensive half of DMSMS — engineering a replacement and qualifying it — remains bespoke labor at specialty houses. On the software side there is nothing at all: a GitHub issue search for DDR4 end-of-life and 'last time buy' tooling returns 0 results, and 'DRAM price tracker memory market' returns 0 repositories; the one adjacent signal is a hardware price database whose own maintainer concedes his data is stale against the move ('many product prices (E.G. Ram and SSD prices shown are before the price increase, the current prices are not showing)', partsniper issue #2, 2026-06-15). This is a phone-and-spreadsheet business in an acronym-laden, DoD-instruction-driven, regulated supply chain — invisible to consumer tech media and exactly the shape SaaS-trained founders pattern-match away from.

Price: server DDR5 contract prices rose +57.3% QoQ in Q1 2026 and +49.7% in Q2, PC DRAM contract forecasts were revised to +105-110% QoQ, DRAM overall +90% in Q1 2026 versus Q4 2025 and DDR5 roughly 4x on the year, because HBM for AI accelerators is crowding out conventional DRAM at roughly 3:1 conversion at the fab level. Supply: DDR4 is in structural decline while still load-bearing for long-life equipment — a market summary posted 2026-02-19 puts the global DDR4 market at USD 23,800 million in 2026 falling to USD 12,500 million by 2034, a -6.2% CAGR (caveat: that figure came from a summary posted in a GitHub issue, not a filing the scout could open, since WebFetch was blocked). Pick two verticals with hard failure costs — infusion pumps and factory PLCs, or on the federal side obsolete analog and mixed-signal ICs on legacy circuit card assemblies — and build the cross-reference database mapping obsolete part numbers to available stock and qualified alternates. opportunities.name: Signed provenance for the secondhand drive and memory market
opportunities.thesis: AI datacenter demand has forced everyone outside the hyperscalers into the secondary market for drives and DRAM at exactly the moment industrial-scale counterfeiting is confirmed — workshops resetting SMART values, altering serial numbers, and relabeling consumer drives as enterprise. Build the provenance layer: parse Seagate FARM / WD-equivalent logs plus SMART and self-test history, score internal consistency (do head-level metrics, power-on hours and reallocation counts agree with a 'new' claim?), cross-check serials, and issue a signed, portable attestation keyed by serial that travels with the part. Extend the same grading standard to memory modules, because a five-year-old machine whose RAM alone now costs more than the whole machine did in 2024 is inventory rather than scrap, and refurbishment is currently merchandised on CPU generation and form factor while the value has moved to memory provenance. The pure-software insight nobody has exploited: FARM logs contain head-level and power-on evidence that is much harder to forge convincingly than the SMART fields the fraudsters are resetting. On the memory side, GitHub returns 0 repositories for refurbished server hardware inventory tooling, and demand is visible only as individual improvisation — developers costing out refurb boxes and discovering memory is the dominant line item, educators hunting sub-$100 builds, homelabbers writing formal hardware-refresh plans to reuse what they own.

opportunities.name: Sub-dollar satellite telemetry for assets nobody could afford to track
opportunities.thesis: 3GPP non-terrestrial-network support lets a standard cellular IoT module talk to a satellite, removing the coverage precondition that killed the LPWAN generation — Sigfox, Ingenu and most public LoRa networks died on a structural chicken-and-egg problem where the network had to exist before the devices that would pay for it, and coverage never reached the assets actually worth tracking: cargo at sea, rail in remote corridors, containers crossing between incompatible national networks. The business is not the constellation and not the chip; it is a single-SKU tracker on off-the-shelf NTN modules plus the vertical workflow that makes it useful, sold as a per-asset monthly subscription with connectivity included so the customer never sees a roaming bill. Everyone chasing satellite connectivity is chasing consumer direct-to-cell handsets, which is the crowded, capital-intensive half.

Two repositories on the entire platform for a standardized radio access technology is as close to a vacuum as this instrument measures — the calibration point is 55,891 repositories for 'RAG chatbot.' Beyond the empty developer ecosystem: 'IoT connectivity' is a category investors associate with a decade of disappointment and commodity margins, the direct-to-device narrative has been captured almost entirely by consumer smartphone emergency messaging, and the incumbent tracking vendors built on cellular are structurally reluctant to cannibalize roaming-based revenue.

Both scouts flagged the central claim — that per-device NTN IoT connectivity has crossed roughly the one-dollar-per-month floor that makes low-value asset tracking close — as unverified, because WebSearch budgets were exhausted and WebFetch was blocked on every host this session. Pricing is the entire thesis: if per-message and per-device cost has not fallen far enough, the opportunity fails, and confirming current commercial pricing and module BOM is the first diligence step. The only dated evidence actually retrieved is the neglect measurement itself (2 repos total; the more recent created 2026-04-16) plus the repos' own citations of 3GPP Rel-15 and Rel-16 NTN support, indicating the standards work is done and public. From model knowledge and explicitly unconfirmed: 3GPP Release 17 standardized NB-IoT over NTN, and Starlink Direct to Cell and Skylo's NTN service moved toward commercial availability across 2024-2025. Standards ratified and silicon shipping while the developer ecosystem is empty is the classic too-early-to-be-crowded window, but treat the cost floor as a hypothesis.

First customer: a single logistics operator or agricultural cooperative with a quantified loss problem, so the claims data proves ROI and becomes the sales asset. Defensibility comes from the vertical workflow and the carrier/roaming agreement, not the radio. Before any of this, spend week one confirming live per-device NTN IoT pricing from Skylo, Viasat and the module vendors — the wedge is only real if that number is under the vertical's tolerance.

opportunities.name: Part 146 ADSP certification: strategic deconfliction plus the sub-400-foot obstacle layer
opportunities.thesis: The FAA's BVLOS rulemaking creates a brand-new federally certificated business category — Automated Data Service Providers under proposed Part 146, separately authorized for strategic deconfliction, conformance monitoring, and supplemental data services. Every routine BVLOS flight, and mandatorily every operation over open-air assemblies, must buy from a certificated ADSP, which is a licensed toll position on US low-altitude airspace with no established winner. The visible entrants (ANRA, SkyGrid) are all racing at deconfliction because it is the glamorous algorithmic part; the supplemental-data lane is nearly empty, and the thing that lane needs — a survey-grade, continuously refreshed national database of sub-400-foot obstacles (distribution power lines, guy wires, transmission spans, met towers, temporary cranes) that existing FAA obstacle data does not resolve — is the input the deconfliction players will have to source rather than build. Sell the obstacle layer into utility, rail and pipeline drone-inspection budgets today; certify it as a Part 146 supplemental data service when the rule lands.
opportunities.why_overlooked: Software founders filed drones under 'failed 2016 hype cycle' and stopped reading, so the entire discussion sits in drone trade press and aviation law firm alerts rather than general technology media — the classic profile of an overlooked licensed market. Within the industry, commentary explicitly calls Part 146 'the real disruptor in the NPRM' that the industry is not taking seriously, and what attention exists is concentrated on deconfliction. Supplemental data services get dismissed as a commodity feed; building the obstacle database looks like fieldwork and a mapping company rather than a software company, which repels the typical founder. That mismatch between perceived and actual difficulty is the entire opening.

Certification takes time, so whoever is already collecting data, running software and holding operator relationships during the implementation window holds the first certificates, with the revenue curve landing 2028-2031 as routine delivery, infrastructure inspection and public safety BVLOS scale. HONEST RISK: this publication date has slipped repeatedly and could slip again into 2027 — of the dated triggers in this set, this is the softest.

In parallel, run strategic deconfliction and conformance monitoring as a free/low-cost API built against the published Part 108/146 requirements, integrated with existing Part 107 waiver operators and drone flight software, purely to accumulate flight data and operator dependence before certification exists. The regulatory work runs alongside; the data and the operator network are the moat.
