opportunities.name: Ride-through models and curtailment proof for NERC-registered data centers
opportunities.thesis: Data centers are becoming NERC-registered reliability entities with generator-like performance obligations, and almost nobody can do the engineering or produce the evidence. The business is a boutique that builds the filed dynamic model (EPRI UDM for the power-electronic portion, CMLD for cooling), runs disturbance-response testing of UPS transfer thresholds, rectifier and chiller settings, designs remediation, and assembles the attestation package — repeated per campus, per interconnection, per ISO, at roughly $150k-$600k a campus with mandatory re-validation after every trip event. Bolted onto that is the flexibility half: ERCOT's Provisional Controllable Load Resource construct splits a load into a firm portion and a SCED-dispatched flexible portion, and nobody sells the registration filings, penalty-exposure tracking, or the signed, timestamped metering record that proves each curtailment instruction was actually honored. Buyers are large-load customers (data center developers, electrolyzers, crypto) and the utilities that must administer these agreements; whoever owns the measurement and verification record owns the settlement.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The entire 'data center power' startup wave aimed at generation, siting and physical flexing (Emerald AI, VoltaGrid, Verrus, Build.inc), and the adjacent software money went to generator interconnection queue automation (Google/Tapestry HyperQ with PJM, Enverus SUGAR with MISO). Neither touches the load-side reliability-compliance obligation or the paperwork-and-proof layer that decides whether a curtailable interconnection agreement is granted, honored and paid for. Today that work sits with a handful of tiny consultancies (EPE Consulting, Keentel Engineering) and hyperscaler internal EE teams that have never filed a NERC-facing dynamic model; large-load interconnection is so new as a formal construct that incumbent transmission-planning software does not model it and consulting engineers do it by hand. NERC's own Large Loads Task Force white papers (Jul 2025, Mar 2026) describe this as a gap in existing practices and Reliability Standards.
opportunities.why_now: Four dated triggers have already fired. NERC issued a Level 3 Essential Actions Alert on 4 May 2026 — only the third in its 58-year history — with entity responses due 3 August 2026. FERC issued an order in Docket RD26-7-000 on 16 July 2026 directing NERC to file mandatory reliability standards for computational loads by 31 December 2026 and a Phase II work plan by 1 March 2027. FERC issued tailored Section 206 orders to every RTO on 18 June 2026 (Docket RM26-4) to accelerate large-load interconnection. ERCOT's NOGRR 282 grandfathers only facilities energized or study-complete on or before 14 November 2025 and imposes a 90-day root-cause / 90-day corrective-plan / 180-day implementation cycle after any failed ride-through. ERCOT is tracking more than 438 GW of large-load requests with roughly 198 GW applying in Q1 2026 alone, nearly 90% data centers — every one of which will need a filed, defensible model and a performance record by 2029-2031.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two power-systems engineers with PSS/E and PSCAD licenses and EPRI UDM familiarity, starting in ERCOT where the construct is furthest along. 90 days: publish a free 'NOGRR 282 / NERC Level 3 Alert readiness gap assessment' aimed specifically at ERCOT large loads that are NOT grandfathered (energized after 14 November 2025), then convert to the paid dynamic model build plus UPS transfer-threshold study — field data collects off existing PQ meters at the point of interconnection, and the scarce input is the person who can translate IEC 62040-3 UPS transfer behavior into an ISO-acceptable load model. Second product, sold to the same three data center developers already paying consultancies per filing: the PCLR/Batch Zero registration and modeling data pack (PGRR145 artifacts, ride-through documentation, self-limiting control descriptions) as guided software, plus a metering pipeline that emits a signed, timestamped curtailment performance record against each dispatch instruction.

opportunities.name: Neutral clearing house for the HTTP 402 crawler economy
opportunities.thesis: Cloudflare customers already return more than a billion HTTP 402 Payment Required responses per day to AI crawlers, and from 15 September 2026 AI companies that do not separate search crawlers from training and agent crawlers get blocked by default across a large share of the web. Two sides of that market are unbuilt. On the supply side, the enormous population of sites below CDN scale can only block — proof-of-work walls like Anubis, whose own design docs call the mechanism a stopgap — and a wall converts unwanted traffic into no traffic and zero revenue while breaking legitimate agents along with abusive ones. On the buy side, an agent paying thousands of micro-invoices across thousands of counterparties needs a wallet, spend policy, per-domain caps and an audit-surviving ledger, and none of that exists. Build the neutral rail: a drop-in origin module that verifies signed agents, admits and meters instead of walling, emits signed priced 402s and monthly settlement statements, plus an agent-side SDK — and stay neutral, because as pay-per-crawl becomes pay-per-answer the gatekeeper cannot credibly adjudicate its own attribution disputes.
opportunities.why_overlooked: All attention sits on the gatekeeper and on the big bilateral deals (Condé Nast, AP, Reddit, Stack Overflow, Patreon), a structure that serves the largest few hundred publishers and completely excludes the long tail that will start emitting 402s with no billing, reconciliation or dispute capability. RSL and x402 exist as specs with almost no operational tooling around them; the ecosystem below CDN scale has built blocking and nothing else, while metering and monetization are offered only by the largest edge providers — precisely the tier these operators are not on. Founders are additionally repelled by 'micropayments never work', a belief backed by twenty years of corpses (Flattr, Google Contributor, and most instructively Blendle abandoning pay-per-article); the usual diagnosis blames card interchange, but the real killer was the human decision cost per article, and the payer is now a machine with no decision friction at all.
opportunities.why_now: 15 September 2026 is a hard, announced default-block enforcement date with Patreon as anchor partner, and Cloudflare is already evolving pay-per-crawl toward a pay-per-answer model that pays publishers when content appears in an AI result — instantly creating a measurement and attribution dispute the gatekeeper cannot referee for itself. Supply-side pressure is extreme and measured: small publishers lost roughly 60% of search referral traffic over two years, mid-size 47%, large 22%. The enforcement primitives shipped in parallel — Anubis matured into a sponsored project with policy tooling, honeypots and nginx/Caddy/Apache/HAProxy/WordPress integrations, and samesame wired Web Bot Auth into Anubis in November 2025 — so cryptographic agent identity is already in the wall and only settlement is missing. Neutral clearing houses historically appear 2-4 years after a payment rail reaches volume, putting the window at 2026-2028. CAVEAT: the merged 'machine as payer' candidate's claims about x402, RSL and Cloudflare launch timing were self-flagged by its scout as unverified model knowledge and should be re-checked before acting.

Ship (a) an open-source Anubis policy plugin plus Caddy module that verifies Web Bot Auth signatures against published key directories, applies per-agent rate and price policy, and emits signed usage records — distributed free into the existing Anubis install base — with hosted monthly settlement behind it, and (b) an agent-side SDK with budget policy, per-domain caps and an exportable ledger. In 90 days: 200 long-tail publishers on the supply side (trade publications, recipe and how-to sites, specialist databases, regional publishers — the ones who will never sign a bilateral lab deal), aggregated into a single catalog under one set of terms because the buy side wants one integration not ten thousand, plus 3 AI/agent companies on the buy side. Then publish the first independent reconciliation report comparing what publishers were told they were owed against what your ledger shows. Charge basis points on settled access; the aggregation and the neutrality, not the metering, are the defensible assets.

opportunities.name: Tamper-evident record of which agent crawled what, under whose key, against which declared preference
opportunities.thesis: The IETF is formally amending robots.txt — draft-ietf-aipref-attach carries 'updates: 9309' and is authored by Google's Gary Illyes and Mozilla's Martin Thomson — and Web Bot Auth (RFC 9421 HTTP message signatures plus .well-known key directories) is shipping through Cloudflare as the way an origin learns which agent is knocking. Both stop at the instant of the request: preferences do not travel with the bytes, so the moment content is ingested the signal is gone and compliance becomes unfalsifiable, and when an implementer asked whether auditability of signed exchanges was in scope, the issue was closed. Build the acceptance layer in two halves — distributed vantage points that snapshot and cryptographically timestamp what preference each publisher declared at each URL at each moment, and a hardened verifier plus an RFC 6962-style append-only log that origins write verified request digests into. The product is the forensic report: did this crawler or model honor what was declared, backed by a dated, tamper-evident record. Buyers are publishers, rightsholder collectives, and the litigators and licensing lawyers who need an audit clause to mean something.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The AIPREF working group has burned roughly 100 issues and eighteen months arguing vocabulary semantics — whether 'search' nests under 'AI output', whether 'non-substantive' is the right qualifier, whether foundation models are too narrowly defined — and the vocabulary draft still carries a note that its contents DO NOT REFLECT CONSENSUS. Everyone is building the signal; nobody is building the proof of violation, which is the only artifact with commercial value. On the authentication side, the state of the art available to an origin not behind a major CDN is web-bot-auth's own explicitly unaudited examples, which a third party documented as fragile: the Caddy example returns success from Provision but leaves the validator nil and then panics on the first request if the key directory was unreachable at startup, loads only Keys[0] so key rotation silently breaks verification with no indication why, never refreshes the directory at all, and validates only a single signature.
opportunities.why_now: The attachment draft is the near-complete half of the work and formally updates RFC 9309, so the mechanism is settling now even while the semantics stay contested — that asymmetry is the window, and one participant has already argued in-thread for scrapping the vocabulary entirely in favor of a market for content rights documents. The verifying side is multiplying in parallel: 2026 produced vestauth (created 2026-01-15, 155 stars), FingerprintJS's verify frontend and backend, lightpanda's Go server, an Apache module, a Guzzle middleware, and samesame bringing Web Bot Auth into Anubis in November 2025. HONEST NOTE: unlike the grid and gas opportunities in this set, there is no statutory effective date forcing this — the dated triggers here are draft status and repository telemetry, not a regulatory deadline.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two products, both shippable in 90 days. First, a genuinely production-grade Web Bot Auth verifier module for Caddy, nginx and Envoy that fixes exactly the documented failure modes — load the full keyring from the directory rather than Keys[0], refetch on unknown keyid, refresh periodically, select among multiple signatures by label, support ECDSA P-256 alongside Ed25519 — released open source for distribution. Second, a hosted append-only transparency log the origin writes verified request digests into, sold as the subscription, paired with a free preference-archive crawler that snapshots robots.txt and preference headers per URL on a schedule and seals each observation with a timestamp anchor. Start free for publishers: the historical archive is the moat and it can only be accumulated forward from today, so the first 90 days are worth more than any later 90. First customers are publishers already running Anubis or Web Bot Auth, plus one rightsholder collective that needs diffs of declared preferences against observed crawler behavior in server logs.

opportunities.name: Licensed recovery and mass-balance ledger for phased-out high-GWP gases
opportunities.thesis: Two phase-outs with published statutory dates are simultaneously forcing a decommissioning wave and creating legally mandated demand for recovered gas. In the EU, new SF6 medium-voltage switchgear up to 24kV was banned from 1 January 2026 (52-145kV in 2028, 24-52kV in 2030, above 145kV in 2032), and the installed fleet of hundreds of thousands of units must by law have its gas recovered, reclaimed or destroyed by licensed and certified personnel with mass-balance records. In the US, EPA's AIM Act banned new R-410A residential and light-commercial installs from 1 January 2026 — starting the retirement wave that generates feedstock — while requiring reclaimed rather than virgin HFCs when servicing supermarkets, refrigerated transport and commercial ice machines from 2029. The business on both sides is the same shape and nobody has consolidated it: a certified recovery and reclamation service network (technicians, DILO carts, cylinders, per-pound tailgate buyback for contractors) plus the cylinder-level gas ledger — in/out, mass balance, certificate generation — that utilities, hyperscalers and reclaimers need to prove compliance. Razor-and-blades services with a certification moat and a captive installed base on a published retirement schedule.
opportunities.why_overlooked: Every narrative and all the capital went to the replacement product: SF6-free switchgear from ABB EconiQ, Schneider, Siemens, Eaton and nuVenturA, and in HVAC the industry's entire 2026 attention is on the A2L installation transition — training, tooling, warranty, labor premiums. The decommissioning tail is treated as a cost line inside utility O&M and handled by a fragmented set of regional switchgear service firms; on the refrigerant side, contractors routinely vent or dump recovered gas because the collection economics are invisible to them. Reclaimers exist but are processors, not originators, and there is no branded, contractor-facing collection network. No VC-backed company is visible in searches. It is gas plumbing plus paperwork applied to a molecule with a statutory buyer, which is exactly why it is still available.
opportunities.why_now: The dates are already law. EU: SF6 MV switchgear ban effective 1 January 2026 with staged deadlines to 2032, licensed handling required under the F-gas regime, reported end-of-life recycling cost of 10-20% of original equipment cost, and SF6 at a GWP around 24,300 — making any vent or leak a Scope 1 disaster for a hyperscaler with public targets, at the same moment the data center buildout is installing and retiring MV switchgear at record rates in the same jurisdictions. US: 1 January 2026 R-410A install ban starts the feedstock wave; from 1 January 2026 EPA-certified reclaimers must certify container contents meet the reclamation standard (max roughly 15% virgin by weight), formalizing the chain of custody; the 2029 reclaimed-use mandate creates guaranteed demand while HFC production allowances keep stepping down, making virgin supply structurally scarcer. A collection network built in 2026 gets repriced in 2029-2031.
opportunities.buildable_today: Pick one leg and one geography; both are two-person businesses. EU leg: one certified F-gas technician plus one operator — obtain the national F-gas handling certification in a single member state, buy or lease DILO recovery/reclaim carts, and sign framework agreements with two or three DSOs and one colocation operator for decommissioning-day gas recovery; add the ledger software after the first ten jobs, since the data model falls out of doing the work. The same playbook replicates in the UK, where servicing SF6 switchgear is already licensed, and in US states adding SF6 reporting. US leg: two people and a box truck — sign 30-50 HVAC and refrigeration contractors in one metro to a per-pound buyback for recovered R-410A and R-404A/R-22 mixes, supply certified cylinders and scheduled pickup, and sell aggregated volume to an existing EPA-certified reclaimer under an offtake. Working capital is cylinders and gas inventory; nothing here requires technology, only being the first person to show up and pay.

opportunities.name: Forward exchange for transformer and switchgear production slots
opportunities.thesis: Transformers, switchgear and turbines are now the binding constraint on roughly $750B of annual AI datacenter capex, and manufacturers hold production slots against a 10-30% deposit. That makes a slot a de facto option contract with no market, no price discovery, no verification and no way to resell when a site dies — and everybody over-orders, double-booking slots across two or three manufacturers as insurance, so a large stock of paid-for slots is already orphaned. Build the clearinghouse: verified slot listings confirmed directly with the OEM order desk, standardized spec templates (kVA, voltage class, impedance, delivery window), escrow, assignment paperwork, and eventually a forward curve on MVA by delivery quarter. The monetizable fact is that half the announced projects will never break ground.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The entire investor conversation is about building more transformers — capital-intensive with a 3-5 year payback — or about used-equipment brokerage of physical assets (Transformer Exchange, VAWN lead-time indices), which is old-school and backward-looking. Nobody is trading the forward position. Industry sources openly acknowledge the phantom demand that makes the secondary market necessary: Terrapin's 2026 lead-time report states outright that there is believed to be double booking on transformers and switchgear because of extra-long lead times, which inflates backlogs and hides real availability. GE Vernova's slots are reported tight through 2030 and MV switchgear is described as sold out through 2028 in many channels, yet a large share of announced capacity will never be built — and there is no venue where those slots can change hands.
opportunities.why_now: The gap between announced and constructed capacity blew open in 2026: Sightline Climate tracked 12-16 GW of announced US datacenter capacity for 2026 with only about 5 GW under construction, and roughly $650B was committed to AI datacenters this year against components representing less than 10% of build cost. Lead times went from about 40 weeks pre-pandemic to 24-60 months; substation transformers now run 75-110 weeks and GSU transformers 100-150+ weeks. FERC's 18 June 2026 Show Cause Orders to all six RTOs (Docket RM26-4) force expedited co-location and large-load study processes, which will pull even more simultaneous orders into the queue and deepen the double-booking. By 2029-2031 the orphaned-slot pool is a multi-billion-dollar secondary asset class, and whoever holds the transaction data owns the only real forward curve for grid iron.
opportunities.buildable_today: No product for the first 20 trades. Two people with an energy-procurement background run a brokerage desk: cold-call the roughly 200 datacenter, BESS and utility developers with cancelled or delayed projects, list their slots, match to buyers, take 2-4% and escrow the deposit. Then build the listing and verification product — a slot record confirmed directly with the OEM order desk and standardized on kVA, voltage class, impedance and delivery window. Ninety-day goal: 10 closed assignments and a proprietary dataset of real transacted slot prices that nobody else has, which is the seed of the forward curve.

opportunities.name: Carrier-side credential passport after Montgomery v. Caribe
opportunities.thesis: On 14 May 2026 the Supreme Court held 9-0 in Montgomery v. Caribe Transport II that state-law negligent-selection claims against freight brokers survive FAAAA preemption, and brokers tightened carrier vetting within 24 hours. The entire existing vetting stack — Highway, RMIS, MyCarrierPortal, FreightValidate — is broker-side software that treats small carriers as risk to be excluded, and nobody sells anything to the roughly 600k small motor carriers now being locked out. Carrier-side pain was previously merely annoying, so no product exists whose customer is the carrier; SCOTUS made it existential and the market has had under three months to react. The magnitude is measured: Overdrive's 2026 owner-operator survey found only 39% of owner-operators had never been denied business based on information in a vetting platform — meaning 61% have been — with RMIS at 69% and Highway at 61% penetration.

Simultaneously, FMCSA's non-domiciled CDL final rule took effect 16 March 2026 and is removing roughly 194,000 drivers (about 200k holders down to roughly 6k), with California revoking around 17,000 CDLs and New York facing 16,000+ — so brokers are vetting harder against a shrinking, churning carrier base. By 2029-2031, negligent-selection verdicts will have repriced broker liability insurance and provable carrier quality becomes the gating asset in a $1T+ freight market.

A two-person shop charges owner-operators $99/month to monitor their FMCSA/SAFER/CSA profile, insurance certificates and status across the vetting platforms, alerts them the day something flips, and files corrections and DataQs on their behalf. opportunities.name: Customs bond sufficiency radar for tariff-exposed importers
opportunities.thesis: A continuous customs bond is sized at 10% of the importer's prior-year duties, taxes and fees, so when tariff rates jump 3-5x the bond silently goes insufficient and CBP halts cargo at the port with a surprise insufficiency notice. Build the monitoring layer first: pull an importer's ACE/ABI entry summary data, forecast rolling 12-month duty liability, project the exact date the bond goes short, and broker the increase before CBP notices. Revenue starts as a per-importer SaaS subscription plus surety agency commission on every bond increase you trigger, and graduates into an MGA writing the customs surety itself once you can prove a loss-ratio edge from having real-time duty exposure data no surety has today.
opportunities.why_overlooked: This sits in the seam between customs brokers, who do not underwrite, and sureties, who do not build software — so neither builds the product. The entire trade-tech funding wave went to HTS classification, landed-cost calculators and duty drawback (drawback alone drew roughly half a dozen funded 2026 entrants); bond adequacy drew none. Sureties are reportedly managing 200-550% bond increases on spreadsheets, and CBP surfaces insufficiency as an after-the-fact notice rather than a forecast, so the importer's first signal is cargo already stopped.
opportunities.why_now: CBP recorded 27,479 bond insufficiencies in fiscal 2025 worth nearly $3.6 billion — the highest count and highest total value ever recorded, roughly double the 2019 Section 301 peak, and CNBC put the shortfall at $3.5 billion in a Feb 12, 2026 report. 2026 stacked new layers on top: a 10% universal Section 122 surcharge effective Feb 24, 2026; restructured Section 232 steel and aluminum duties at 50% of full customs value effective April 6, 2026; and indefinite suspension of the de minimis exemption by regulation effective June 24, 2026, with statutory repeal following July 1, 2027. Bond amounts now span the $50,000 minimum to $450 million, and duty levels look like a durable feature of the 2026-2031 political economy, so exposure recomputes and compounds every year.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two people — one licensed customs broker, one engineer. Months 1-2: build the ACE/ABI data pull plus a rolling duty-forecast model, and sell a $500/month bond sufficiency monitor to 50 mid-market importers using customs brokers as the referral channel (brokers want the save, not the liability). Month 3: sign on as an agent of one existing customs surety and take commission on every bond increase the monitor triggers. No balance sheet or capital required for phase one; the MGA only comes after the forecast data proves out.

opportunities.name: CUI determination and marking for small defense machine shops
opportunities.thesis: Every CMMC vendor sells the enclave — GCC High, managed SIEM, a policy binder — but almost none solve the step that actually fails assessments: a 30-person machine shop cannot tell which of the thousands of drawings, travelers, quotes and emails moving through it is Controlled Unclassified Information. Build a determination-and-marking engine that ingests customer drawings and PDFs, reads DoD distribution statements and DFARS flow-down clauses, decides CUI vs FCI vs neither, applies correct markings, and emits shop-floor labels and a defensible audit trail for the traveler packet. opportunities.why_overlooked: The market has decided CMMC is an IT-infrastructure purchase, so money and attention flowed to enclaves and MSSPs. But missing or incorrect CUI marking keeps showing up among the top findings in 2025-2026 reviews, and 'we don't have CUI' remains a near-universal and near-universally wrong belief among active DoD subcontractors. The real failure mode is document classification and physical shop-floor labeling, not networking, which is precisely why an MSP-shaped industry is structurally blind to it. The tell: the best available how-to material is a self-published Amazon guide and blog posts from label vendors — no software product owns this.
opportunities.why_now: The 48 CFR CMMC acquisition rule was published in the Federal Register on September 10, 2025 and took effect November 10, 2025, converting CMMC from guidance into a binding contract clause for primes and subcontractors alike. Phase 1 (Nov 2025 through late 2026) is self-assessment; the phase requiring third-party Level 2 certification begins around November 2026 and ramps over three years, so the certification wave hits the long tail of tens of thousands of small shops across 2027-2029. Subcontractors touching CUI must meet the same bar as primes or lose the award, and small contractors face $20k-$100k+ in compliance cost. It is a mandatory purchase with an already-effective legal trigger.
opportunities.buildable_today: 90 days: a drop-a-folder desktop/web tool that parses distribution statements B through F, export-control markings and DFARS 252.204-7012 flow-down language out of PDFs and CAD title blocks, then emits a per-file CUI determination with written rationale, a marking overlay, a printable CUI cover sheet and a shop-floor label. Land 10 consultancies, reach a few hundred shops.

opportunities.name: Condo project remediation for the GSE mortgage-ineligible list
opportunities.thesis: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac maintain non-public lists of condo and co-op projects ineligible for conventional financing; a project lands there for deferred maintenance, structural findings, thin reserves or non-conforming insurance, and the first anyone learns of it is when a buyer's loan dies at underwriting. Build the diagnostic-and-remediation business: assess a project against published GSE eligibility criteria, produce the specific defect list, run the fixes (reserve study, insurance rebuild, structural documentation, assessment plan), and maintain a continuously updated project eligibility file that lenders and listing agents can trust. The recurring revenue is a per-project subscription sold across a management company's whole portfolio; the second line is selling verified project status to lenders and agents.
opportunities.why_overlooked: Proptech capital went to brokerage, rentals and mortgage origination. Association governance is served by decades-old HOA software (Yardi, AppFolio, TOPS) that handles accounting and violations, not capital-markets eligibility. Property managers, boards and lenders each assume one of the others owns the problem, so nobody does. The opacity is the whole mechanism: because the list is secret there is no market signal, no ranking and therefore no product — which is exactly the arbitrage. Reported scale is 696 affected projects across Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach as of March, and figures up to roughly 1,700 projects nationally, but the true number is unknown because the list is hidden.
opportunities.why_now: Honest caveat: the group's raw material contains no single published effective date for the decisive unlock. opportunities.name: Micropollutant EPR fee ledger for pharma and cosmetics under the UWWTD
opportunities.thesis: The recast Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive (EU) 2024/3019 makes pharmaceutical and cosmetics producers fund at least 80% of the capital and operating cost of new quaternary treatment across the EU — the first extended producer responsibility scheme in history levied on molecules rather than packaging. Each company's fee is a function of the mass and hazardousness of the substances it placed on each national market, and today no company can compute that number and no national producer responsibility organisation can allocate it. Build the substance-mass-on-market ledger and fee simulator that sits between thousands of marketing authorisation holders and cosmetics responsible persons and 27 national schemes. The same dataset becomes the input to reformulation and portfolio-exit decisions, which is the far larger business.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The industry's entire response so far has been litigation rather than tooling: EFPIA, AESGP and off-patent manufacturers filed annulment actions, the EU General Court dismissed them as inadmissible in February 2026, and Zentiva has appealed to the CJEU — meaning the sector spent two years trying to argue the law away instead of building the data infrastructure to comply with it. Searching for UWWTD EPR fee calculation software returns law-firm alerts and consultancies (CEHTRA, Ithos, Ramboll), not a product, versus a dozen software vendors serving packaging EPR. The obligated entity is also non-obvious — it is whoever places the product on the market, which for generics is the MAH rather than the API maker — and nobody has mapped that graph.
opportunities.why_now: The dates are in law and now legally unavoidable: member states must transpose by 31 July 2027, EPR schemes must be operational by 31 December 2028, and quaternary treatment milestones follow in 2033, 2039 and 2045, with producers covering a minimum of 80% of additional treatment cost. The February 2026 General Court dismissal removed the 'it might be annulled' excuse that was suppressing compliance spend. Critically, each member state writes its national implementing law during 2026-2027, which is exactly when the mass-times-hazard fee methodology gets fixed — a 12-18 month window to become the reference calculation before the formulas harden. Pharmaceutical and cosmetic residues are cited as the source of about 90% of the micropollutants requiring the new treatment.
opportunities.buildable_today: 90 days: ingest national medicines sales and dispensing datasets plus cosmetics volume data, map to substance identity (INN/CAS), join to ecotoxicity and persistence endpoints from ECHA and EMA environmental risk assessment dossiers, and output a per-member-state, per-product fee exposure model with scenario toggles for the different national weighting formulas being drafted. First product is a EUR 30-80k board-level exposure report, not software: the top 50 generics and cosmetics groups each need a defensible provision number for their 2027 statutory accounts, and their finance function will buy it before their regulatory function will. Convert those accounts to the recurring filing product as national PROs stand up in 2028.

opportunities.name: EU positive-list clearance for drinking-water contact materials
opportunities.thesis: Commission Implementing Decisions (EU) 2024/367 and 2024/368 create the first single European positive list of starting substances, compositions and constituents permitted in anything that touches drinking water — pipes, valves, pumps, meters, taps, gaskets, membranes, coatings and resins. From 31 December 2026 a product may only be placed on the EU market if every substance in it appears on the list, backed by an EU declaration of conformity and EU-specific marking. Build the clearance layer: bill-of-materials and formulation in, list-conformance verdict plus a gap, testing and derogation plan out.
opportunities.why_overlooked: This is plumbing-industry regulation, which makes it invisible to software people, and it is currently served by test houses (NSF, KIWA, DVGW, WRAS) and consultancies rather than by any product. The EU lists were assembled by merging the national lists member states notified to ECHA in 2021, so a substance perfectly legal under one national scheme can simply be absent from the European list — FOBIG's own framing is literally 'are your substances covered'. There is no searchable machine-readable conformance tool, no supplier-declaration collection workflow, and no queue management for the substance-addition applications that will be needed. Meanwhile the compliance-software crowd is entirely occupied with PFAS and digital product passports.
opportunities.why_now: 31 December 2026 is roughly five months out and the regime applies in full from that date for new products, while a legacy transition runs to the end of 2032 for products already certified under national schemes such as UBA. That double clock is the business: an acute crisis for every 2027 product launch, plus a five-year dated re-certification pipeline covering every legacy SKU through 2032. Conformity-assessment and testing lab capacity is the binding constraint, so whoever can pre-screen and triage which SKUs actually require lab work owns the funnel into a multi-billion-euro component market, and the UK is explicitly considering mirroring the regime.
opportunities.buildable_today: 90 days: scrape and normalise the positive lists from the Official Journal annexes to 2024/367 into a queryable CAS-level substance database, then build a supplier-declaration portal that collects composition under NDA, runs the conformance check, and produces a red/amber/green SKU matrix, a prioritised lab-testing plan aligned to the 2024/368 methodologies, and draft substance-addition dossiers for the gaps. opportunities.name: Wind-Down Desk: Asset Re-Homing for the Small Businesses That Never Sell

opportunities.name: The 24-Month Clock on Every Bridge-Power Turbine
opportunities.thesis: With grid interconnection and new gas turbine slots gone until 2030, a large share of new data center capacity is being energized on temporary on-site turbines and engines. EPA's stationary combustion turbine NSPS created a conditional exclusion for temporary units capped at 24 months on site — and if a unit stays longer, EPA applies the rule retroactively as though it had always been permanent, putting the operator in immediate noncompliance. The business is the fleet clock: a dated registry of every bridge-power unit and its on-site tenure, sold as a subscription exposure report to data center owners, their lenders and their insurers, with rotation/relocation orchestration and the permanent-source NNSR/Title V fallback application as the services upsell.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The bridge-power conversation is entirely about supply and megawatts — VoltaGrid, ProEnergy, Aggreko, United Rentals — while the compliance clock is buried in an NSPS most developers read once for the good news (reduced permit obligations) and never operationalize. Searches surface no product, no tracking system and no service firm. The retroactive-noncompliance mechanic means the liability stays invisible until it is catastrophic, which is the classic shape of an overlooked services market.
opportunities.why_now: The rule published 15 January 2026, so the first cohort of units placed under the exclusion hits month 24 in early 2028, and units deployed through 2026-2027 hit it in 2028-2029 — precisely when grid interconnection for most of these campuses still will not be complete. GE Vernova's turbine book is sold through 2030 with roughly 10 GW remaining across 2029 and 2030 combined (Power Engineering, July 2026), Siemens' large-frame slots are nearly full for 2028, and Mitsubishi has warned new blocks may not ship until the 2030s. That guarantees bridge power sits on site well past 24 months unless somebody manages the rotation.
opportunities.buildable_today: An air permitting engineer plus an operations analyst, capital-free. In 90 days: build the registry — scrape state air permit databases, construction notices and rental-fleet deployment announcements to identify temporary turbine and large reciprocating-engine installations at data centers, date-stamp each one, and compute months-to-exposure. First product is a quarterly 'clock and exposure report' per campus; first customers are the lenders and insurers on two or three named Virginia, Ohio or Texas data center projects, who will pay for exposure they cannot otherwise see, followed by the owners themselves once the report lands on their desk.

opportunities.name: Tank Car Shop-Slot Brokerage Ahead of the May 2029 DOT-117R Deadline
opportunities.thesis: Roughly 17,000 tank cars carrying PG II/III flammable liquids must be retrofitted to DOT-117R or replaced by 1 May 2029, while the pool of qualified tank car repair facilities shrinks and new-build 117J lead times run 12-18 months at premium pricing. The business is a retrofit-capacity brokerage plus fleet compliance triage: contract forward shop slots at certified facilities now, run car-by-car retrofit-versus-replace-versus-retire engineering economics for shippers and lessors, and resell matched slots into the 2027-2028 crunch. It is pure scheduling arbitrage against a statutory date with no possibility of substitution, and it requires no capital beyond the working capital behind slot deposits.
opportunities.why_overlooked: Rail assets are not a venture category and 2029 sits just past most fleet managers' planning horizons. The visible commentary comes from railcar lessors and brokers marketing their own inventory rather than from anyone aggregating shop capacity across facilities. The industry has repeatedly assumed there is sufficient shop capacity — the same assumption that failed in the last 18 months of the 2015-2020 crude/ethanol phase-out.
opportunities.why_now: The deadline is fixed by statute at 1 May 2029 for the remaining moderately-to-mildly flammable PG II/III liquids; the earlier tranches already cleared by 1 May 2025, which means the remaining ~17,000 cars are the hardest, least economic segment, owned by the smallest shippers with the least planning capacity. Retrofit demand will compress into 2027-2028 as owners wait for clarity, exactly when shop capacity is also absorbed by ordinary requalification cycles. Slots contracted cheaply in 2026 are worth a multiple in 2028.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two people with rail mechanical and commercial backgrounds. In 90 days: enumerate the certified tank car repair facilities using the BTS Annual Tank Car Facility Survey, sign non-binding forward capacity agreements for 2027-2028 slots at three to five shops, and in parallel sell a paid fleet triage to 20 mid-size chemical and ethanol shippers — car-by-car retrofit economics built from AAR/UMLER data. First customer is a mid-size specialty chemical shipper with 150-400 legacy cars who has not yet modeled the 2029 cliff; the triage report is the paid entry point and the slot book is the follow-on.

opportunities.name: The Covered-Entity Side of the 340B Rebate Flip
opportunities.thesis: HRSA's 340B Rebate Model Pilot inverts a 30-year-old mechanic: hospitals and clinics will buy at wholesale acquisition cost and then submit claims-level data to manufacturers to claw the discount back as a rebate. Every dollar of software money so far has gone to the manufacturer side, leaving the covered entity with a submission, tracking, dispute and reconciliation problem plus a brand-new cash-flow hole. The product is a rebate-claim engine wired into pharmacy dispensing and split-billing systems with a 45-day-per-claim deadline tracker, and — the real prize — working-capital financing advanced against pending 340B rebate receivables. Buyer is the hospital or FQHC 340B program director and pharmacy finance lead; budget line is 340B program savings, which for many safety-net hospitals is the operating margin.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The vendor landscape is entirely manufacturer-facing. Kalderos, the platform manufacturers proposed to use to administer rebates, was acquired by Model N in June 2026 and folded into life-sciences gross-to-net revenue management; 340B ESP (Second Sight Solutions) is likewise the manufacturer-mandated claims-data platform; Craneware and peers serve split-billing and compliance, not rebate claiming or the resulting cash-flow gap. Providers are publicly objecting to the administrative burden rather than buying anything — because there is nothing to buy. Model N's own 2026 State of Revenue Report reports only 1% of life sciences revenue leaders have real-time visibility into 340B discounts and rebates, so even the funded side of the market is immature.
opportunities.why_now: HRSA paused the model for court reasons and reset the pilot to start 1 January 2027. Manufacturers had to submit claims-collection and rebate-issuance plans by 24 August 2026 with approvals around 24 September 2026, and HRSA has published notice contemplating expansion to roughly 25 products from 13 manufacturers. The operational forcing function is the 45-calendar-day window from date of dispense to submit data and claim a rebate. HRSA's own estimate is roughly 15,250 covered entities carrying nearly 4 million hours of annual burden, about 260 hours per entity — a recurring operational load that arrives on a fixed date.
opportunities.buildable_today: A two-to-three person team, one of whom knows pharmacy 340B split-billing plumbing. In 90 days: build the claims-extraction and rebate-submission connector for one or two of the most common dispensing/split-billing systems, wrap it in a 45-day-per-claim deadline tracker with per-claim status and manufacturer dispute handling, and pilot with 5-10 DSH hospitals or FQHC networks that already know the cash-flow hit lands 1 January 2027. First customer is a multi-site FQHC network whose 340B savings fund clinical staffing. Financing starts as simple factoring against validated, submitted claims once the data pipeline is trusted.
source_lenses: Revealed enterprise demand — what large organizations are actively trying to buy or staff for, where no good vendor exists

opportunities.name: Work-Hours Capture Sold to Medicaid Plans, Not to States
opportunities.thesis: From 1 January 2027, 44 states plus DC must condition Medicaid expansion eligibility on documenting 80 hours a month of qualifying activity, re-verified at least every six months, and a June 2026 CMS interim final rule sharply limits self-attestation. States must check payroll and encounter data before asking the enrollee — but this population is gig workers, home health aides, seasonal and cash-wage workers whose hours are largely invisible to payroll databases. The move is to skip the 18-month state RFP cycle entirely and sell hours-capture and exemption-evidence directly to the managed care organizations and provider systems that lose money on every disenrollment. Budget line is MCO member retention and administrative spend, plus hospital uncompensated-care avoidance.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The topic is politically radioactive, which keeps founders away, and the obvious go-to-market is structurally closed — CBPP's own vendor-landscape analysis notes RFP cycles are typically too long to meet the January 2027 deadline. So the entire conversation has stayed policy-analytic (KFF, CBPP, Georgetown CCF trackers) rather than commercial, and searches surface state procurement pages and policy trackers instead of a product. The party with the most immediate, quantified P&L exposure — the managed care plans — is the party nobody is selling to.
opportunities.why_now: Hard federal effective date of 1 January 2027, with states needing to send enrollee notices no later than 31 August 2026 and system logic ready for testing in late 2026 — meaning the operational scramble is happening this quarter. The June 2026 CMS interim final rule limits self-attestation for verifying activities or exclusions to 2027. Molina Healthcare's CEO has publicly guided to Medicaid membership contraction of roughly 565,000 to 715,000 people before work requirements and six-month redeterminations even begin, and CBO's estimate of coverage loss under the law runs to millions by 2034. The verification burden recurs every six months, permanently, across roughly two dozen million expansion adults, and the same design is spreading to SNAP.
opportunities.buildable_today: A three-person team with consumer-product and benefits-eligibility experience. In 90 days: ship an hours-and-exemption capture flow — SMS and lightweight app, photo capture of a schedule or paystub, OAuth connections to the major rideshare, delivery and staffing platforms, school enrollment and caregiver attestation forms — that outputs a state-acceptable evidence packet in the format one target state accepts. Sell it to two or three MCOs in that single state as a retention pilot priced against avoided member churn; the plans already hold member contact data and have a quantified reason to pay before the first six-month re-verification cycle in mid-2027.

opportunities.name: Funded-Claim Detection for Casualty Reserving
opportunities.thesis: Third-party litigation funding is the largest unmodeled driver of casualty reserve development, and until 2026 insurers had no way to tell whether a given claim was funded. New state registration statutes just created the raw material. The product is a claim-scoring data utility that fuses the newly public funder registries with docket data, UCC-1 filings, plaintiff-firm network graphs and medical-lien patterns to flag probable funder involvement at first notice of loss, months before it shows up as adverse development. Buyer is P&C carrier and reinsurer claims and actuarial reserving leadership; budget line is claims analytics and reserving, plus the outside counsel spend it directly reduces. The moat is entity resolution through shell layers, which compounds as more states adopt registration.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The clearest proof nobody has productized this: Law.com had to file an open records request with the Georgia Department of Banking and Finance in July 2026 to assemble a dataset of who owns Georgia's registered litigation funders. A journalist doing FOIA to build the list means no commercial data provider had it. Verisk and peers publish social-inflation thought leadership and general claims analytics, but the specific, hard work of resolving funder identity through shell layers and linking it to individual open claims is not being done. It is unglamorous, legally sensitive, and demands patience with state registry plumbing — three filters that keep founders out.
opportunities.why_now: The registries only became populated in 2026. Georgia's regime commenced 1 January 2026, requiring litigation financiers to register through NMLS with disclosure of any party holding 5% or more of voting shares; West Virginia requires registration with the Secretary of State; and a wave of states including Arizona, Colorado, Kansas, Montana, Oklahoma and Tennessee added disclosure and control provisions in 2025. Senator Grassley's Litigation Funding Transparency Act of 2026 (S.3826) would extend disclosure to class actions, MDLs and large coordinated federal proceedings. EY projects TPLF could add as much as $50B in costs to US insurers over five years, a 4-5% annual loss ratio effect — so the prize scales with the dataset that only started existing this year.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two people: one data engineer, one with casualty claims or reinsurance underwriting background. In 90 days: scrape and normalize the Georgia NMLS registrations and West Virginia Secretary of State filings, resolve beneficial ownership and attorney affiliations, and cross-join to PACER and state docket data plus UCC-1 filings naming those funders as secured parties. Ship it first as a paid quarterly intelligence report — the list of funders, their owners, their affiliated firms and their visible case footprint — to a handful of casualty reinsurers and excess carriers, who will buy a list long before they will buy an API. Productize as real-time claim scoring once two or three of them are renewing.
source_lenses: Revealed enterprise demand — what large organizations are actively trying to buy or staff for, where no good vendor exists

opportunities.name: Muon tomography sold per-tendon: seeing grout voids inside post-tensioned bridge ducts
opportunities.thesis: Grouted, metal-ducted post-tensioning tendons are the one bridge component the entire NDT toolkit publicly cannot inspect — the steel duct blocks wave-based methods, and FHWA's own review of 11 NDE technologies documents that no method reliably finds grout voids, strand position, and strand corrosion together. Cosmic-ray muon scattering tomography passes through steel and concrete indifferently and is now buildable from catalog extruded scintillator and SiPM readout for a few tens of thousands of dollars in parts. The business is an inspection service, not an instrument company: clamp two tracker planes around a suspect anchorage or segment, dwell 12-72 hours, deliver a density map and a void/corrosion call. Price per tendon to state DOTs, toll authorities, and the engineering firms doing their in-depth inspections.
opportunities.why_overlooked: Commercial muography has concentrated on nuclear (dry-storage casks, waste drums, decommissioning), volcanology, and archaeology, plus a small Japanese civil-inspection effort. The civil-structures literature includes review papers and a 2020 first-principles proof of concept on a reinforced concrete block, but the search surfaced no company positioned specifically on post-tensioned tendons — the single asset class where the incumbent method is officially admitted to fail. Note the evidence provenance: the scouting session was blocked from fetching pages, so all quotes are search-snippet level and the competitive scan is a negative result from search, not a verified market map.
opportunities.why_now: The dated triggers that exist are publication triggers, not regulatory ones, and should be read that way. FHWA-HRT-22-090 (published 2022) is the written admission that 11 reviewed NDE technologies leave the void/strand-location/corrosion problem unsolved; a 2025 Structural Concrete review (10.1002/suco.202400591) restates that 'there is currently no direct method for assessing corrosion in these tendons'; and 2025 work presented at NDT-CE is explicitly framed as 'Muon tomography — ready for practical application?', with a May 2025 arXiv preprint (2505.04821) publishing usable trajectory reconstruction. A claimed IAEA muon-imaging applications guide dated September 2025 appeared at search level only and is UNVERIFIED — do not put it in a deck before confirming it. There is no regulatory effective date forcing adoption; the demand-side clock is the 1980s-2000s US PT inventory aging into the grout-void corrosion window plus IIJA-era inspection budgets.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two people, 90 days, roughly $30-60k of parts. Build two 1 m x 1 m tracker planes from extruded scintillator bars with SiPM readout, a laptop coincidence DAQ, and the published scattering-density reconstruction seeded from the µTRec preprint. Then manufacture your own sales artifact: pour a concrete test block containing a metal duct with deliberately placed voids and pre-corroded strand, have a third party record the ground truth, image it blind, and publish the result. First customer is not a bridge owner but a state DOT research office or a university transportation center that funds NDE validation — a blind-test result on a mock-up is exactly what unlocks that contract, and the first real bridge follows from it.
source_lenses: The academic-to-commercial gap: 2024-2026 findings in unfashionable fields (metrology, tribology/corrosion, industrial chemistry, soil/ag science, acoustics, structural biology of non-human organisms, ceramics, NDT) that are replicated and de-risked but unclaimed by any startup.

opportunities.name: Azole-resistance hotspot mapping and compost protocol certification for green-waste operators
opportunities.thesis: Pan-azole-resistant Aspergillus fumigatus is manufactured in decomposing plant, wood, and flower-bulb waste treated with agricultural azoles — the TR34/L98H and TR46/Y121F/T289A tandem-repeat mutations are selected there and then arrive in hospitals via air, which is why azole-naive patients present with resistant infections. In 2025 five EU agencies jointly named agricultural and wood waste storage and management as a control point. Nobody sells the control. The business is two products stacked: a paid hotspot surveillance service (sample, culture on azole-supplemented agar, sequence cyp51A, map) sold to composters, biomass yards, bulb growers, and to hospitals and insurers who want to know their catchment risk; and a certified treatment protocol (turning regime, thermophilic hold time, covering) that a site operator can be audited against.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The problem sits in the seam between three industries that do not share regulators, customers, or conferences: agrochemicals, waste management, and hospital infection control. No single party carries the liability, so no party buys the fix. The mycology literature has mapped the hotspots for a decade — the Emerging Infectious Diseases study of Danish hot spots and resistance-associated application practices covers 2020-2023 — and yet the entire response today is national advisory guidance in a couple of member states. The scouting search returned zero commercial actors. Caveat on provenance: page fetching was blocked that session, so 'zero commercial actors' is a negative search result, not a verified competitive scan.
opportunities.why_now: The dated trigger is the 2025 EFSA multi-agency assessment (10.2903/j.efsa.2025.9200), the first time the EU treated environmental azole resistance as a cross-sector regulatory matter, with ECDC, ECHA, EEA, and EMA co-signing and with explicit recommendations on 'proper agricultural and wood waste storage and management' and on approval/renewal of azole fungicides. Be honest about what that is: a formulated recommendation, not a binding rule with an effective date. There is no compliance deadline to sell against yet. The bet is the normal 2-4 year lag from a joint EU scientific opinion to member-state obligations, which puts mandatory hotspot management for large composters plausibly in the 2028-2031 window, and the WHO fungal-priority framing plus resistant-aspergillosis mortality is what makes hospitals willing to pay for catchment data before any rule exists.
opportunities.buildable_today: One mycologist plus one field tech. In 90 days, sample 40 green-waste, wood-chip, and bulb-waste sites in a single country (the Netherlands, Denmark, or Ireland — small, dense, and already sensitized), culture on azole-supplemented agar, sequence cyp51A for TR34/L98H and TR46/Y121F/T289A, and publish the national hotspot map. The map is simultaneously the paper, the press event, and the lead list — every operator on it now has a named problem and a phone call coming. First paying customer is a large green-waste operator or a bulb-growing cooperative buying a pilot: a baseline survey of their sites plus a controlled trial of one cheap intervention at three of them. That trial output becomes the certifiable protocol you sell repeatedly.
source_lenses: The academic-to-commercial gap: 2024-2026 findings in unfashionable fields (metrology, tribology/corrosion, industrial chemistry, soil/ag science, acoustics, structural biology of non-human organisms, ceramics, NDT) that are replicated and de-risked but unclaimed by any startup.

opportunities.name: Municipal land-use decisions as a B2B feed for developers and site selectors
opportunities.thesis: Hyperlocal news died because a human had to sit through a four-hour planning commission meeting in each of ~19,000 US municipalities, funded by local display ads that never covered it. EveryBlock, Outside.in, and Patch all failed on that arithmetic, and the failure was misread as 'nobody cares about local news.' Speech recognition plus long-context models take the marginal cost of covering a meeting to near zero. The correction is to change the customer, not the product: sell structured land-use, zoning, permit, and procurement decisions per seat to developers, energy and data-center site selectors, contractors, and lobbyists, who value a single approval at hundreds of millions and will pay for it. The compounding asset is the continuously indexed archive of every municipal meeting, which nobody can rebuild retroactively.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The category's failure signature is strong enough to repel founders outright, and the recent entrants are overwhelmingly philanthropy-funded newsroom projects chasing reader subscriptions — reproducing the exact monetization mistake that killed the for-profit generation. B2B political intelligence is a proven model in adjacent tiers (federal lobbying, state legislative tracking, construction bid data) but the municipal tier remains a data desert because the source material is unstructured video scattered across hundreds of separate Granicus, Swagit, YouTube, and Zoom endpoints. Important caveat carried from the scout: competitive density was NOT verified. Before acting, check specifically whether any venture-backed company is already doing municipal land-use intelligence.
opportunities.why_now: There is no dated or numeric trigger in this group's raw material — the only two evidence URLs are a startup-postmortem roundup and the EveryBlock Wikipedia entry, and every claimed unlock is flagged unverified model knowledge. Stated plainly: this opportunity currently rests on three unconfirmed assertions, each of which is a cheap one-day check and each of which is load-bearing. (1) Transcription cost per audio-hour has fallen by orders of magnitude — verify against current ASR list prices. (2) A large majority of US municipalities now stream and archive public meetings by default, versus almost none in 2013 — verify against a vendor deployment count (Granicus/Swagit customer lists) or a municipal-clerk association survey. (3) Data-center and energy siting has raised the stakes of municipal land-use decisions — verify with a count of 2025-2026 data-center rezoning applications in one target metro. Do not pitch this until at least (2) has a number attached.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two people, one metro with high development velocity (Columbus, Phoenix, Northern Virginia, or the Dallas exurbs). In 90 days: scrape and transcribe every municipal meeting, agenda packet, and set of minutes for every jurisdiction in that metro; extract land-use, permit, and procurement decisions into a structured weekly digest with parcel-level references. Hand-build a list of 200 local developers, site selectors, and construction and utility firms and charge per seat from the first issue. The historical trap is a free reader product — do not ship one, and do not take philanthropic money that requires open access. The ingestion pipeline is identical in the second metro, so first-metro revenue funds expansion.

opportunities.name: Auracast retrofits sold to venues as assistive-listening compliance, not to consumers as earbuds
opportunities.thesis: Doppler Labs built genuinely good hearing-augmentation hardware and died in 2017 against three constraints: Bluetooth could not do low-latency multi-device broadcast, battery life was inadequate, and there was no regulatory route to sell hearing enhancement without a hearing-aid license. All three are gone — Bluetooth LE Audio and Auracast solved broadcast and latency, the FDA's over-the-counter hearing aid category opened the regulatory path, and mainstream earbuds shipping hearing-aid features normalized the behavior. The move is to flip the customer entirely: sell to venues that carry assistive-listening obligations and currently discharge them with 1990s infrared emitters and induction loops. You are an integrator — survey, size, install, commission, provide the venue-branded receiver app and QR onboarding, and hand the facilities manager a compliance document.
opportunities.why_overlooked: Hearables as a consumer category is considered settled, and no investor wants another earbud company — a correct verdict that is simply irrelevant to a business selling transmitters and commissioning to stadiums, theaters, houses of worship, airports, transit systems, lecture halls, and gyms. The buyer is an accessibility or facilities manager, a channel with essentially no startup presence; the incumbents are small AV hardware firms with no software capability. Three things were explicitly NOT verified and should be checked in order: whether ADA technical standards have been updated to reference or accept Auracast (this is the load-bearing question — check it first), current Auracast deployment rates in venues, and the size of the assistive-listening retrofit market.
opportunities.why_now: The dated triggers are real but carried from model knowledge and flagged for confirmation: the FDA's OTC hearing aid rule took effect in October 2022; Apple received clearance for a hearing-aid feature on AirPods Pro in 2024; Bluetooth LE Audio and Auracast shipped broadly across Android phones and earbuds through 2023-2025. Confirm each against the FDA and Bluetooth SIG pages before quoting them. The arithmetic that follows is the actual why-now: as receiver penetration in the general population crosses a majority around 2027-2028, venue-side broadcast becomes the cheapest way to satisfy an assistive-listening obligation and the installed base of infrared and loop systems becomes stranded capital on a normal 2029-2031 replacement cycle. Note what is missing: there is no confirmed regulatory effective date requiring Auracast, and if ADA standards never reference it, this is a cost-savings sale rather than a compliance sale.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two people with AV field experience, no hardware development — Auracast transmitters are commodity. In 90 days, productize the survey-to-commissioning workflow for one venue class and do ten installs: houses of worship and municipal council chambers first, because they have small budgets, fast single-decision-maker procurement, existing accessibility obligations, and there are thousands of them within driving distance. Deliverable per site is the transmitter install, coverage map, QR onboarding signage, and a written compliance memo the facilities manager can file. The software layer that turns this from a services shop into a product — channel management, multi-language streams, usage analytics proving the accommodation was used — gets built out of the first ten deployments.

opportunities.name: O&M for the orphaned residential solar fleet: inverter swaps and monitoring reinstatement
opportunities.thesis: US residential solar has experienced a mass extinction of the companies that sold and financed it, while the hardware they installed stays on roofs for another two decades. Millions of homeowners now hold panels under warranties from dissolved entities, monitoring portals going dark, inverters aging out, and lease or PPA contracts assigned through bankruptcy to servicers with no field presence. The business that died was customer acquisition for new installations — subsidy-dependent with catastrophic CAC. The business that is alive and unowned is O&M, warranty adjudication, monitoring reinstatement, and repowering, with near-zero acquisition cost because every customer is already named in public interconnection, permit, and UCC records.
opportunities.why_overlooked: Residential solar is the most reputationally damaged sector in climate tech; investors will not open a deck with 'solar' in it and founders have migrated to storage and grid software. That blanket avoidance is the moat, because this business is not exposed to what killed the sector — it sells no new systems and depends on no tax credit. It also reads as a boring services roll-up rather than a venture business, which suppresses competition further. Two risks were explicitly NOT verified and are serious: how much of this the surviving national servicers and O&M firms already cover, and whether truck-roll economics work at single-home scale. Test the second one on your own first fifty jobs before raising anything.
opportunities.why_now: The dated triggers here are strong if they hold, and all come from model knowledge needing independent confirmation: SunPower filed Chapter 11 in August 2024; Sunnova and Solar Mosaic filed for bankruptcy in 2025; and the federal residential clean energy credit under Section 25D was terminated for expenditures after 31 December 2025 by 2025 tax legislation. Verify each in the docket and the statute text before relying on it — the 25D termination date is the single most important number in this thesis, because it is what structurally impairs new-sales competition. Independent of policy, the mechanical clock is inverter service life of roughly 10-15 years against panel life of 25+, applied to several million US systems accumulated over fifteen years, which puts the replacement wave squarely in 2029-2031 no matter what Congress does next.
opportunities.buildable_today: Start regional, start with public records. In 90 days, assemble a fleet database for one or two counties where a now-failed installer had density: interconnection applications, permit records, and UCC filings together give you address, vintage, equipment make, and often the bankrupt originator. Then sell exactly one product at a flat published price — inverter replacement plus monitoring reinstatement — via direct mail and door-knocking in that county. No menu, no assessments, no subscription in v1. The software leverage (fleet database, vintage-and-make failure model, predictive outreach) accrues while you do the work, and it is what eventually makes the company acquirable by a utility, a servicer, or an asset owner holding orphaned lease paper.

opportunities.name: The agent-incident loss database that makes agent E&O underwritable
opportunities.thesis: Tamper-evident agent audit logging has already commoditized itself: five independent libraries built in 2026, all pitching hash-chained EU AI Act Article 12 decision trails, all with zero stars. Supply mass-produced itself because everyone reasoned to the same artifact, and none of it is worth anything without a counterparty who accepts the log as evidence. The scarce asset is the loss database — a rigorous incident taxonomy plus frequency and severity data that lets an underwriter actually price agent-error coverage. Build the registry, give away the SDK that normalizes traces into claims-grade records, keep the aggregate, and partner with one MGA or specialty carrier to co-develop rating factors. The insurer you enable becomes the acceptor that retroactively gives everyone else's logs value.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The zero-star repos are unusually legible evidence of misallocated effort: agenttrace, sealvera-js, sealvera-python, incident-ledger, and memtrail were each created between March and July 2026, independently, describing near-identical hash-chained tamper-evident audit trails against the same regulations, and not one attracted a single user. Everyone built the issuance side; nobody asked who reads the log. Meanwhile the acceptance side — an institution that will take the proof and pay out against it — has no builder at all. Provenance note: this scout ran entirely against GitHub as a primary source because all other hosts were blocked, so the repo and star telemetry is directly observed while the insurance-market gap is inferred rather than confirmed with carriers.
opportunities.why_now: The trigger is a measured shift with dates attached: five separate tamper-evident agent-audit libraries created between March and July 2026, each at zero stars — supply saturation with demonstrably zero demand, observed directly from repo telemetry. Alongside that, Google's AP2 agentic-payments work writes the 'agent acts, someone later adjudicates' pattern into a payments standard, and its FAQ states plainly that 'due to their non-deterministic processes, even well-behaving Agents need to have their behavior tightly constrained above what a normal authorization model would require of human users.' EU AI Act Article 12 record-keeping obligations are already generating the raw telemetry these logs capture. The compounding argument is the strongest part: loss data accrues only with calendar time and cannot be bought later, so a 2026 start is structurally worth more than a 2028 start, and by 2029-2031 the incumbent in agent errors-and-omissions will be whoever holds five years of classified incidents.

Second, ship a thin open-source SDK that normalizes traces from the common agent frameworks into that schema, and get it adopted by giving it away and doing the integration PRs yourself into the frameworks. First customer is not an AI company: it is one MGA or specialty carrier who will co-develop rating factors with you in exchange for early access to the aggregate. Seed the registry by hand-classifying publicly reported agent failures so it is non-empty on day one.

That is a technical gap, not a philosophical one, and a small team can close it: card and bank-level blocking that includes brokerage MCCs and named platform merchants, DNS/app-level containment, a family financial-containment service, and a paid structured recovery program. The incumbent blocking tools (Gamban and GamStop-style services) inherited a UK gambling-merchant taxonomy that predates event contracts, so their coverage lists miss the new platforms by construction — a user who self-excludes is still fully able to fund and trade. Nobody owns the intersection of brokerage-aware transaction blocking and family-facing recovery. opportunities.name: Ingestion firewall for government-cleared e-invoices (hostile XML on national tax rails)
opportunities.thesis: Clearance-model e-invoicing mandates force every business in a country to ingest structured XML authored by arbitrary counterparties, delivered through a government API that validates schema but not content — so the tax authority effectively launders attacker-controlled strings into a channel the receiving ERP treats as trusted. The business is a drop-in sidecar that sits between the national API and the customer's ERP: canonicalize and Unicode/homoglyph-normalize inbound documents, quarantine injection patterns, enforce entity-expansion and size limits (XXE, billion-laughs), flag semantic anomalies the state schema permits but the ERP cannot handle (blank line-item sets, collapsed whitespace in invoice numbers), and preserve the byte-exact original for legal audit. Sell it first as an open-source validator against Poland's published FA(3)/KSeF schemas to win the integrator community, then monetize the hosted quarantine console, alerting, and per-country schema packs. Second revenue line: fuzzing-as-a-service against each national schema, sold to ERP vendors and e-invoicing service providers who now have a statutory obligation to accept whatever the state hands them.
opportunities.why_overlooked: The receiving side of these mandates has no product category yet. In Poland's own Ministry of Finance schema repo (CIRFMF/ksef-schematy), issue #3 is titled 'Serio? Apostrofy w P2?' — an integrator who hit a PRODUCTION purchase invoice with quote characters in the invoice-number field and asked, in public, whether SQL injection can traverse KSeF; it has 10 comments and remained open as of 2026-08-02. Issue #30 documents that XSD token inheritance silently collapses repeated spaces, so the invoice number KSeF returns no longer matches the issuer's and ERP document matching breaks. Issue #31 (22 comments) shows the submission API accepting invoices with zero line items despite line items being a required element. These are integrators reporting data-integrity and security defects to a tax authority because there is nowhere else to take them — no vendor, no scanner, no library. GitHub repo searches for e-invoice validation tooling return roughly 0-2 results per mandate country. The gap is structural: the security industry does not read tax-authority schema repos, and the tax-compliance industry (Avalara, Sovos, Pagero, Comarch, Storecove, local PACs/ASPs/GSPs) sells transmission and legal validity, not threat models. Honest caveat carried from the scout: those incumbents' receive-side security features were NOT diligenced — the scouting session had no open web access — so competitive overlap is the first thing to check before building.
opportunities.why_now: Dated triggers, all from the source material and verified on GitHub on 2026-08-02: the three defect reports above are stamped 2026-02-12 (#31), 2026-04-02 (#3) and 2026-04-28 (#30) — i.e. the first national cohort of receivers is discovering this right now, as KSeF 2.0 ramps from zero to full production volume in 2026. The same receive-side exposure lands on published schedules elsewhere: Nigeria FIRS/NRS (UBL 2.1) for large taxpayers from 1 Nov 2025, Malaysia MyInvois Phase 4 from Jan 2026, Costa Rica all taxpayers from 1 Sep 2025. The structural timing argument is that receive-side tooling runs roughly 18-24 months behind send-side tooling in every mandate, so the pain surfaces now and repeats country by country. What is explicitly NOT verified: there is no confirmed public incident of an ERP compromised via a cleared e-invoice, and no market sizing or funding-landscape check was possible — treat the 'first breach makes this board-level' claim as a hypothesis, not a trigger.
opportunities.buildable_today: Days 1-30: ship an MIT-licensed Python/Java validator against Poland's public FA(3) schema that takes a raw KSeF XML payload and returns (a) a canonicalized document, (b) a structured findings list — quote/backslash/control characters in identifier fields, homoglyph and bidi-override runs, whitespace collapse divergence between submitted and returned invoice numbers, DOCTYPE/external-entity presence, expansion ratio, missing line items — and (c) the untouched original bytes plus a hash for audit. Days 31-60: publish a corpus of ~200 adversarial-but-schema-valid FA(3) invoices as a public test suite and run it against every open-source KSeF client, then send each maintainer their results; that report is the marketing. Days 61-90: wrap it in a hosted quarantine console — inbound documents held, findings shown, one-click release to ERP, webhook out — priced per receiving entity. First customers are the named Polish integrators and ERP partners already self-identifying in the CIRFMF issue threads (they are publicly complaining about exactly this and are pre-qualified design partners), plus mid-market Polish firms receiving four-figure monthly invoice volumes into Comarch/enova365/Symfonia stacks. Two people can do this because the schemas, official test environments, and reference clients are all published openly by the Ministry of Finance.
source_lenses: Non-US/EU markets and leapfrog dynamics (2025-2027 global wave of clearance-model tax mandates: Poland KSeF, Saudi ZATCA, Malaysia MyInvois, Nigeria FIRS/NRS, Kenya eTIMS, Bolivia SIAT, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Pakistan FBR, Indonesia Coretax)

opportunities.name: Master-Lease Operator for Empty Congregation Space
opportunities.thesis: US congregations hold the largest stock of already-built, already-permitted community space in the country — fellowship halls, commercial kitchens, gyms, childcare-licensed rooms — sitting idle roughly six days a week, in buildings whose congregations are shrinking but not closing. The business is not buying these buildings; it is operating them. Sign standardized master use agreements with 10-30 congregations in a single metro, take over insurance, keys, scheduling, cleaning and licensing, and fill weekday hours with paying programs: licensed childcare and after-school, senior day programs, supper clubs, coworking. Revenue share with the congregation, gross margin on the programming, and a portfolio of space that no single operator could assemble on the open market.

One pole treats congregational decline as a culture story with no commercial implication. The other pole is adaptive reuse into housing under the 'Yes In God's Backyard' laws — a slow, capital-intensive developer game requiring entitlement, financing and years. The light-capital OPERATING layer between them has no branded player: congregations rent ad hoc to whoever calls, at below-market rates, with no standard agreement, no insurance wrapper and no sales function. Meanwhile the well-capitalized loneliness and third-place startups are building matching apps and dinner clubs with no space of their own — they are demand for this business, not competition. Beyond that, be plain: the supporting claims are unverified. The scout flagged the 'Pew 2025 religious affiliation plateau' explicitly as [unverified], and the claim that municipal social-infrastructure/loneliness funding has become a budget line item is asserted with no dated source. There is no verified numeric trigger here — no measured vacancy rate, no dated funding program. Verify SB 4's effective date and copycat-state adoption count before capitalizing anything on this.
opportunities.buildable_today: Two founders, one metro, zero code. Days 1-30: retain a broker to build a liability/COI wrapper that lets a third party program someone else's sanctuary building, and draft one 3-page master use agreement with a 70/30 revenue split. Days 30-60: sign five congregations, selecting only for buildings that already hold a childcare-licensed room or a commercial kitchen — those two assets carry the permits that take everyone else 18 months to get. Days 60-90: do not invent your own programming first. Sublet weekday hours to operators who are already turning customers away for lack of licensed space — a childcare center with a waitlist, a senior day program, a caterer needing commissary hours.
