opportunities.name: Clinician-Supervised Off-Hormonal-Birth-Control Transition Program
opportunities.thesis: A large cohort of women is quitting hormonal contraception on the strength of online discourse rather than clinical advice, and then managing the fallout alone. The clinical system's only answer is 'get back on it,' so nobody owns the transition itself: rebound acne, cycle irregularity, unmasked PMDD, and — the part that actually terrifies users — a contraception plan that works. Sell a paid 6-12 month managed program: baseline labs, a written dermatology protocol through a partner prescriber, cycle-tracking hardware, coaching, and an accountable non-hormonal contraceptive path with real efficacy counseling. Charge $1,200-2,500 for the arc, because the failure mode the customer is buying insurance against costs vastly more than that.
opportunities.why_overlooked: Femtech capital went to employer fertility benefits, IVF and menopause — categories with an employer payer. Cycle-tracking apps monetize the tracking layer and have no clinical delivery arm, no labs, no prescriber. And the OB/GYN establishment is in an openly adversarial posture toward this trend, which is the structural guarantee that incumbents will not build the product: a clinic whose position is 'this decision is a mistake' cannot sell a service that helps you execute it well. The result is that a medically consequential transition is being coached entirely by influencers with no labs, no liability and no follow-up.
opportunities.why_now: Be plain: the raw material contains no verified dated or numeric trigger for the current shift. The scout flagged the prescription-decline and survey data as [unverified specifics] and had zero live web access. The two firmly dated facts available are older enabling conditions, not fresh triggers: FDA clearance of Natural Cycles as digital contraception in 2018 (which made a non-hormonal path defensible rather than fringe) and Dobbs in June 2022 (which made contraceptive failure far costlier for the user, and therefore made a paid, accountable service viable where a free app is not). Before funding this, verify the actual direction and magnitude of hormonal contraceptive prescription volume 2022-2026 — that number is the whole thesis and nobody in this chain has checked it.
opportunities.buildable_today: Three people: one nurse practitioner or MD with multi-state licensure through a telehealth partner, one operator, one content lead. Days 1-30: write the protocol — a fixed lab panel (androgens, thyroid, ferritin, DHEA-S), a stepped derm pathway, and a documented contraceptive-efficacy consent flow. Use an existing lab partner and an existing FDA-cleared app; build nothing. Days 30-60: sign a distribution deal with ONE creator already giving this advice away free — revenue share, not ad spend. Days 60-90: run a single paid cohort of 25-40 women through a 12-week onboarding at $900-1,500, group calls plus async clinician review. First customer is the creator's audience, and the cohort is simultaneously the product test and the outcomes dataset you will need to sell the 12-month version.

opportunities.name: In-Person Work-Sample Assessment Days for One Role Family
opportunities.thesis: AI collapsed the signal in resumes, take-home assignments and remote interviews simultaneously, and the rational employer response is not better cheating detection — it is putting candidates in a room for a day. Nobody runs that as a service. Build the operations company that hosts proctored, same-day, in-person work-sample assessments for specific role families across a growing set of metros, scored against rubrics written with practitioners. Employers pay per seat to see verified work; candidates pay a small fee to own a portable result they can send to any employer, which is what turns a services business into a credential with network effects.

The incumbents with physical testing footprints (Pearson VUE, Prometric) run standardized knowledge exams under a model built for licensure, not open-ended work samples, and have no incentive to rebuild their scoring apparatus for a fragmented employer market.
opportunities.why_now: Be plain: this group has no verified dated or numeric trigger. The scout had zero live web access and flagged the key number — 'roughly 25 states adopted skills-based hiring policies removing degree requirements' — explicitly as [unverified count]. The mechanism claim (remote technical assessment cheating normalized across 2024-2026, hiring managers openly discounting take-homes) is asserted from the scout's own knowledge with no dated source behind it. opportunities.name: Graded, Warrantied Refurbished Film Cameras — the CarMax of Analog
opportunities.thesis: Film photography, vinyl and instant film have grown for roughly a decade on a durable authenticity and status shift, but the binding constraint is now supply chain, not demand: film-camera repair technicians are retiring without replacements, used body prices have multiplied, and mail-in labs run backlogged. Build the branded refurbished-camera business — buy dormant bodies at near-scrap through estate and bulk channels, service them to a published condition grade, sell DTC with a real 12-month warranty. Attach rentals for the try-before-buy segment and a develop-and-scan subscription once volume justifies the chemistry. The moat is trained repair labor and consistent grading, neither of which an eBay seller can produce.

opportunities.why_now: Be plain: the raw material contains no verified dated or numeric trigger. The strongest claims — that the Gen Z film cohort is now roughly a decade deep, that on the order of a hundred million dormant film bodies sit in closets, and that tariffs raised new-camera prices and widened the refurb spread — are all reasoned from the scout's own knowledge with no dated source and no live verification. opportunities.thesis: A growing set of states added a Medicaid doula benefit across 2022-2026, creating statutory demand and a real payer for thousands of independent doulas — who then discover they cannot enroll as a Medicaid provider, cannot get credentialed, cannot submit a clean claim, and therefore do not get paid. The whole category looks like a rounding error until you notice Medicaid finances roughly 40% of US births, which makes aggregate claim volume large even at small ticket sizes. opportunities.name: Scoped Credential Broker for National E-Invoicing Systems (KSeF first)
opportunities.thesis: In clearance-model tax regimes, the certificate that authenticates you to the national invoicing system grants full owner rights over the taxpayer entity — issue invoices, grant permissions to other people, mint further tokens and certificates. There is no read-only. Any SaaS vendor or accounting bureau serving many clients therefore stores owner-level private keys for hundreds of companies with no technical way to scope them down, and the taxpayer has no way to see or revoke what a vendor did in their name. Build the credential broker that sits underneath: HSM/KMS-backed custody that mints narrow, short-lived, per-capability sessions and returns a tamper-evident audit log per taxpayer. This is the IAM layer beneath tax compliance, not another compliance product.
opportunities.why_overlooked: Verified on 2026-08-02 through primary sources: Poland's Ministry of Finance API repository carries an open issue (CIRFMF/ksef-api #838, filed 2026-07-21) from an integrator who tested the flow and got back a token containing per: ["Owner"], and the Ministry has no answer for it. The reporter states plainly that leaking the certificate file gives a third party full owner permissions over the entity, and that the taxpayer has no technical means to limit what an application does on their behalf — they can only trust the vendor's declaration. Tooling searches confirm the vacuum: 'UAE e-invoicing ASP Peppol' returns 0 repos, 'ZATCA einvoice' returns 17 (all invoice generators, zero credential management), 'FIRS Nigeria e-invoicing MBS' returns 1. Every vendor is racing to build invoice senders. Nobody is building the permission substrate, because the category is filed under 'tax compliance' and security founders never look there.
opportunities.why_now: Dated and verified: Poland's KSeF 2.0 is in production now — the Ministry posted a live deployment schedule in issue #837 reading '21.07.2026 - TEST, 23.07.2026 - DEMO, 28.07.2026 - PRD', and integrators report hitting real production invoices. Issue #838 (2026-07-21) additionally references the Ministry signalling that KSeF tokens will be maintained past '31 grudnia 2026', which means the token-versus-certificate architecture is being settled in the open right now, in a public issue tracker, with no vendor solution in the field. The same certificate-equals-total-control pattern is being copied into every new clearance mandate (Saudi ZATCA, Malaysia MyInvois, Nigeria FIRS, UAE), so a broker proven in Poland ports outward. [UNVERIFIED] The claim that the EU's ViDA program makes this EU-wide by 2029 needs confirmation, as does all market sizing and the incumbent landscape (Avalara, Sovos, Pagero, Storecove, Comarch and local GSPs/PACs/ASPs are real and must be diligenced).
opportunities.buildable_today: A stateless signing proxy, Poland-only, three people. The customer uploads their national certificate once into a KMS; the proxy performs the XAdES authentication and hands back a session token scoped to a single capability (e.g. InvoiceRead) with a short TTL, plus a per-taxpayer tamper-evident log of every call made in their name. The official Ministry clients are open source (CIRFMF/ksef-client-csharp, ksef-client-java), so wrap them directly rather than reimplementing the protocol — that alone compresses the build to weeks. Sell to Polish accounting bureaus (biura rachunkowe), each of which currently holds owner-level certificates for hundreds of client companies and carries the entire concentrated breach risk personally; three signed bureaus inside 90 days is a real business and an unarguable reference story. Land-and-expand into the ISVs those bureaus depend on.
source_lenses: Non-US/EU markets and leapfrog dynamics — the 2025-2027 global wave of clearance-model tax and payment mandates (Poland KSeF, Saudi ZATCA, Malaysia MyInvois, Nigeria FIRS/NRS, Kenya eTIMS, Bolivia SIAT, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Pakistan FBR, Indonesia Coretax) forcing SMBs onto machine-to-machine government rails with almost no independent tooling layer

opportunities.name: Negative Test Corpora for Regulated Data Formats
opportunities.thesis: Every candidate above shares a hidden dependency: to prove an implementation is correct you need a corpus of documents that are wrong in exactly one specified way. Standards bodies ship happy-path examples and prose; almost none ship a maintained, versioned suite of deliberately-broken artifacts keyed to each rule. stateful-hash-signature-key-state-custod.kill_risk: NSA has signaled it anticipates permitting stateless ML-DSA for firmware signing in future CNSA 2.0 guidance; if that lands, the catastrophic-state-management problem the entire company exists to solve simply stops being mandatory, and the narrow NSS/DIB buyer base means there is no adjacent market large enough to absorb the pivot.

copper-retirement-life-safety-circuits.crowding_check: METHOD CAVEAT: this is the candidate I could verify LEAST — GitHub is silent on it and no live commercial search was possible, so treat the overlooked score as provisional. Merged from two candidates that share only a macro headline — a forensics CLI and a regional refurb warehouse are different companies.

eu-data-act-cloud-exit.crowding_check: Same tooling caveat; this one is services/GRC so GitHub tells us nothing. Regulatory facts are the best-verified of the six: Data Act 2023/2854 in force 11 Jan 2024, applicable 12 Sep 2025; Art.29 switching-charge ban from 12 Jan 2027 with the 2024-2027 transitional cost-based regime; Art.30 functional equivalence for IaaS; Art.25 30-day transition window. eu-data-act-cloud-exit.kill_risk: The why_now already fired two years ago and the obligation points at the wrong buyer. AWS, Google and Azure all zeroed egress-on-exit in 2024 in direct anticipation of this regulation, so the legislated price of leaving is largely already zero and 12 Jan 2027 is symbolic — the scout's central claim that the price goes to zero on that date is the thesis's load-bearing beam and it is wrong. Worse, Arts.29/30 obligate the PROVIDER to enable switching, not the customer to prove it can leave, so the compliance budget sits with cloud vendors while the product is aimed at buyers. The provider-side remediation is contract drafting plus a bulk export endpoint — a one-time EUR 15-40k engagement that law firms already own the relationship for and that the vendor's own engineers ship in a sprint. No annuity, and a published clause library is a moat you are giving away as marketing.

material-assistance-cost-ratio-attestati.crowding_check: WebSearch unavailable; GitHub returned 0 repos for FEOC/MACR, which is meaningless for a tax-SaaS market. Meanwhile MACR is a documentation workflow Crux or Empact ships as a feature, and Treasury publishes the safe-harbor cost tables, so there is no proprietary data to defend.

ntn-satellite-asset-telemetry.crowding_check: LIVE SEARCH UNAVAILABLE (see above), but the 'two GitHub repositories therefore a vacuum' argument is self-refuting — satellite IoT is a telco-and-hardware market with no reason to have a GitHub footprint, so the instrument measures nothing and the candidate has mistaken an empty developer ecosystem for an empty market. peppol-access-points-global-south.crowding_check: Live GitHub CONFIRMS the open-source AP supply is thin — 13 hits, only OxalisCommunity/oxalis (150 stars) and phax/phoss-ap (42) plus massivex/hyperway (15) are real; the rest are toys. grid-equipment-slot-forward-exchange.crowding_check: The adjacent PHYSICAL secondary market is crowded, but forward SLOT trading appears genuinely empty. Confirmed physical-equipment competitors: Anza Exchange (exchange.anzarenewables.com — explicitly a B2B marketplace to buy/sell NEW power transformers and HV breakers, plus a separate Anza transformer procurement service), Transformer Exchange Inc, Utility Surplus Exchange, Electrical Trader, Surplus Record, MegaGrid Supply, Mission Critical Facilities International, CIRKLA. Nasdaq's power derivatives are energy, not equipment. Also verified: 'Capacity allocation occurs through prepayments, where buyers wire money upfront to hold a slot in the queue' (chargeduppro/Build.inc) and OEMs are booked 3-4 years out (GE Vernova, Hitachi Energy, Mitsubishi Electric), so the underlying asset is real. why_now checks out precisely: FERC issued FPA §206 show cause orders to all six RTOs/ISOs on 18 June 2026 in the RM26-4 proceeding, defining large loads as >50MW on >69kV lines, with 60-day responses due 17 Aug 2026 (McGuireWoods, Bracewell, Baker Botts, White & Case, Day Pitney, Troutman all confirm). Lead times verified: LPT averaging 128 weeks, GSU 144 weeks, up to 4 years in constrained segments (pv-magazine USA, 11 May 2026).
grid-equipment-slot-forward-exchange.kill_risk: The whole business runs through the OEM's consent. Standard supply agreements carry anti-assignment/anti-delegation clauses and non-refundable staged deposits; once an OEM learns a slot is worth more than the contract price it has every incentive to cancel, keep the deposit and re-sell at market itself rather than let a broker capture the spread. Warranty assignability is separately restricted. Second risk: the phantom-demand premise is contested — SemiAnalysis published 'Stop Saying Half of 2026 US Datacenter Capacity Is Canceled' rebutting exactly the cancellation statistic this thesis rests on, and if hyperscaler demand holds, orphaned slots never accumulate and there is nothing to clear. Third: Anza already runs a new-equipment exchange plus a procurement desk and is one product decision away from listing undelivered slots. Evidence quality is also weak — six of the ten cited URLs are x.com posts.

signed-agent-request-transparency-audit.crowding_check: Not empty — the two halves of this product each already have shipping vendors, several of them very large. Violation detection: Cloudflare AI Crawl Control (GA August 2025, originally branded 'AI Audit') already ships per-crawler verification, a Robots.txt tab that names the crawler, operator, violated path, specific directive and violation count, Web Bot Auth signed-agent verification, and Pay Per Crawl; Microsoft Clarity added robots.txt violation flagging inside Bot Analytics with trendlines and per-operator filtering. Commercial publisher-side monitors: TollBit (documented AI firms circumventing robots.txt; used by Skift and Digital Trends), ScalePost (reports whether bots respect robots.txt), ProRata.ai (Bill Gross, publicly asserting near-universal robots.txt violation), HUMAN (400+ ML models, routing unlisted bots to TollBit's paywall), Fastly, Sphere AI, Created by Humans, Miso.ai — Brookings counts 'more than a dozen' intermediaries. Forensic/court-grade web capture is a separate existing category: Page Vault, TrueScreen, GetProofAnchor all sell FRE 901-defensible timestamped captures and explicitly market against Wayback's weaknesses. Verifier side has many open-source entrants already: cloudflare/web-bot-auth examples, OpenBotAuth reverse proxy (published Docker image), vestauth, Stytch/FingerprintJS IsAgent, ngx_bot_verifier, Anubis/samesame, Apache module, Guzzle middleware. Only the exact combination — an RFC 6962-style append-only log of origin-verified request digests diffed against cryptographically timestamped per-URL preference snapshots — has no commercial vendor; the closest is academic (the Aegon paper's CT-style Merkle ledger for content licensing).
signed-agent-request-transparency-audit.kill_risk: The candidate itself concedes there is no statutory forcing date — the triggers are draft status and GitHub stars, the weakest why_now in the batch. draft-ietf-aipref-attach is real and verifies (rev -04, 28 Apr 2026, Standards Track, updates RFC 9309, Illyes/Thomson, Aug 2026 IESG milestone), but the companion vocabulary draft still carries a no-consensus note, so the thing being audited is not yet fixed. Worse, adoption of the authentication half is negligible: reporting on Pay Per Crawl notes only two small companies have implemented Web Bot Auth, so there is almost nothing to log. Cloudflare sits at the vantage point, owns the signed-agent handshake, already logs violations, and can ship the tamper-evident log as a checkbox. Meanwhile the market is visibly routing around litigation evidence toward licensing (News Corp $250M, Reddit $60M/yr, $1.5-3B 2025 licensing spend, Anthropic's $1.5B settlement), and courts are already extracting evidence directly via discovery (Judge Stein's Jan 2026 order for OpenAI's 20M-log sample) — which is a cheaper substitute for the forensic report. Buyer set (rightsholder collectives, licensing litigators) is small, slow and project-based.

broker-carrier-credentialing-passport.crowding_check: Crowded, and crowded specifically by things that shipped in the six months after the ruling. Both halves of the proposed product already exist: (1) carrier-side credential — Highway has already launched a carrier-facing product giving 'carriers the same level of insight that brokers have had for years,' and became exclusive reseller of Bluewire's Broker Package on 7 July 2026; NMFTA's SCAC Verified turned the SCAC into an identity-assured, carrier-paid credential with ID verification required at application/renewal from 26 Feb 2026; Verified Carrier launched Verified Pickup (driver-level verification) in April 2026; Carrier Assure sells carrier-facing performance ratings. (2) The 'defensible-selection evidence package' named as the wedge back to brokers — Descartes shipped AuditLog for MyCarrierPortal on 23 June 2026, and Cipher & Row publishes a 2026 comparison of carrier-vetting audit trails across TMS platforms, Highway and Descartes. Existing vetting incumbents named in the thesis all verify as real and funded: Highway (Dallas, founded 2022, Jordan Graft), RMIS (Transportation API), Descartes MyCarrierPortal, Truckstop Carrier Monitoring, Carrier411.
broker-carrier-credentialing-passport.kill_risk: The dated triggers are the strongest in this batch and both verify exactly — Montgomery v. Caribe Transport II, LLC, No. 24-1238, decided 9-0 on 14 May 2026, holding negligent-hiring claims against brokers fall within the FAAAA safety exception (supremecourt.gov opinion, Justia 608 U.S. ___, Crowell, Gordon Rees, Adams and Reese); FMCSA non-domiciled CDL final rule effective 16 March 2026 with ~194,000 holders affected (FR 2026-02965, 13 Feb 2026; FMCSA FAQ page). The kill is competitive, not factual: the incumbents own the denial-cause dataset by construction — Highway and RMIS see every denial across every broker, a $99/mo aggregator sees only its own subscribers' complaints — so the stated data moat inverts. Distribution is also adversarial: the value depends on brokers honoring a credential issued by a vendor whose explicit pitch is that brokers' vetting is wrong. Revenue base is 600k price-sensitive, high-churn micro-carriers; and the non-domiciled CDL rule shrinks that base rather than growing it. FMCSA's March 2026 proportionate-percentile SMS overhaul also directly reduces the small-carrier score volatility that generates the pain.

regulated-gas-recovery-and-reclaim-ledge.crowding_check: The claim 'no VC-backed company is visible' and 'there is no branded, contractor-facing collection network' is simply false — this is a mature industry with a public company in it. Refrigerant leg: Hudson Technologies (NASDAQ: HDSN) runs a named Refrigerant Buyback program, ships Cylinder QuickScan QR tracking (i.e. the cylinder-level ledger), does on-site recovery and system conversions, and acquired reclaimer Refrigerants Inc in December 2025 explicitly to expand access to field technicians and grow recovered volume — that is the exact roll-up thesis, already executing. American Refrigerants markets contractor buyback programs framed around the AIM Act by name. Golden Refrigerant and Tradewater are additional aggregators. SF6 leg: the mass-balance ledger has at least three shipping vendors — DILO Direct-Track (cloud, cylinder-to-switchgear, barcode scanning, automated compliance reporting with audit trails), EMT/Trakref SF6 Gas Management Software, and Concorde's ConcordeTrak. Recovery services: In-Gas Direct (recycling, disposal, reconditioning), Concorde Specialty Gases, Hitachi Power Solutions SF6 Gas Recovery Service, Schneider EcoFit Recover, RB Switchgear end-of-life services, Romu Keinänen (Finland), SF6 Relations, plus OEM service arms at ABB and Siemens. Nothing described here is unbuilt.
regulated-gas-recovery-and-reclaim-ledge.kill_risk: Every date verifies — EU Reg 2024/573 bans SF6 in new MV switchgear ≤24kV from 1 Jan 2026, 52-145kV from 2028, 24-52kV from 2030, >145kV from 2032, general prohibition 2035; AIM Act cuts HFC allowances to 30% of baseline in 2029; recovery/reclaim/destruction by certified personnel is compulsory under the F-gas regime. The triggers are real and the opportunity is still dead, because the incumbents were built on exactly those dates and have processing plants, AHRI-700 certification, offtake contracts and cylinder fleets. A two-person entrant is a price-taking subcontractor to Hudson or A-Gas, not a consolidator: working capital is cylinders and gas inventory, the certification is a licence anyone can obtain rather than a moat, and the ledger software you would build after ten jobs is already given away by the cart manufacturer (DILO) to lock in equipment sales. Secondary risk: recovered-gas economics depend on the HFC price spread holding, and reclaimed product not counting against allowances draws exactly the well-capitalized competition already present.

customs-bond-sufficiency-mga.crowding_check: The core premise — 'customs brokers do not underwrite, sureties do not build software, so neither builds the product' — is contradicted by the first page of results. Trade Risk Guaranty is a customs surety agency that already ships the exact product: bond sufficiency reports, entry history, unliquidated entries, claims analysis, a proprietary Importer Score, online bond sufficiency and liquidation checking 'in minutes,' and it receives data directly from CBP on every bond it holds — a data feed better than the ACE/ABI pull proposed here, obtained by being the bondholder. TRG also publishes the FY2025 insufficiency analysis this candidate cites as its own discovery. Other direct competitors: Roanoke Group (US Customs Continuous Import Bond Calculator, major customs surety), Avalon Risk Management, Merlin (purpose-built surety technology for customs brokers, incl. Merlin Information Exchange for bond renewals), eBond platforms that issue bonds and analyze client activity and sufficiency while interfacing directly with ACE, Expeditors (bond saturation guidance to clients), GingerControl (free bond/FTZ/duty calculators), Star USA (June 2026 webinar on preparing for changing bond requirements), Diaz Trade Law (insufficiency advisory). Automated email notification of bond insufficiency is described as an existing feature of customs bond management systems.
customs-bond-sufficiency-mga.kill_risk: The numeric why_now verifies exactly — 27,479 insufficiencies worth almost $3.6B in FY2025, highest count and value ever, roughly double 2019 (Sourcing Journal/WWD, capwolf); CNBC's 12 Feb 2026 piece puts the shortfall at $3.5B; CBP collected $200B in tariffs 20 Jan–15 Dec 2025. But the candidate's own evidence list includes a 6 Feb 2026 CNBC article on the Supreme Court tariff case and refunds, which is the kill: if the IEEPA-based tariffs are struck and duties refunded, prior-year duty liability collapses, bonds become over-sized rather than insufficient, and the entire monitoring product loses its reason to exist within one bond cycle. Even absent that, the practical barrier is ACE/ABI data access — you need filer status or per-importer portal delegation for each of the 50 targets, which is slow, unglamorous plumbing that TRG and Roanoke get for free as bondholders. The MGA endgame needs capital, a surety carrier partner and a multi-year loss history before any underwriting edge is bankable, which is well outside the stated two-person, no-balance-sheet frame.

ai-exclusion-gap-insurance-layer.crowding_check: The most crowded candidate in the batch. Policy parsing and coverage-gap diffing is a settled product category with multiple shipping vendors: Patra PolicyCheckingAI (patent-pending, first-to-market, self-service tier launched 2024 for brokerages of all sizes, claims 85% time reduction), InsurGrid (2026 expansion — extracts data from any carrier PDF and generates side-by-side comparisons in under 60 seconds), Coverages.ai (analyzes/compares/explains policies in plain English, specifically surfacing limits, exclusions and endorsements in a comparison table), InsureScope (clause-by-clause review, up to five policies at once, risk-prioritized briefs with page-level citations), LEGALFLY (policy wording and endorsement comparison for insurance legal/compliance teams), Indico Data, Gradient AI. Adjacent underwriting AI: Federato, Kalepa Copilot, Sixfold, FurtherAI. On the AI-exclusion content itself, the 'nobody is arming the brokers' claim fails on inspection: Aon, Gallagher and Lockton have all publicly flagged the implications for corporate clients, Gallagher published an explainer on CG 40 47, and there are already public AI-exclusion checklists and trackers (aipolicydesk.com, rmstudygroup, Testudo's glossary entry for CG 40 47, The Intelligence Council's ISO/Chubb/Berkshire/Travelers coverage). The affirmative-market side you would route to is likewise built out: Armilla, Testudo, Munich Re, HSB AI Liability Insurance (March 2026).
ai-exclusion-gap-insurance-layer.kill_risk: The facts verify — ISO CG 40 47 (broad, Coverage A and B), CG 40 48 (narrow, Coverage B only) and CG 35 08 (products/completed ops) took effect January 2026, and AIG, WR Berkley, Great American, Berkshire Hathaway, Chubb and Travelers have filed or won approval for their own wordings. That is precisely the problem: a dated, universally-reported, non-proprietary regulatory event is the worst possible foundation for an information moat. The claimed moat — a corpus of carrier AI exclusion wordings — is not proprietary at all: ISO forms are published by Verisk and carrier deviations are filed publicly through SERFF and state DOI systems, so the corpus is a scraping exercise any of the seven incumbents above can run in a week. This is a content update to an existing feature, not a company. It is also a self-extinguishing window: because commercial policies renew annually, the whole book passes through diagnosis by end-2027 and the wording set stabilizes into known market practice, so by the 2029-31 horizon the diagnosis product has no job. Buyer is the retail brokerage, historically the hardest and cheapest software buyer in insurance, and the plan gives the product away free.

cui-determination-for-machine-shops.crowding_check: Exact wedge (parse DoD distribution statements B-F / DFARS 7012 flow-down / export-control markings out of PDFs and CAD title blocks, emit a written CUI-vs-FCI determination + marking overlay + shop-floor label) was NOT found as a product across four differently-worded searches.
