cui-determination-for-machine-shops.kill_risk: why_now verified and holds: 48 CFR CMMC final rule published in the Federal Register 10 Sep 2025, Phase 1 effective 10 Nov 2025, DFARS 252.204-7021 now in new solicitations, Phase 2 third-party Level 2 ramp from ~Nov 2026. Real risks are commercial, not factual. (1) Channel conflict: CUI scoping is the most-billed hour in a consultancy's engagement — a tool that automates it cannibalizes the reseller's own revenue, so 'they will resell it' is the weakest link in the thesis. (2) Liability: a shop will not accept an automated CUI determination without a human attestation, so the product degrades into a workpaper generator with consultant sign-off, compressing price. (3) One-time purchase shape — scoping happens at engagement start, not monthly, so recurring revenue is unproven. (4) Microsoft Purview is already paid-for in every GCC High seat and is the path of least resistance for the MSP channel. (5) Small ACV against a long tail of 30-person shops facing $20k-$100k total compliance cost, most of which goes to the enclave, not to determination.

neris-fire-data-quality.crowding_check: Space is thoroughly occupied. NERIS-compatible RMS vendors already shipped and are competing on exactly this: First Due (live nationwide 1 Jan 2026, and its Data & Analytics product plus 'Accurate Occupancy Records' article covers the pre-plan/occupancy inventory the candidate calls ownerless), ESO (NERIS-compatible since Feb 2025), ImageTrend, FirePrograms (20,000+ records uploaded, fully released nationwide), EPR Fireworks (dedicated NERIS module plus fire-service BI tooling), Station Boss, Fire Rescue Systems, Emergency Reporting, Lexipol. USFA itself posts NERIS compliance reports monthly for free and NERIS ships its own analytics dashboard, so a 'free NERIS Report Card' competes with the regulator's own free output. Grant side is equally mature: First Responder Grants, Firehouse Grants ($110M placed), MissionCIT, Fire Apparatus Consultants, and 5AlarmData — which already publishes an AFG narrative guide built around citing NERIS incident data, i.e. the exact 'AFG narrative generator' pitch. State fire marshals (FL, IL, NE, TX, MI, NC, NJ, MA) are publishing free NERIS onboarding material, closing the intended distribution channel.
neris-fire-data-quality.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is false. FEMA's own published FAQ states NERIS/NFIRS reporting is NOT required to apply for or be awarded an AFG grant; the obligation attaches only post-award, and recipients unable to report at award get 24 months to establish capacity and then must report for 12 months. So 'AFG eligibility loss from data-quality shortcomings' — the entire product framing — is not a real mechanism, and no source ties field-level NERIS completeness to AFG scoring or eligibility. Market arithmetic also fails: FY25 AFG was $291.6M across 1,678 awards (applications closed 22 Jun 2026), so per-department expected value is far too small to underwrite. The 30,000-department TAM is overwhelmingly unpaid volunteer departments with no IT staff and no budget — the candidate says so itself, then prices at $100-300/month. The NFIRS sunset facts (2025 edits closed 31 Jan 2026, retirement Feb 2026) do check out, but a real trigger pointed at a non-existent pain is still a cut. Occupancy/pre-plan inventory 'has no owner' is directly contradicted by First Due's shipping product.

condo-project-eligibility-remediation.crowding_check: The core mechanism has already been dissolved by Fannie Mae itself. Fannie Mae now operates the free Condo Status Finder (condostatus.fanniemae.com), explicitly built for HOAs, management companies and authorized advisors to check in real time whether Fannie Mae is aware of conditions rendering their project ineligible — that is the candidate's product, shipped by the counterparty, for free. Fannie Mae also mandates its free Condo Project Manager (CPM) for lender Full Review certification. On the services side: Katzman Chandler launched CondoBlacklist.com as an informational resource explicitly covering removal options; Allcock Marcus (MA) and KSN publish blacklist resource pages; Florida and Massachusetts firms formed a joint effort on the blacklist. Remediation delivery is a mature licensed-professional market: Association Reserves, Reserve Advisors, Miller Dodson, teamUES, Building Mavens, FPAT and PropFusion all sell SIRS/reserve studies and milestone-inspection compliance in Florida, and SIRS work is statutorily reserved to licensed engineers, architects or RS/PRA-credentialed analysts. Insurance rebuild is owned by commercial brokers.
condo-project-eligibility-remediation.kill_risk: The candidate's own why_now concedes there is no published effective date for the unlock — and the '2026 transparency' catalyst it hedges on has now shipped as the Condo Status Finder, which destroys rather than creates the opportunity: the stated arbitrage was 'because the list is secret there is no market signal, and therefore no product.' Numbers are also off: the blacklist was reported at 5,175 named projects as of 11 Mar 2025, not the ~1,700 national figure cited, so the candidate is working from stale secondary press. Structurally, the assessment is free (candidate's own plan) and the paid work — reserve studies, structural engineering, insurance placement — requires licensure the founding team will not hold, making this a referral-fee coordination layer sitting between well-established engineering and legal incumbents. No compounding data asset: Fannie Mae owns the eligibility ledger and now publishes status directly to the same buyer.

micropollutant-epr-billback.crowding_check: Thinner than the rest of this batch, but not empty, and the nearest competitor is the exact artifact. PwC has already built an EPR cost calculation tool commissioned by the cosmetics and pharmaceutical industries — that is the fee simulator, funded by the obligated population itself, before a startup arrives. Specialist regulatory consultancies are already selling UWWTD positioning: CEHTRA ('Revision of the UWWTD 2024: A Paradigm Shift for the Pharmaceutical Sector'), Ithos Global (dedicated UWWTD cosmetics compliance page), Ramboll, Arche. Legal advisory is saturated — Hogan Lovells, Baker McKenzie, Covington/Inside EU Life Sciences, Crowell & Moring, McCann FitzGerald, Stentors, LexisNexis guidance — and law firms will own the provisioning-opinion sale to CFOs. Adjacent EPR platforms are one product decision away: Lorax EPI (200+ schemes, enterprise), Sphera (chemical/product compliance + regulatory content), Ecoveritas (runs on Lorax ENVI), plus the whole packaging-EPR vendor directory. Trade bodies EFPIA, AESGP, Medicines for Europe and Cosmetics Europe are running coordinated data work that will likely become the sector reference methodology.
micropollutant-epr-billback.kill_risk: The why_now is materially out of date and omits the decisive event. It argues the Feb 2026 General Court dismissal 'removed the it-might-be-annulled excuse' and that a 12-18 month window exists to become the reference calculation before formulas harden. But on 18 June 2026 the European Parliament passed a resolution backing a temporary 'stop the clock' suspension of the UWWTD EPR provisions and financial obligations, and demanding a fresh Commission impact assessment by end-2026 to re-verify quaternary treatment costs and re-identify which sectors are actually responsible — i.e. the mass-times-hazard methodology is being actively reopened, not hardening. IPHA is separately pushing a CJEU preliminary reference through the Irish High Court, and EFPIA/Cosmetics Europe/AESGP/Medicines for Europe took a joint stop-the-clock demand to the Competitiveness Council on 25 Feb 2026. The Feb 18 2026 orders were inadmissibility rulings on standing, not a merits validation — the candidate overreads them. Legally the dates hold (in force 1 Jan 2025, transposition 31 Jul 2027, EPR from 31 Dec 2028, 80% cost share), but political suspension risk through 2027 is high and it is precisely the period the business needs. Buildability is also overstated: per-country medicines volume is IQVIA-licensed proprietary data, not something a 1-3 person team ingests in 90 days, and EMA ERA dossier endpoints are not available in structured machine-readable form. The 90-day plan is honestly a consulting report, not a wedge.

drinking-water-materials-positive-list.crowding_check: The two specific assets claimed to have no owner both already exist. (1) Fit4DW (fit4dw.com) is a live raw materials database for drinking-water products, launched jointly by DVGW CERT, figawa and Kiwa, holding verified formulation data on raw and semi-finished materials, evaluating a formulation once to avoid repeat testing and cutting certification time by 6-9 months — that is precisely the 'accreting supplier composition data no test house or consultancy has in structured form' the candidate calls its defensible asset. (2) Kiwa launched an EU Positive List Consortium (reported June 2026) to fund and coordinate substance retention/addition dossiers — the 'queue management for substance-addition applications' the candidate says nobody does; the consortium exists because ~600 of the 2,042 EUPL substances expire 31 Dec 2028. Machine-readable/searchable EUPL already published: ECHA's own European Positive Lists portal, plus ChemRadar's searchable/downloadable EU Positive List tool (live Jan 2026). Gap-analysis and portfolio-review consulting is a full field: Arche Consulting (dedicated DWD service line), Penman Consulting, FOBIG, Charles River, Linmark, NSF (published 'New Compliance Map for Water-Contact Products' whitepaper), UL Solutions, Eurofins. Kiwa is also the second European conformity assessment body with DWD accreditation, i.e. it holds the regulatory accreditation the candidate identifies as the moat.
drinking-water-materials-positive-list.kill_risk: why_now is the most factually solid in the batch and is not the problem: 2024/367 and 2024/368 apply from 31 Dec 2026 (~5 months out), legacy national-scheme products deferred to 31 Dec 2032, certification for new products can start Jan 2027 and takes 12+ months, renewal applications for near-term expiries due by July 2027. All verified. The candidate dies on overlooked, not on timing. The claimed white space — machine-readable conformance tool, supplier-declaration collection, substance-addition queue — is occupied by ECHA, ChemRadar and Fit4DW/Kiwa respectively. Worse, the moat is structurally unavailable: the binding constraint is conformity-assessment and lab capacity, and only accredited bodies (Kiwa, DVGW, NSF, UL, Eurofins) can issue what customers actually need, so a software pre-screener sits upstream of gatekeepers who are already building the same database and can bundle it into certification for free. A EUR 15-50k portfolio review is a consulting engagement competing head-on with FOBIG, Arche and Penman, who have the toxicology staff and the ECHA relationships.

small-business-wind-down-desk.crowding_check: Adjacent lanes are well funded but all aim elsewhere; the specific motion — harvesting business brokers' rejected and expired listings and re-homing the customer book, license/permit, crew and equipment for a success fee — was not found in any search. Nearest funded players and why they miss: SimpleClosure ($20M+ total, $15M Series A May 2025 led by TTV, plus Carta/Anthemis/LegalTech Fund) automates dissolution paperwork and investor distributions for venture-backed startups, not Main Street asset re-homing. Teamshares ($245M raised, 85+ businesses in 30+ states, $490M consolidated revenue) explicitly markets against '70% of small businesses lack buyers' but only acquires businesses that are profitable and sellable — it is the direct competitor for the good listings and a non-competitor for the reject pile. Common Trust ($2.6M seed, Crossbeam/Schmidt Futures) and Project Equity do employee-ownership buyouts, again for viable companies. Restructuring/wind-down firms J.S. Held, Ravix Group, Arkus Advisory, VLPC, Bizcap, Aevitium, Cornerstone Licensing all serve distressed mid-market at $6.5k-13k+ managed-wind-down pricing, not micro-business value recovery. Book-of-business brokerage is mature but only in high-value verticals (insurance agencies, dental, accounting, routes) via BizBuySell, Sunbelt, Benchmark, BayState, with Live Oak Bank financing purchases. Business-broker economics genuinely do exclude the reject pile, and no one found is farming it.
small-business-wind-down-desk.kill_risk: why_now is the best-verified in this batch: McKinsey Institute for Economic Mobility (Feb 2026, covered by Forbes/HousingWire/ATR) puts 6M US SMBs into ownership transfer by 2035 with ~1M sold at ~$5T cumulative, >50% of owners already 55+, ~92% of exits ending in closure rather than sale, ~5% of exiting owners completing a sale, and annual exits up to 42% above 2011 levels (~665k/yr) by 2035. The candidate's ~30% and 6.46% close-rate figures are shakier secondary snippets, but the McKinsey spine holds without them. Real risks are economic, not factual. (1) Unit economics: a business with no buyer has near-zero recoverable value by definition — a success fee on a $50-150k customer book is $5-15k, against weeks of bespoke legal, licensing and placement labor, so gross margin per engagement is thin and the sales cycle is emotionally loaded with a distressed, often unresponsive owner. (2) Zero defensibility: broker referral relationships are the only asset, they are per-metro, non-exclusive and replicable, and there is no compounding data — the candidate's own plan defers software until after 10 manual engagements. (3) Supply risk: brokers may not hand over reject lists at all, since a dead listing is still a relationship they may want to re-approach, and privacy/engagement-agreement terms complicate transfer. (4) Ceiling: this is a regional professional-services firm, not a venture-scale outcome, and the 6M/$5T TAM narrative wildly overstates the monetizable slice. Advancing on wedge honesty and buildability, not on size.

contractor-license-qualifier-succession.crowding_check: Not empty — the scout's 'no purpose-built product' claim fails on first contact with search. Three separate layers are already occupied. (1) Qualifier placement as a service: Nationwide Contractor Licensing (apiprocessing.com) sells 'License Qualifier Placement' as a named product line; Licensing Connection matches vetted qualifying agents nationwide and claims 48-hour match times; Contractor Qualifier Connect covers FL/CA/TX/GA/NC with 'over a decade' of operation; QualifyingAgents.com and RMO Agency do the same in CA. (2) Multi-state license compliance software: Harbor Compliance explicitly markets software for 'contractors with complex multi-state footprints' that can 'track qualifier licenses'; Avalara License Management covers 23,000+ US jurisdictions and is built for 100+ license portfolios; Foundation Software sells contractor licensing solutions; Citizenserve on the municipal side. (3) The proposed phase-two apprentice-hour capture is a commodity: GoSprout (apprenticeship compliance + DOL RTI/OJT tracking with state rules engines), ToolGrit (free tracker, 15 trade presets incl. IBEW/UA), SparkShift, ShiftFlow. Even the 'diligence product' wedge already exists as free content marketing: Acquisition Stars publishes 'Contractor License Transfer in Construction M&A: State-by-State Diligence,' and CT Acquisitions' 2026 PE-in-trades guides already state the CA/TX/FL rule that the qualifying individual cannot be transferred and that lining up a qualifier 6-12 months pre-close is the standard mitigation. M&A advisors are giving this away as a lead magnet.
contractor-license-qualifier-succession.kill_risk: The why_now is a dud and the candidate half-admits it. The one verified figure holds (52.3% of US employer-businesses owned by people 55+, per McKinsey/Project Equity), but 'silver tsunami' has been an ambient, heavily-covered SMB theme for a decade — it is a trend, not a trigger, and the candidate itself concedes 'no known effective date or regulatory change driving the timing.' Worse for the thesis: the standard PE playbook has already routed around the problem. The dominant close mechanic is buyer-supplies-the-qualifier from the acquiring platform's existing licensed master, which is described as 'cleanest when the buyer is a PE roll-up' — i.e. the exact buyer this product targets is the one that least needs it. The remaining need is met by human placement agencies at low cost. Also note the 90-day CSLB replacement window: the problem has a well-known, cheap, legally-defined fix, which caps willingness to pay for a rules engine.

standby-fiduciary-for-kinless-elders.crowding_check: The thinnest field in this batch, but not empty and not empty for a flattering reason. Adjacent occupants: SAFE Planners Inc. and Reliance Fiduciary operate as professional fiduciary practices; Fiduciary CMS already sells case-management/court-accounting software to professional fiduciaries (the 'software backbone' the candidate proposes to build from scratch); PFAC is an established trade body running a fiduciary academy; Solo Aging Solutions LLC does patient advocacy for elders; Navigating Solo and Solo Agers Connect are community networks; Aging Life Care Managers / geriatric care managers overlap on the coordination half. On the institutional side the incumbent 'solution' is free or public: hospital ethics consultation services, hospital counsel searching for a willing guardian, community-volunteer surrogate protocols, Texas HHS's legislatively-mandated Surrogate Decision-Making Program, Indiana's 90-day volunteer guardian appointments, and MD/state public guardianship offices. What I could NOT find, across five differently-worded queries, is any venture-funded company productizing hospital-contracted standby fiduciary services on a per-case or retainer basis. That specific wedge genuinely looks unbuilt. Demand-side evidence is solid and academic rather than commercial: Brierley-Bowers et al. quantified medically-unnecessary days awaiting guardianship in a state acute system; ABA Bifocal's 'Hospital to Guardianship Pipeline'; a cited finding of 17 days and 6 attempts on average to find a guardian; AGS 2025 position statement on unrepresented older adults. Awareness is rising fast (NPR ran a solo-agers feature 9 July 2026, citing 17M solo agers), which shortens the window.
standby-fiduciary-for-kinless-elders.kill_risk: The core wedge has a structural conflict-of-interest problem that is already named in the literature the candidate would be citing. Syracuse Law's 'Use and Misuse of Guardianship by Hospitals and Nursing Homes' and ABA Bifocal state directly that when guardians draw significant income from the hospital, their duty to the ward and the court conflicts with the hospital's desire for a swift discharge — and many state laws insist guardianship be a last resort. Selling 'we consent to the SNF placement, the hospital pays us per case' is precisely the arrangement reformers are trying to stamp out, and the 2026 reform wave runs against it: Kansas HB 2359 (effective 1 Jan 2026) and Idaho's UGCOPAA adoption emphasize least-restrictive alternatives, procedural safeguards, and heightened fiduciary accountability; CA AB 586 is live on professional fiduciaries. So the candidate's unverified 'guardianship reform is under legislative pressure' claim does verify — but the direction of that pressure is a headwind for a hospital-paid for-profit surrogate, not a tailwind. Secondary kills: licensure is a months-long gate before revenue (candidate concedes this), the business is per-case services with human-linear costs and no obvious path past low-hundreds-of-millions capture, and the category carries live reputational contamination from documented for-profit guardianship abuse. Every quantitative claim in the candidate remains unsourced — the only attached URL is a BLS employment-projections release that says nothing about kinlessness.

supervised-hours-marketplace.crowding_check: Densely crowded — this is close to a textbook case of a screener's null result. Motivo Health raised a $14M Series A led by Cox Enterprises (SteelSky Ventures, Great Oaks participating), $16.3M total, doing exactly this: matching pre-licensure therapists with clinical supervisors and selling into behavioral health orgs, digital health companies and health plans. TMind AI runs a supervisor marketplace with AI matching, automated hour tracking and HIPAA-compliant sessions across all 50 states. Track Your Hours literally already does the proposed wedge — it 'applies BBS rules and generates forms' for LMFT/LCSW/LPCC. Guidara sells clinical supervision software (hours, agreements, exportable records). Clinical Supervision Tracker (supervisiontracker.org) targets LPC/LMFT/LCSW candidates. Clinical Supervision Now and Firelight Supervision are operating supply-side networks. Therapy Training Collective gives away a free LCSW hours tracker. Every named component of the proposed product — hour logging, board-form export, supervisor recruitment, two-sided marketplace — ships today from a funded or established vendor.
supervised-hours-marketplace.kill_risk: Beyond the crowding, the causal chain in why_now is broken at the joint. The argument is 'AI absorbs junior task volume, so trainees cannot log hours.' The BLS numbers cited are roughly real but slightly off (BLS 2024-34 puts office and administrative support at -3.9%, not the -3.5% quoted) and, more importantly, they describe clerical occupations. LCSW/LPC supervised hours are direct clinical contact hours — face-to-face therapy — which is not the task volume AI is eating. The chosen launch wedge is the one credential where the stated trigger does not apply. The trigger that would apply (appraisal/AXP boards authorizing simulation or practicum alternatives) is flagged unverified by the candidate itself and I found nothing confirming it. Defensibility is also weak: state board form-mapping is public information that six vendors have already replicated, and supervisors multi-home across platforms.

perpetual-records-custody-for-closures.crowding_check: The core wedge — perpetual transcript custody for closed institutions — is the incumbent's existing product. Parchment (Instructure) publishes 'How to Support Your Alumni Transcripts When Your College or University Has to Close' and sells an end-to-end Registrar Service storing and servicing alumni records for closed schools. National Student Clearinghouse maintains a closed-school search and Transcript Ordering Center and is repeatedly named alongside Parchment as the records custodian of record. DiplomaSender services transcripts on behalf of state boards from closed institutions. On top of that, the buyer often pays nothing: states run free or statutory depositories — Maryland and DC operate a centralized hybrid depository, Texas THECB, Alabama ACCS, Missouri DHEWD and CA BPPE all field closed-school transcript requests, and teach-out partners absorb records directly (University at Albany now holds College of Saint Rose records). The adjacent upsells are also taken: Higher Ed Consolidation Solutions is a merger-and-closure consultancy staffed by people who ran the Mount Ida and College of New Rochelle wind-downs, Doug Moore runs a firm specializing in college closures and wind-downs, and The Change Leader sells the same. Student Defense has published the policy paper on securing records when schools fail, so the advocacy channel is already mapped.
perpetual-records-custody-for-closures.kill_risk: The why_now verifies but the market does not. Real: WICHE has US high school graduates peaking in 2025 and falling 13% through 2041 (~576,000 students); Grawe projects ~15% decline in the college-age population 2025-2029; Federal Reserve work cited by Education Next models up to ~80 institutional closures by 2029. So the enrollment cliff is genuine, which is why competitors are already positioned. The economics are the kill: at roughly 20-80 closures a year nationally, mostly small tuition-dependent institutions with terminal cash measured in the low millions and creditors ahead of you in line, a one-time endowment per custody filing gives a tiny absolute TAM — nowhere near multi-billion. Closing institutions are distressed payers, and the free state depository is the reservation price. Also note the candidate's own evidence is empty: the single attached URL is a BLS employment-projections release with no relationship to institutional closure.

shared-certified-water-operator.crowding_check: Not a gap — a mature, consolidated, regulator-blessed industry that has existed since 1980. The shared-operator model is already a formal regulatory category: Pennsylvania DEP defines a circuit rider as 'a management program in which a certified operator may make process control decisions at more than one system of different ownership,' and contract operators are defined as certified operators in responsible charge of three or more public water systems. The National Rural Water Association has run its circuit rider program since 1980; Oregon Health Authority contracts circuit riders for systems under 10,000 population; EPA's own small-system guidance lists 'certified circuit rider' and 'shared operator arrangement' as the standard options. Commercial third-party O&M is a tracked market with a Bluefield Research market report and this competitive set: Veolia North America, Inframark, Jacobs, American Water, Alliance Water Resources, ClearWater Solutions, H2O Innovation, California Water Service Group, US Water Services, PeopleService, Woodard & Curran (90+ clean-water facilities, four new municipal contracts in 2025 alone), Indigo Water Group. The SCADA half is equally taken: High Tide (htt.io, SOC-2, automatic regulatory reporting), eLynx Technologies (explicitly targeting rural water districts), Anexee, AVEVA, GE Vernova, Iconics, Ziptility (publishes the contract-operator agreement template).
shared-certified-water-operator.kill_risk: The candidate concedes it has zero dated or numeric trigger and flags every quantitative claim as unverified — and the only attached URL is a BLS release that does not cover water operators. There is no regulatory change, no deadline, and no price break; the enabling premise ('remote SCADA is now cheap enough') has been true for a decade, which is why the incumbents above already built it. A two-person team entering here competes for low-margin municipal O&M contracts against Veolia and Jacobs while needing a certified operator on payroll from day one, and procurement runs through state primacy agencies and SRF administrators that have decades-long relationships with NRWA affiliates. Nothing about the timing is 2026-specific.

digital-court-record-custody.crowding_check: The load-bearing claim — 'every AI transcription company optimizes word error rate and ignores the certification layer' — is simply false, and it is the claim the whole thesis rests on. AAERT is a decades-old certification body for electronic reporters and transcribers, and its credential is the de facto standard courts require. VIQ Solutions markets security, confidentiality and chain-of-custody explicitly and is a CJIS-Ready organization. Verbit's legal line is built around certified 'Final Transcripts,' not AI drafts. FTR (For The Record) Recording Suite — Reporter/Manager/Player — is described as the industry standard for capture plus 'management, storage, and security' of the judicial record. JAVS (Justice AV Solutions) is a leading global courtroom recording provider and signed a strategic partnership with VIQ in 2023 for end-to-end court documentation. CourtSmart and Voice Products round out the capture hardware field. On the services side: U.S. Legal Support fields AAERT-certified digital reporters, Esquire Deposition Solutions runs a digital reporting practice, Steno is publishing on the shortage. Even the 'durable asset' the candidate names — the state-by-state rules map — is already published for free by SonicClear ('A State by State Analysis of Digital Court Reporting'), and courts publish authorized-transcriber lists (Maricopa County Superior Court under AZ Supreme Court Rule 30; NY Courts' electronic-recording transcription vendor list).
digital-court-record-custody.kill_risk: Ironically this candidate has the strongest verified why_now in the batch and still fails, which is the point. The trigger checks out and then some: stenographer headcount down 21% over the decade to ~23,000 with stenography school enrollment down 74% and nearly half of programs closed (2025 Court Reporting Industry Trends Report); California AB 3013 launched remote court reporting pilots in 13 counties including LA, San Diego and Santa Clara on 1 July 2025 with an extension to 2028 under consideration; AB 1189 expands certified digital court reporters; the California Supreme Court heard argument in June 2026 in Family Violence Appellate Project v. Superior Court of Contra Costa on whether the electronic-recording prohibition is unconstitutional; 2M+ hearings since 1 April 2023 have gone without a verbatim record and CA needs 458 more FTE reporters. That is a genuine, dated, live inflection — which is exactly why FTR, JAVS, VIQ, Verbit and US Legal Support are already standing on it. Additional kills: court procurement is multi-year and incumbent-locked, capture appliances are a hardware business a two-person team will not ship in 90 days at courtroom-integrity standards, and the stenographer lobby is litigating and legislating against the transition state by state (see the CalMatters and Capitol Weekly coverage of the fight), so the regulatory ground under any launch state can move.

superload-route-and-schnabel-brokerage.crowding_check: Not empty. Permit/routing WITH bridge evaluation is a mature software category: Bentley SUPERLOAD, Hexagon Octave SafeHaul (explicitly bundles 'bridge evaluation'), AASHTOWare PermitRoute powered by ProMiles (used by 57% of states), ProMiles PermitManager, Oversize.io. Permit-service firms (Omni Permits, Beardown, FreightMonster 'Superload & Route Survey Planning') sell multi-state superload orchestration today. Route-survey/transport-engineering with clearance envelopes and axle-load modeling is a standard published service line at Kuehne+Nagel project logistics engineering, Rhenus, AIT, Mammoet (published transformer route case studies), Barnhart, Emmert International, HLI Rail and Rigging (Schnabel service). No pure-play 'pre-cleared corridor certificate' product or Schnabel/HMT slot aggregator surfaced across five differently-worded queries — that specific packaging does look unbuilt. why_now VERIFIED: 128-week power transformer and 144-week GSU lead times confirmed against WoodMac Q2 survey reporting; prices +77%/+45% since 2019; turbine slots tight through 2030. Candidate honestly flags this as numeric-not-regulatory.
superload-route-and-schnabel-brokerage.kill_risk: The 'pre-cleared route certificate' has no legal standing — states, not you, issue superload permits, and each state re-runs its own bridge analysis, so the certificate sells confidence rather than a binding entitlement. The claimed moat (pre-computed bridge ratings from public state DOT inventories) is built on open data that AASHTOWare Bridge Rating already normalizes for the agencies that actually decide, so Bentley/Hexagon can extend into the shipper side faster than a two-person firm can accumulate corridors. Schnabel option layer is decorative: ~30 cars in North America means the total revenue pool on that asset is trivial and the owners (rail carriers, Emmert, HLI) will not let a broker sit between them and a utility. Requires a licensed PE stamping load ratings, which caps how fast headcount scales and imports professional liability on $12M cargo.

biosolids-outlet-exchange.crowding_check: No dedicated biosolids outlet exchange, capacity marketplace, or cross-state PFAS-threshold arbitrage broker found across four query framings — that shape genuinely looks unbuilt. BUT the customer is already served by large full-service incumbents delivering the identical outcome (firm per-ton price, compliant destination, documentation): Synagro (largest US biosolids manager, publicly investing in PFAS destruction tech), Denali Water Solutions (PE-backed; the two swapped asset portfolios in Aug 2024), Merrell Bros., US Submergent, Agri-Sludge, Midwest Injection, plus Casella/WM/Veolia on landfill and thermal. Johnson County KS just awarded Denali a 3-year land-application contract at ~$1M/yr with commissioners raising PFAS concerns — i.e. procurement already runs through incumbents. Source-control/pretreatment consulting is covered by Brown and Caldwell, Hazen, CDM Smith, EA Engineering; Bluefield Research covers the market analytically. why_now VERIFIED PRECISELY: Maryland SB 719 signed 28 April 2026, bans land application at or above 50 ppb PFOA/PFOS from 1 October 2028, with a 25-50 ppb restricted tier and a mandatory source-identification/mitigation duty above 25 ppb — the strongest-verified trigger in this batch. Maine/Connecticut bans and EPA's 2026 biosolids PFOA/PFOS draft guidance also corroborate.
biosolids-outlet-exchange.kill_risk: Defensibility is the weak leg: non-exclusive outlet contracts, zero capex, and no proprietary data mean Synagro or Denali can match any quoted per-wet-ton price and bundle the hauling you do not own. The 'knowing which outlet accepts which concentration this quarter' edge is a decaying asset — once state thresholds stabilize (MD's are already written into statute with numbers), the arbitrage compresses. Landfill airspace is the substitution risk in the other direction: Maryland/Maine reporting already flags landfill capacity concerns, so the outlets you forward-contract may themselves be closed to biosolids by state action. Market size is modest — US biosolids management is single-digit billions of total spend and a Mid-Atlantic broker's take rate is a thin slice of that. Working capital risk if you sign firm per-ton prices against outlet costs that reprice.

bridge-power-permit-clock-manager.crowding_check: Crowded on every adjacent surface. Data center air permitting is a active practice line at Trinity Consultants, ALL4 (which also ships Overture, software for managing air permit limits and compliance demonstrations), Encino Environmental, Ramboll, ERM, Montrose. Permit-obligation and compliance-calendar tracking is a saturated software category: Cority, Intelex Permit Management, Enablon, Ecesis compliance calendar. Data center permit/build tracking data products already exist: Hubexo ConstructionWire, BuildCentral, Construction Monitor, Buildermuse running lists, plus Virginia DEQ publishing issued data center air permits directly. Environmental due diligence for data center siting is sold by Transect, Build.inc, BDO, Azura. why_now VERIFIED: NSPS published 15 January 2026 at 91 Fed. Reg. 1910; 24 consecutive months at a single stationary source; clock runs regardless of actual operating hours; if exceeded EPA treats the unit as never having been temporary.
bridge-power-permit-clock-manager.kill_risk: Half the product is foreclosed by the rule itself: the final NSPS explicitly prohibits replacing one temporary turbine with another to circumvent permitting, so the 'rotation/relocation orchestration' upsell is a compliance-evasion service EPA already named and blocked. The 'invisible liability' premise is already falsified — as of mid-2026 at least one Clean Air Act citizen suit has been filed against a data center operator relying on temporary status, and Greenberg Traurig, Clark Hill, Frantz Ward and A&WMA have all published on it, so owners and their counsel are watching the clock without a subscription. Registry construction is harder than stated: temporary units are frequently authorized under general permits or permits-by-rule that never surface as dated records in state databases, so coverage will be incomplete exactly where exposure is highest. Market ceiling is low — a few hundred campuses, a quarterly report, and the moment it works Trinity or ALL4 sells it with real PE credibility and existing owner relationships. Selling niche exposure reports to lenders and insurers who have not asked for them is a long, low-conviction sales cycle.

dot-117r-retrofit-slot-brokerage.crowding_check: Heavily occupied and the scarcity premise is contradicted by the primary sources. AllTranstek (founded 1994, acquired by Bourque Logistics Jan 2025) manages 500,000+ railcars for Fortune 100 shippers, explicitly offers regulatory compliance support that 'sets up programs to track regulatory requirements... a specific body of work that needs to be completed by a certain date,' coordinates shopping events, audits repair activity, and its StencilWatch product covers 16% of the North American tank car fleet — that is the proposed fleet-triage product, already sold at scale. Kaleris Railcar Repair Management System spans 75+ shops and connects owners, lessors and shops, which is the shop-capacity coordination layer. Lessors (GATX, Trinity Industries Leasing, Union Tank Car, Wells Fargo Rail) own both the cars and the leverage. Railbroker, CarTanks and MRC Rail are already publishing 2026 'phase-out: problem or opportunity' marketing. why_now PARTIALLY FALSE: the 1 May 2029 PG II/III date and the ~17,000 remaining cars check out, but the capacity crunch does not — PHMSA states there is sufficient shop capacity to retrofit to 117R and build 117J by 2029, and AAR puts the need at ~27,000 DOT-117s against ~86,000 already produced, with build+retrofit capacity projected at ~8,000/yr in 2028 and 2029.
dot-117r-retrofit-slot-brokerage.kill_risk: The entire thesis is scheduling arbitrage against a shortage that the two authoritative bodies (PHMSA, AAR) say does not exist; at 8,000 cars/yr of 2028-2029 capacity against 17,000 remaining cars, the cliff clears without a broker. Retrofit-versus-replace economics also cut against volume: for the oldest, least economic legacy cars the rational answer is retirement or a lease of a compliant 117J, not a shop slot, so the brokerable pool is a fraction of 17,000. Shops will not sign forward capacity to an uncapitalized two-person intermediary when GATX and Trinity are standing there with fleets and balance sheets, and 'non-binding forward capacity agreements' are worth nothing in a soft market. Slot deposits require real working capital, which the candidate claims not to need. Zero proprietary data — BTS Annual Tank Car Facility Survey and UMLER are available to every incumbent. Terminal event risk: the deadline is a one-time 2029 cliff, so even if it worked the business has no second act.

340b-rebate-covered-entity-side.crowding_check: The core claim ('the vendor landscape is entirely manufacturer-facing... there is nothing to buy') is directly falsified. The Craneware Group hosted a 340B Rebate Forum and publicly confirmed NO NEW VENDOR IS NEEDED for the pilot — its Trisus 340B rebate module integrates with existing Sentinel/Sentrex for automated, compliant rebate submission AND reconciliation. Verity Solutions states it has been 'actively collaborating with Beacon to develop a fully integrated submission solution for both pharmacy and medical claims' so its covered-entity clients are ready. Beacon (Second Sight Solutions, operated with Berkeley Research Group) is the manufacturer-designated submission and rebate-status rail that covered entities log into directly, with 10-day payment benchmarks and real-time claim status built in. Also serving covered entities: Apexus (HRSA Prime Vendor, Vizient), Macro Helix (McKesson), Sentry Data Systems, 340B Complete (Walgreens), Wellpartner (CVS). The candidate's own framing is factually off in a second place: manufacturers in the approved pilot designated Beacon, not Kalderos, as the platform. 3 Axis Advisors has already published cash-flow analysis of the rebate model, and Alchemy Health publishes covered-entity guidance.
340b-rebate-covered-entity-side.kill_risk: why_now is legally fragile and the candidate understates how badly. The D. Me. issued a nationwide preliminary injunction on 29 December 2025 blocking the 1 January 2026 launch, the First Circuit denied the government's stay, and on 10 FEBRUARY 2026 the court VACATED the pilot and remanded to HRSA in AHA v. Kennedy; HHS then scrapped it and ran a fresh RFI. HRSA's re-noticed 1 January 2027 pilot (Federal Register 3 August 2026) is a second attempt at a program the hospital lobby has already killed once in court, with the same plaintiffs, the same statutory-authority argument, and providers still publicly objecting — a binary litigation dependency, not a dated forcing function. Even if it survives, scope is small: ~25 products from 13 manufacturers, roughly 95% of 340B process unchanged, so the software wedge is a narrow module the incumbent TPAs are bundling free into contracts they already hold. The proposed integration targets are the competitors' own split-billing systems, which control the claims data and have no reason to open it. The receivables-financing 'real prize' requires a balance sheet, lending licenses and underwriting against a rebate stream with no payment history and an unsettled dispute process — not a 2-3 person 90-day build.

medicaid-work-hours-verification.crowding_check: Among the most crowded things in US healthcare IT right now. CMS announced that 10 major vendors pledged $600M in discounted and free services for work-requirement implementation: Accenture, Acentra Health, Conduent, GDIT, Deloitte, Gainwell, Maximus, Curam by Merative, Optum and RedMane — with some offering managed care compliance and performance monitoring platforms at NO COST to states through 2028. States get a 90% federal match for system builds, so the money is flowing to that channel, not around it. The specific 90-day build described — OAuth into rideshare/delivery/staffing platforms to produce an evidence packet — is already a shipped product: Argyle runs a dedicated Government Benefits Eligibility Verification line, and Truv's public-sector product explicitly pulls 'payroll providers, employers, gig platforms, disability programs, benefits, military'; Pinwheel, Atomic, Plaid and Equifax Work Number are adjacent. Consent-based verification is already the recommended state design pattern per SHVS. The MCO channel is likewise pre-worked: Avalere Health Advisory and the Managed Care Alliance publish 'How can MCOs Prepare for Medicaid Community Engagement (Work) Requirements,' National Health Law Program published 'How Managed Care Plans Can Help,' and CHCS runs a tech implementation learning series. CBPP's vendor-landscape paper exists precisely because there is a dense vendor landscape.
medicaid-work-hours-verification.kill_risk: Two numeric claims are wrong. '44 states plus DC' is inflated — KFF puts adoption at 41 states including DC (some sources 40 plus DC), so roughly a fifth of the claimed footprint does not exist. The self-attestation claim is also overstated: the 1 June 2026 CMS interim final rule permits self-declaration through JANUARY 2028, generally once per continuous enrollment period — it does not shut it off in 2027, which softens the urgency the thesis rests on. Substantively: the 'skip the state RFP' insight is real but the resulting business has no moat — Argyle and Truv own the payroll and gig connections you would resell, the ten CMS-blessed incumbents own the state channel and are giving MCO-facing compliance tooling away free through 2028, and MCO procurement is not meaningfully faster than state procurement. Evidence-packet formats are per-state and still unsettled in late 2026, so a single-state wedge does not port. Political volatility is a live risk in both directions: enforcement delays (Arkansas already delayed to January 2027) or litigation could stretch the timeline and strand a retention-priced pilot.

funded-claim-detection-for-casualty.crowding_check: Adjacent space is busy but the specific wedge (resolving funder beneficial ownership through state registries and linking it to individual open claims) is not productized by anyone I could find. Real adjacent players: Verisk runs a full TPLF content program (legislative activity map, Jan 2026 transparency insight, 2021 webinar 'Who's Funding the Case?') but sells no claim-level funder-detection product; Findevor launched an AI 'legal system abuse prevention' product for casualty insurers that cross-references plaintiff-firm activity and judicial hotspot maps — closest overlap; CLARA Analytics (CLARA Litigation) predicts attorney involvement and litigation propensity with plaintiff/defense attorney scorecards; Gen Re publishes casualty litigation analytics guidance; Premonition, UniCourt, LexisNexis CourtLink and Docket Alarm supply the docket substrate anyone would build on; Westfleet Advisors publishes the annual funder market report (39 funders identified) but at market level, not claim level; NICB has called for transparency without building a tool. why_now verified and holds: Georgia SB 69 signed 21 Apr 2025 with NMLS litigation-financier registration effective 1 Jan 2026 ($25k threshold, $2,000 fee); S.3826 Litigation Funding Transparency Act of 2026 confirmed introduced by Grassley on 11 Feb 2026 with Tillis, Kennedy, Cornyn, covering class actions/MDL/100+ case aggregations; EY's ~$50B-over-five-years / 4-5.2% loss-ratio-drag figure confirmed in trade press. The Law.com 17 Jul 2026 open-records piece on Georgia's registry is real, supporting the claim that no commercial provider had assembled the list.
funded-claim-detection-for-casualty.kill_risk: The thesis is self-cannibalizing. The same disclosure wave that creates the raw material also destroys the need for detection — Georgia, Kansas, Indiana, Louisiana, Montana, West Virginia and Wisconsin already mandate funder-identity disclosure, ISO has approved a Litigation Funding Disclosure Condition endorsement, and S.3826 would federalize it for class actions and MDLs. If disclosure becomes routine by 2028-2029, insurers get funder identity for free and a paid inference product is worth little. Second, the data-linkage claim is weaker than stated: consumer pre-settlement advances to individual plaintiffs are generally not UCC-1 filed (UCC-1s attach to businesses and law-firm portfolio deals), so the 'cross-join UCC-1 to open claims' mechanic likely resolves only firm-level portfolio funding, not per-claim funding at FNOL. Georgia's registry lists funders and their owners, not which cases they funded — the case linkage is the hard, unsolved part and the 90-day plan quietly assumes it. Third, Verisk or Findevor can bolt this on as a feature the moment it looks valuable; neither lacks the docket data or the carrier relationships.

muography-for-pt-bridge-tendons.crowding_check: The core claim — 'the search surfaced no company positioned specifically on post-tensioned tendons' — is flatly false. GScan (Estonia, CERN spin-out, €3M seed Mar 2024) is doing exactly and only this: its muonFlux system was run on a post-tensioned concrete bridge with UK National Highways, AtkinsRéalis and Jacobs between June 2024 and February 2025, explicitly demonstrating identification of 'the internal mechanics of post-tensioning ducts as well as signs of weakness and deterioration' with 3D visualisation, claiming 10 m penetration at 1 mm accuracy. That project won Product Innovation of the Year at the Digital Construction Awards 2025 and entered a phase three on operational assets completing mid-2026. VSL — one of the largest post-tensioning specialists in the world, i.e. the exact channel — resells GScan muon tomography inside its bridge inspection and SHM service line. Lynkeos Technology (University of Glasgow spin-out, publicly funded, working with Germany's BAM on commercial approval) is field-testing portable muon detectors on a series of Glasgow bridges with Transport Scotland. Muon Solutions markets civil-engineering muography for bridges, tunnels and dams. Decision Sciences International is the incumbent (Los Alamos spin-out). There is also granted US patent 11,692,959 — 'System and method for imaging tendon cross sections for detecting voids and other deficiencies in grouted external tendons.' That is four commercial actors plus IP on the precise application. The FHWA-HRT-22-090 and Structural Concrete 2025 publication triggers are real, but they are exactly what pulled these companies in years ago.
muography-for-pt-bridge-tendons.kill_risk: Direct, funded, credentialed competition with a two-plus year head start and the incumbent PT channel (VSL) already locked up; National Highways is a reference customer a two-person startup cannot match. The 90-day/$30-60k build plan is a fantasy against that — GScan burned €3M and years to get to a phase-three trial, and the binding constraint is not detector parts but dwell time, reconstruction quality and validated blind-test credibility with DOT research offices, which takes years. There is no regulatory effective date forcing adoption (the candidate concedes this), so procurement is slow research-office money. Granted IP on grouted-tendon void imaging is a freedom-to-operate hazard. The candidate's own provenance note admits the competitive scan was an unverified negative search result — and it was wrong.

azole-resistance-hotspot-control.crowding_check: This one genuinely looks empty on the commercial side and the 'zero commercial actors' claim largely survives scrutiny. Everything I found is academic or public-sector: the FUNgalSnelders lab at Wageningen (studies environmental-to-clinical azole resistance transmission and airborne exposure quantification), Radboudumc-CWZ Center of Expertise for Mycology with RIVM Bilthoven, Statens Serum Institut's Mycology Reference Laboratory in Denmark, published environmental hotspot surveys from Belgium (two composting facilities plus horticulture, six pan-azole-resistant isolates), Ohio, Georgia USA (TR46 in 30% of samples incl. compost, hibiscus, hemp), and the Netherlands. The only commercial artifact is VIPcheck, an azole-screening agar plate — a consumable, not a surveillance or certification service. Public programmes are moving into the space and would be the real competitors for any tender: the UK PATH-SAFE programme covers antifungal-resistance molecular epidemiology, DHSC put £12M over five years into fungal research, WHO published a GLASS-FUNGI blueprint on 30 June 2026 (though scoped to Candida bloodstream infections, not environmental), the Fungal One Health AMR Network launched 24 Apr 2025, and the Botucatu Document (Dec 2025) calls for environmental aerobiome surveillance. On the certification side, PAS 100 / the Compost Certification Scheme (audited by bodies like Aardvark) is the incumbent framework a resistance module would have to plug into or displace. why_now verified: the EFSA/ECDC/ECHA/EEA/EMA joint opinion (10.2903/j.efsa.2025.9200) is real, names stockpiled agricultural waste, soil amendment use and freshly cut wood as resistance-selection hotspots, and recommends 'proper agricultural and wood waste storage and management.'
azole-resistance-hotspot-control.kill_risk: There is no buyer and no deadline. The candidate honestly concedes the EFSA output is a recommendation with no effective date, and the 2028-2031 mandatory-management window is pure extrapolation — EU scientific opinions frequently produce nothing binding for a decade or never. Meanwhile the paying customer is structurally absent: green-waste composters and bulb cooperatives run on thin margins and have no liability exposure for a hospital infection three towns away, and hospitals buy infection control inside their own walls, not catchment epidemiology from a private lab. The founding move (publish the national hotspot map, then sell to everyone on it) is antagonistic — you name operators as public health hazards and then invoice them, which is a hard first sale and invites the trade association to fund a rebuttal instead. Publishing the map also destroys the information asymmetry and hands the method to Wageningen, SSI or a national agency who can run it for free with better credibility. Realistic ceiling is a single-country consultancy of a few million euros, not a venture outcome.

local-government-decision-feed-for-buyer.crowding_check: The candidate explicitly asked for this check and the answer kills it. GatherGov is the identical thesis already shipped: a real estate development and zoning intelligence platform that ingests local government meetings across 6,200+ US municipalities (94%+ of US population), transcribes audio, parses permits and zoning records, extracts entitlements, applicants and decision-maker activity into a municipal knowledge graph, and sells to CRE developers, brokers, REITs and investors — down to per-municipality development pipeline pages. It is venture-backed (ComposeVC, OPCO Ventures per SEC Form D; PitchBook profile). Hamlet (myhamlet.com) searches government meeting transcripts across 3,500+ governing bodies with explicit zoning/permit/regulatory tracking. ZoneWire monitors council meetings for zoning keywords for CRE professionals. Cloverleaf AI (Denver, founded 2021, formerly Engaged Citizens) does the same ingestion for govcon sales intent, with Starbridge, GovSpend and Ontopical as its named rivals — Ontopical being a long-established local-government-meeting AI intelligence player. Polco, CivicPlus and Granicus sit on the government side of the same data. That is five-plus companies on the exact wedge and the ingestion pipeline is the commodity layer, not the moat.
local-government-decision-feed-for-buyer.kill_risk: why_now is empty by the candidate's own admission: 'There is no dated or numeric trigger in this group's raw material,' the only two evidence URLs are a CB Insights postmortem roundup and the EveryBlock Wikipedia page, and the three load-bearing claims (ASR cost collapse, municipal streaming penetration, data-center siting stakes) are all flagged unverified. Screening a thesis whose author says do not pitch this until claim (2) has a number attached is straightforward. Worse, the claimed moat — 'the continuously indexed archive nobody can rebuild retroactively' — is already held by GatherGov at 6,200 municipalities, and archives are in fact rebuildable from Granicus/Swagit/YouTube backfill, which is how the incumbents built theirs. Nothing here is overlooked; the correction the candidate proposes (sell B2B, not to readers) was made by the market years ago.

auracast-ada-venue-retrofit.crowding_check: Occupied end to end, including the exact go-to-market. Ampetronic | Listen Technologies (merged; Ampetronic is the legacy hearing-loop incumbent) launched Auri in January 2025 as 'the world's first assistive listening system based on Auracast' — a full stack of transmitters, receivers, manager software, docking stations and accessories, already installed in stadiums, houses of worship, universities, transit stations and theaters, expanded with new products at both ISE 2026 and InfoComm 2026, and backed by a dedicated awareness partnership with consultancy AuraFuturity aimed at exactly the venue/facilities buyer this candidate claims has no startup presence. Williams AV ships a full Auracast assistive-listening product category. On the integration/services layer specifically: Equal Access Audio sells inclusive assistive listening installs to churches, performance venues and public facilities; Complete Hearing Solutions is described in the industry as a specialist assistive-listening integrator doing in-situ commissioning verification. Behind them sits the entire AVIXA-channel integrator base that has installed ADA assistive listening for thirty years. Deployment is already underway (Frankfurt Airport gates A16/A17 trial, Bristol Temple Meads, Stadium Taranaki, Albuquerque), and ABI Research projects 1.5M Auracast public venues by 2029 — the market is real, which is precisely why it is not empty.
auracast-ada-venue-retrofit.kill_risk: The load-bearing question the candidate itself said to check first fails. ADA is deliberately technology-neutral and performance-based: it does not approve or certify specific technologies and contains no Auracast reference, so there is no compliance mandate to sell against. The Bluetooth SIG's own position is that venues 'can meet their ADA obligations using a whole host of technologies,' and the relevant technical standards are not landing until IEC 60118-17 in December 2027 — meaning it is currently too soon to say whether individual Auracast installs meet ADA at all, which is the opposite of a saleable compliance memo. Strip that away and this is a regional AV services shop reselling commodity transmitters at zero gross margin advantage, with no proprietary data, no network effect and no switching cost, competing against the vendor that makes the hardware and is already running the venue-education campaign. The 'software layer' differentiator (channel management, multi-language, usage analytics) is already shipped as Auri Manager software.

orphaned-residential-solar-servicing.crowding_check: The facts are right and the conclusion is backwards — this is one of the most actively consolidated spaces in climate tech right now. Omnidian raised an $87M Series C in April 2025 (led by B Capital, with BNP Paribas, Citi Impact Fund, Marunouchi Innovation Partners, Liberty Mutual Investments, National Grid, Activate Capital), then bought bankrupt Sunnova's residential servicing/O&M platform ServiceCo for $7M in a stalking-horse deal in July 2025, and in February 2026 was contracted by Renewbrook Energy to monitor and maintain the thousands of orphaned PosiGen residential systems Renewbrook acquired out of that bankruptcy. Solaris acquired other Sunnova assets in September 2025 with SunStrong taking over legacy systems. GreenLancer operates a nationwide solar repair network explicitly marketed for orphaned-system warranty takeover; ElectriCare runs a dedicated 'Orphan Solar Help' line; Solar Medix, Infinity Solar USA and Yes Solar Solutions (maintenance plan and portal built to adopt orphaned systems) all target the same homeowner; Solar Insure sells the warranty-wrapper product. Fronius and other OEMs have shipped repowering tools to make inverter swaps easier, and trade press is openly calling orphaned-system service the emerging 2026 revenue stream. why_now verified in full: SunPower Chapter 11 August 2024, Sunnova Chapter 11 8 June 2025 (S.D. Tex., $8.9B debt, 718 layoffs), Solar Mosaic Chapter 11 June 2025 ($15B funded across 500k+ households), PosiGen bankruptcy late 2025, and Section 25D terminated for expenditures after 31 December 2025 under OBBBA (P.L. 119-21, signed 4 July 2025) — every number holds.
orphaned-residential-solar-servicing.kill_risk: Overlooked is close to zero: an $87M-funded incumbent has already bought the two largest orphaned fleets and is servicing them under contract, which is the endgame this candidate proposes to start walking toward from one county with door-knocking. The 'investors won't open a deck with solar in it' moat claim is refuted by the April 2025 round itself. The unverified risk the candidate flagged is the real one and it is fatal at small scale: single-home truck-roll economics on a $3,000-6,000 inverter job cannot support a two-person company without route density that only a national network has, and Omnidian/GreenLancer already have the network. Portfolio owners and bankruptcy estates award these fleets in bulk to counterparties with balance sheets and nationwide coverage, so the highest-value customers are structurally unreachable. The public-records fleet database is the one differentiated asset and it is replicable in weeks by anyone with the same idea.

agent-liability-loss-data.crowding_check: Densely occupied on BOTH sides the thesis claims are empty. Acceptance side (the claim was 'no builder at all'): AIUC / Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company — $15M seed led by Nat Friedman with Anthropic participating, ships AIUC-1 standard + third-party audits + Lloyd's-backed cover to $50M, ElevenLabs is a named policyholder; Armilla (affirmative AI cover + independent model verification, limits reported to $25M); Testudo (standalone Lloyd's-backed genAI policy to $10M, all 50 states); Klaimee (raised $5.5M July 2026 explicitly to insure autonomous AI agents, first- and third-party harm); plus Corgi, Vouch (affirmative AI E&O since Mar 2026), RiskCube, Relm. Registry/taxonomy side: AI Incident Database (~800-900 incidents, ~130-180/yr), OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor (5,000-7,000 incident-reports via Event Registry), MIT AI Risk Repository (causal + domain taxonomies plus EU AI Act risk levels), AIAAIC. Even the actuarial method is published — arXiv 2606.16465 'Trace-Economic Underwriting', arXiv 2606.05449 'Insurance of Agentic AI', arXiv 2606.03777 CER framework. Market sizing is public (FactMR: $0.5B 2026 to $11.5B 2036, 36.8% CAGR), which is itself a crowding signal.
agent-liability-loss-data.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim — 'the acceptance side has no builder at all' — is false as of Aug 2026; AIUC/Armilla/Klaimee ARE the acceptor and each accretes its own claims data with privileged access an outsider cannot match. The why_now evidence is the weakest kind: five zero-star GitHub repos is a supply observation, not a demand trigger, and zero stars on issuance tooling says nothing about who wins on the underwriting side. Worse, a third-party registry cannot see closed claims — carriers own those and will not share them with a startup that plans to resell the aggregate. Seeding from 'publicly reported agent failures' just re-scrapes AIID and OECD AIM, which are free.

prediction-market-harm-infrastructure.crowding_check: The central technical premise is falsified. Gamban already lists prediction markets as a blocked category alongside crypto gambling and spread-betting platforms — the claim that 'their coverage lists miss the new platforms by construction' does not hold in 2026. Self-exclusion is also built: Kalshi is the first active partner of SelfExclude, a cross-platform prediction-market exclusion network run by compliance vendor IC360, with Polymarket, Robinhood and ProphetX expected to connect. Kalshi shipped a consumer-protection hub (deposit caps, trading breaks, opt-outs), proactive suggested deposit limits with proof-of-funds requests, and 'Inner Circle' family activity-sharing (Axios, May 2026). Recovery/treatment is funded and partnered: Birches Health ($20M total, General Catalyst seed + AlleyCorp Series A, now smartphone-delivered, RG partnerships with betting operators), Kindbridge ($5.4M, DraftKings partnership, already monetizing 'responsible trading' for prediction markets). Free blockers BetBlocker and GamBlock cover the hard-blocking layer; Michigan hands out free Gamban licenses.
prediction-market-harm-infrastructure.kill_risk: The gap the whole thesis rests on was closed before the idea was written down — both the blocking taxonomy (Gamban) and the cross-platform exclusion registry (IC360 SelfExclude). Regulatory heat is real (Michigan AG Nessel suit vs Kalshi, Washington crackdown and Robinhood's countersuit, a Nevada federal ruling treating sports event contracts as gambling, Robinhood pulling sports contracts in MD/NJ/NV, and the Gillibrand-McCormick Prediction Market Act of 2026 mandating self-exclusion and age verification) — but that heat routes revenue to the incumbent compliance vendor (IC360) and the platforms' in-house teams, not to a new entrant. Card-level blocking is not buildable by a 3-person team either: merchant blocking is an issuer capability, and no issuer API grants a startup MCC-level block authority.

invoice-xml-ingestion-firewall.crowding_check: The space is populated by CONFORMANCE validators, not adversarial ones — a real distinction. Found: easybill/e-invoice-validator (open source, Peppol BIS / XRechnung / Factur-X / EN16931 schematron), ecosio free validator, Invoice Navigator (explicitly supports KSeF), B2BRouter, Sorgera (Peppol + KSeF), MyInvoice, eaglessoft. Every one validates schema/schematron conformance; none markets injection quarantine, homoglyph/bidi detection, entity-expansion limits or a hold-and-release console. Compliance incumbents (Sovos, Avalara E-Invoicing and Live Reporting, ONESOURCE Pagero, Tradeshift, EDICOM) sell transmission, legal validity and AP receipt — searches surfaced zero receive-side security features from any of them. One security researcher occupies the topic (invoice.secvuln.info, 'Security Issues with Electronic Invoices and EU eInvoicing'), with a documented ZUGFeRD XXE that exfiltrates server files, and notes Java stdlib and Saxon ship insecure defaults inside the e-invoicing ecosystem — corroborating the threat while confirming no vendor owns it. Real overlap to respect: the generic capability is a 20-year-old product category — IBM DataPower XML Firewall (schema validation, threat protection, entity limits, still documented at v10.6.0) and Forum Sentry XML Gateway do this class of filtering already, just without country schema packs.
invoice-xml-ingestion-firewall.kill_risk: Two live risks. (1) A security-first framing may not have a budget owner: there is still no confirmed public incident of an ERP compromised via a cleared e-invoice, so the 'first breach makes this board-level' step is a hypothesis, and until it happens the buyer may treat it as an XML-gateway config problem they already own via DataPower/Saxon hardening. (2) Sovos or Pagero can bolt receive-side sanitization onto an existing KSeF/Peppol pipeline once it becomes a checkbox, and they already hold the receiving-entity relationship. Market size is the real ceiling — realistic buyers are ERP vendors, ASPs and mid-market receivers per country, not a multi-billion pool. The why_now, by contrast, is the strongest in this batch and verified: KSeF is mandatory 1 Feb 2026 for taxpayers over PLN 200M, 1 Apr 2026 for all other established taxpayers, Jan 2027 for micro-entrepreneurs, the Ministry of Finance has stated deadlines will NOT be postponed, and the clearance model is confirmed (an invoice has no legal existence until KSeF accepts it) — so the receive-side cohort is arriving on schedule right now.

congregation-space-third-place-operator.crowding_check: The claim of 'no branded player' is wrong. ChurchSpace (founded 2021, Emmanuel Brown and Day Edwards, $1.2M oversubscribed round May 2025, HQ moved to Detroit with a City of Detroit partnership piloting expanded use of church facilities) is the 'Airbnb for churches' and explicitly handles pricing, photography, INSURANCE, LIABILITY and cleaning — i.e. the exact wrapper this candidate proposes to build, differing mainly in booking-marketplace vs master-lease structure. RootedGood (Mark Elsdon, author of 'We Aren't Broke' and editor of 'Gone for Good?') sells consulting, guides and courses to churches on income-generating property use. Faith Property Collaborative and Partners for Sacred Places occupy the nonprofit advisory layer. The childcare-in-church wedge specifically is a mature cottage industry: Child Care Biz Help runs a dedicated Church Childcare Consulting practice (feasibility, licensing, staffing, financial forecasting), Procare and TrustedCare publish 2026 how-to guides for opening a church daycare, and multiple state agencies (e.g. Missouri DESE) run religious-organization childcare licensing tracks. What genuinely was not found: a multi-site master-lease OPERATOR running a P&L across 10-30 congregations in one metro.
congregation-space-third-place-operator.kill_risk: The one verified dated trigger doesn't support the business. California SB 4 is real (signed 11 Oct 2023, effective 1 Jan 2024, sunsets 2036) and copycats are real (Florida SB 1730 in 2025, Virginia effective 1 Jan 2027, Massachusetts 2026, bills in SC/AZ/NY/KY/TX/CO) — but every one of these is a HOUSING DEVELOPMENT entitlement statute. It says nothing about weekday programming or master leases, and if anything it competes for the same buildings by pulling boards toward the capital-intensive redevelopment path. The 'Pew 2025 affiliation plateau' and 'municipal loneliness funding line item' claims remain unverified. No measured utilization or vacancy number exists anywhere in the chain. The likeliest reason no branded master-lease operator exists is that the economics are bad, not that nobody noticed: sub-market revenue share on ops-heavy, one-metro-at-a-time services with a landlord who can terminate.

post-pill-transition-program.crowding_check: This is an established consumer-health category with a dominant personal brand. Dr. Jolene Brighten's 'Beyond the Pill' is the canonical product for exactly this transition — a book plus a 30-day protocol program marketed as balancing hormones and reversing pill side effects, with dedicated post-birth-control acne protocols. Around it: Natural Acne Clinic (paid online program, 60-minute consult with coaches), WSH Care post-birth-control acne programs, WeNatal transition protocols, Ubie clinical roadmaps, and a large functional-medicine/naturopath cottage industry selling 'post-birth-control syndrome' packages. The contraception layer is owned by Natural Cycles (FDA-cleared 2018, correctly cited). The well-funded adjacent player that can extend into this in a quarter is Allara Health — $38.5M across three rounds (Index Ventures, GV, Global Founders), telehealth for PCOS/endometriosis/hypothyroid, already contracted with Aetna, BCBS, Cigna, Humana and UnitedHealthcare in 10 states, i.e. it already owns the labs + prescriber + hormonal-condition delivery arm this candidate proposes to assemble. UCSF has published a 'Beyond the Pill' telehealth protocol (Feb 2025), so even the clinical protocol is free.
post-pill-transition-program.kill_risk: Crowded by an incumbent brand that owns the search term. The one thing the candidate flagged as unverified actually checks out and is the strongest part: hormonal contraception use is genuinely falling — UK 19% (2018) to just over 11% (2023), NHS oral contraceptive users down 63% over ten years (426,800 in 2014/15 to 159,800 in 2024/25), US KFF 33% (2022) to 29% (2024), Germany 45.7% (2012) to 25.3% (2024, n=5,579). But verified demand plus saturated supply is the worst combination for a screener. Execution risk compounds it: multi-state prescriber licensure, a lab panel, and documented contraceptive-EFFICACY counseling make this a regulated clinical business carrying real liability for unintended pregnancy — not a 90-day wedge — and the go-to-market depends on a single creator who can walk. No payer exists, so it is cash-pay against a $30 book.

in-person-practical-assessment-days.crowding_check: Both flanks are occupied, but the specific packaging is thin. The assessment-centre category is 40 years old and delivered in person today: SHL TalentCentral is used by the majority of the FTSE 100 and a large share of the Fortune 500 and runs assessment centres, Aon/cut-e runs assessment-centre exercises and is winning switchers (Schroders moved from SHL to Aon), DDI is the third leg, and major employers still end their funnels in person — Deloitte's process terminates in an in-person assessment centre in 2026. The anti-cheating layer is its own crowded 2026 startup wave (Humanly integrity layers, Truffle, Karat Qualify, MatchCard, aiseptor). What did NOT turn up in search: an open-market, per-seat, cross-employer service issuing a CANDIDATE-OWNED portable work-sample result for non-licensure role families. That gap looks real; the delivery capability around it does not.
in-person-practical-assessment-days.kill_risk: The mechanism is verified better than the candidate claimed — a 2026 sample of 19,368 real interviews showed 38.5% with clear AI-cheating signals, 48% for technical roles, most still passing, and the emerging industry consensus is literally that 'the single most cheat-resistant tool is a work sample.' That is a genuine dated trigger. But the scout's headline number, 'roughly 25 states adopted skills-based hiring policies,' remains UNVERIFIED — my search budget was exhausted before I could count statutes and effective dates, so treat it as unconfirmed. The commercial risks: (1) SHL, Aon and DDI can run this as a line extension on infrastructure and employer relationships they already have, and Prometric can rent them the rooms; (2) candidate-side portable credentials have a brutal historical adoption record — the network effect that turns a services business into a credential is the part most likely to never ignite, leaving a low-margin room-rental operation at $400-600/seat; (3) one role family in one city is a genuinely small starting TAM and metro-by-metro expansion is linear, not compounding.

analog-media-supply-chain.crowding_check: NOT LIVE-VERIFIED (WebSearch budget exhausted 200/200 before task start; all outbound HTTPS 403 at proxy). analog-media-supply-chain.kill_risk: why_now fails on its own terms: the candidate explicitly admits no dated or numeric trigger exists, and the three load-bearing claims (Gen Z cohort a decade deep, ~100M dormant bodies, tariffs widening the refurb spread) are all unsourced scout inference. medicaid-doula-billing-infrastructure.crowding_check: NOT LIVE-VERIFIED (no search or fetch available this session). From training knowledge: the underlying policy fact is the strongest and most checkable in this batch and it holds — state Medicaid doula benefits are real and the candidate's state list is accurate (MN 2014, OR ~2017-18, NJ 2021, VA/MD 2022, RI 2022, NV 2022, MI Jan 2023, CA Jan 2023, plus NY, IL, WA, MA, DC and ~30+ states implemented or in progress by 2026). Low utilization from enrollment/credentialing friction is a documented complaint, notably in California's first year. Competition is real but thinner than the other candidates here. Closest direct competitor: The Doula Network (FL, ~2021) — national doula network that contracts with Medicaid/MCO payers and handles credentialing and billing, i.e. the exact model. medicaid-doula-billing-infrastructure.kill_risk: Largest risk is one the candidate never mentions and that I consider disqualifying-adjacent: the July 2025 federal reconciliation law cut roughly $1T from Medicaid over ten years and imposes work requirements from 2027, and state-optional benefits like doula coverage are exactly what gets trimmed first when state budgets compress — the tailwind could reverse inside the 3-5 year window. Second: payers and states building doula hubs in-house disintermediates the back office entirely. Third: unit economics are thin — a doula billing 2-4 Medicaid births a month at a ~$1,500 bundle yields only $5-11k/yr at a 15-20% take, so this needs 200+ recruited doulas just to reach $1-2M ARR, against high-touch onboarding. Fourth: total claim pool is modest — even 20% doula penetration of Medicaid-financed births is roughly $400M in claims and well under $100M of take. Advance only if the state-by-state effective-date and paid-claims table the candidate itself names as step zero is actually built first; that table is genuinely the whole diligence.

mlm-workforce-landing-pad.crowding_check: NOT LIVE-VERIFIED (no search available). From training knowledge the space is heavily occupied at both ends. mlm-workforce-landing-pad.kill_risk: The why_now is actually stronger than the scout claimed (Beachbody/BODi ended multi-level comp in 2024, Rodan+Fields exited MLM in Sept 2024, Tupperware Chapter 11 Sept 2024, Medifast/OPTAVIA revenue roughly halved on GLP-1 substitution, DSA salesforce counts falling) — but a valid trigger does not rescue a crowded market. Kill reasons: the exact model was funded at $2.35B (Assurance IQ) and written off; the incumbent channel (SIAA/Goosehead/WFG) already serves this cohort; pre-licensing exam pass rates and first-year insurance agent retention are both brutal, so a 30-50 recruit funnel yields a handful of producers and CAC never amortizes; and the core promise — the rep owns the book — is deliberately anti-lock-in, so there is no switching cost by construction. einvoice-credential-least-privilege-brok.crowding_check: NOT LIVE-VERIFIED — and this is the candidate most damaged by that, because its entire evidence base is five GitHub URLs I was blocked from reading (GitHub MCP is scoped to kirkwarren/ci_test; api.github.com returns 403 at the proxy). Issues #838/#837/#842 and the quoted per:["Owner"] token and the '21.07.2026 TEST / 23.07.2026 DEMO / 28.07.2026 PRD' schedule are therefore UNCONFIRMED by me. What I can corroborate from training knowledge: KSeF mandatory rollout was moved to 1 Feb 2026 for large taxpayers and 1 Apr 2026 for the rest, so 'in production now' in Aug 2026 is consistent; KSeF 2.0 does replace authorization tokens with KSeF certificates on a transition that runs to end-2026, matching the '31 grudnia 2026' claim.
